claims.statement: Sita is a Hindu goddess and the principal female character of the Ramayana.
claims.statement_id: Sita adalah dewi Hindu dan tokoh perempuan utama dalam Ramayana.
claims.quote: Sita (Sanskrit: सीता; IAST: Sītā), also known as Siya, Jānaki and Maithili, is a Hindu goddess and the female protagonist of the Hindu epic Ramayana. Sita is the consort of Rama, the avatar of god Vishnu, and is regarded as an avatar of goddess Lakshmi. She is the chief goddess of the Ramanandi Sampradaya and is the goddess of beauty and devotion.

claims.statement: Siya, Janaki, and Maithili are other names of Sita.
claims.statement_id: Siya, Janaki, dan Maithili merupakan nama lain Sita.
claims.quote: Sita (Sanskrit: सीता; IAST: Sītā), also known as Siya, Jānaki and Maithili, is a Hindu goddess and the female protagonist of the Hindu epic Ramayana. Sita is the consort of Rama, the avatar of god Vishnu, and is regarded as an avatar of goddess Lakshmi. She is the chief goddess of the Ramanandi Sampradaya and is the goddess of beauty and devotion.

claims.statement: She is Rama's consort and is regarded as an incarnation of Lakshmi.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah pasangan Rama dan dipandang sebagai penjelmaan Lakshmi.
claims.quote: Sita (Sanskrit: सीता; IAST: Sītā), also known as Siya, Jānaki and Maithili, is a Hindu goddess and the female protagonist of the Hindu epic Ramayana. Sita is the consort of Rama, the avatar of god Vishnu, and is regarded as an avatar of goddess Lakshmi. She is the chief goddess of the Ramanandi Sampradaya and is the goddess of beauty and devotion.

claims.statement: Sita is described as Bhumi's daughter and King Janaka of Videha's adopted child.
claims.statement_id: Sita disebut putri Bhumi dan anak angkat Raja Janaka dari Videha.
claims.quote: Described as the daughter of Bhūmi (the earth), Sita is brought up as the adopted daughter of King Janaka of Videha. Sita, in her youth, chooses Rama, the prince of Ayodhya, as her husband in a svayamvara. After the svayamvara, she accompanies her husband to his kingdom but later chooses to accompany him along with her brother-in-law Lakshmana in his exile.

claims.statement: She chooses Rama of Ayodhya as her husband in a svayamvara.
claims.statement_id: Ia memilih Rama dari Ayodhya sebagai suami dalam svayamvara.
claims.quote: Described as the daughter of Bhūmi (the earth), Sita is brought up as the adopted daughter of King Janaka of Videha. Sita, in her youth, chooses Rama, the prince of Ayodhya, as her husband in a svayamvara. After the svayamvara, she accompanies her husband to his kingdom but later chooses to accompany him along with her brother-in-law Lakshmana in his exile.

claims.statement: She accompanies Rama into exile with Lakshmana.
claims.statement_id: Ia mengikuti pengasingan Rama bersama Lakshmana.
claims.quote: Described as the daughter of Bhūmi (the earth), Sita is brought up as the adopted daughter of King Janaka of Videha. Sita, in her youth, chooses Rama, the prince of Ayodhya, as her husband in a svayamvara. After the svayamvara, she accompanies her husband to his kingdom but later chooses to accompany him along with her brother-in-law Lakshmana in his exile.

claims.statement: Ravana abducts her from the Dandaka forest and holds her in Ashoka Vatika garden in Lanka.
claims.statement_id: Ravana menculiknya dari hutan Dandaka dan menahannya di taman Ashoka Vatika di Lanka.
claims.quote: While in exile, the trio settles in the Dandaka forest from where she is abducted by Ravana, the Rakshasa king of Lanka. She is imprisoned in the garden of Ashoka Vatika in Lanka until she is rescued by Rama, who slays her captor.

claims.statement: In some versions, Sita demonstrates her chastity through the Agni Pariksha fire ordeal.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian versi, Sita membuktikan kesuciannya melalui ujian api Agni Pariksha.
claims.quote: After the war, in some versions of the epic, Rama asks Sita to undergo an Agni Pariksha (an ordeal of fire), by which she proves her chastity, before she is accepted by Rama. Such an episode of trial makes Lakshmana angry at Rama, for the first time.

claims.statement: Other versions say Maya Sita replaces her during the abduction while the real Sita shelters in fire.
claims.statement_id: Versi lain menyebut Maya Sita menggantikannya saat diculik, sementara Sita asli berlindung dalam api.
claims.quote: In some other versions of the epic, Maya Sita, an illusion created by Agni, takes Sita's place and is abducted by Ravana and suffers his captivity, while the real Sita hides in the fire.

claims.statement: Some texts connect her previous birth with Vedavati.
claims.statement_id: Sejumlah teks menghubungkan kehidupan terdahulunya dengan Vedavati.
claims.quote: Some scriptures also mention her previous birth as Vedavati, a woman whom Ravana tries to molest.

claims.statement: In the continuation, Sita shelters in Valmiki's ashram and gives birth to twins Kusha and Lava.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kelanjutan kisah, Sita berlindung di asrama Valmiki dan melahirkan anak kembar Kusha dan Lava.
claims.quote: She takes shelter at Sage Valmiki's ashram. She gives birth to twin sons there: Kusha and Lava.

claims.statement: That ending recounts Sita's return to the earth, her mother.
claims.statement_id: Akhir kisah tersebut menuturkan kembalinya Sita ke bumi, ibunya.
claims.quote: Years later, Sita reunites her two sons with their father Rama and then returns to the womb of her mother, the earth, as a testimony to her ultimate purity.

claims.statement: The name Sita derives from a Sanskrit word meaning furrow.
claims.statement_id: Nama Sita berasal dari kata Sanskerta yang berarti alur bajakan.
claims.quote: The goddess is best known by the name "Sita", derived from the Sanskrit word sīta, ("furrow".)

claims.statement: Mackenzie also places Sita as Lakshmi's human incarnation in the Ramayana.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie juga menempatkan Sita sebagai penjelmaan manusia Lakshmi dalam Ramayana.
claims.quote:
She has had several
human incarnations, and in each case was loved by the
incarnation of Vishnu. She is Sita in the Ramáyana, and
the beautiful herdswoman beloved by Krishna.

claims.statement: The painting discussed by the Carlos Museum depicts Ravana carrying Sita away from a forest hermitage.
claims.statement_id: Lukisan yang dibahas Museum Carlos menggambarkan Ravana membawa Sita dari pertapaan di hutan.
claims.quote: Ravana carries Sita away from her opulent hermitage in the highly stylized forest

claims.statement: Hanuman was sent by Rama to seek Sita and found where she was; Sita gave him her jewellery to pass to her husband.
claims.statement_id: Hanuman diutus Rama mencari Sita dan akhirnya menemukan keberadaannya; Sita memberinya perhiasannya untuk diserahkan kepada suaminya.
claims.quote: Hanuman was sent by Rama to seek Sita and eventually succeeded in discovering Sita's whereabouts. Sita gave Hanuman her jewelery and asked him to give it to her husband.

claims.statement: With a heavy heart Rama had Lakshmana take Sita to a forest outside Ayodhya and leave her there; in her second exile the pregnant Sita took refuge in Valmiki's hermitage and bore the twins Lava and Kusha.
claims.statement_id: Dengan berat hati Rama menyuruh Lakshmana membawa Sita ke hutan di luar Ayodhya dan meninggalkannya di sana; dalam pembuangan keduanya Sita yang hamil berlindung di pertapaan Valmiki dan melahirkan putra kembar Lava dan Kusha.
claims.quote: With a heavy heart, he instructed Lakshmana to take Sita to a forest outside Ayodhya and leave her there. Following her second exile, a pregnant Sita sought refuge in the hermitage of Valmiki, where she gave birth to twin sons, Lava and Kusha.

claims.statement: In response Sita asserted her fidelity by calling on her mother, the earth goddess Bhumi, to receive her; Bhumi emerged from the earth and descended back with Sita amid the assembly's praise.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai jawaban, Sita menegaskan kesetiaannya dengan memanggil ibunya, dewi bumi Bhumi, agar menerimanya; Bhumi muncul dari bumi dan turun kembali bersama Sita di tengah pujian sidang.
claims.quote: In response, Sita asserted her fidelity by calling upon her mother, the earth goddess Bhumi, to receive her. Bhumi emerged from the earth and descended back with Sita, amid praise from the assembly.

claims.statement: According to the Padma Purana, Sita's exile during her pregnancy was due to a curse from her childhood.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Padma Purana, pembuangan Sita saat hamil disebabkan sebuah kutukan pada masa kecilnya.
claims.quote: According to the Padma Purana, Sita's exile during her pregnancy was because of a curse during her childhood.

claims.statement: In Mackenzie's retelling Hanuman beholds the long-lost Sita, "the queen of stars", surrounded by fierce she-demons with the heads of dogs, pigs, horses and buffaloes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penceritaan Mackenzie, Hanuman melihat Sita yang lama hilang, "ratu bintang-bintang", dikelilingi para raksasi buas berkepala anjing, babi, kuda, dan kerbau.
claims.quote: There he beheld the long-lost Sita, the queen of stars. Fierce she demons surrounded her, and some were of fearsome shape; they had dogs' heads and pigs' heads and the faces of horses and buffaloes

claims.statement: Varuna is a Hindu god depicted as sovereign of the sky in early Vedic times.
claims.statement_id: Varuna adalah dewa Hindu yang digambarkan sebagai penguasa langit pada zaman Weda awal.
claims.quote: In the early Vedic era, Varuna is seen as the god-sovereign, ruling the sky and embodying divine authority.

claims.statement: He maintains truth and rta, cosmic and moral order.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjaga kebenaran dan rta, tatanan kosmis serta moral.
claims.quote: He maintains truth and ṛta, the cosmic and moral order, and was invoked as an omniscient ethical judge, with the stars symbolizing his watchful eyes or spies.

claims.statement: Varuna is frequently paired with Mitra.
claims.statement_id: Varuna sering dipasangkan dengan Mitra.
claims.quote: Frequently paired with Mitra, Varuna represents the magical and speculative aspects of sovereignty, overseeing the relationship between gods and humans.

claims.statement: In Itihasa and Purana traditions he becomes lord of oceans, rivers, streams, and lakes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Itihasa dan Purana ia menjadi penguasa lautan, sungai, aliran air, dan danau.
claims.quote: By the time of the Itihasa-Purana, Varuna had transformed into the lord of all waters, ruling over oceans, rivers, streams, and lakes.

claims.statement: He also serves as the dikpala guarding the west.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga berperan sebagai dikpala penjaga arah barat.
claims.quote: Varuna’s earlier supremacy diminished, and he was relegated to a lesser role as a dikpala, or guardian of the western direction.

claims.statement: His depictions include a youthful figure riding the creature Makara.
claims.statement_id: Penggambarannya mencakup sosok muda yang menunggang makhluk Makara.
claims.quote: He is depicted as a youthful man, mounted on Makara (crocodile-like creature)

claims.statement: In depictions he holds a pasha (noose) and a pitcher.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penggambarannya ia memegang pasha (jerat) dan sebuah kendi.
claims.quote: and holding a Pasha (noose, rope loop) and a pitcher in his hands.

claims.statement: The Tolkappiyam calls him Kadalon, god of sea and rain.
claims.statement_id: Tolkappiyam menyebutnya Kadalon, dewa laut dan hujan.
claims.quote: Varuna is also mentioned in the Tamil grammar work Tolkāppiyam, as Kadalon ... the god of sea and rain, and is furthermore present as a deity in Jainism.

claims.statement: In Japanese Buddhism he is known as Suiten and belongs to the Twelve Devas.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Buddhisme Jepang ia dikenal sebagai Suiten dan termasuk Dua Belas Dewa.
claims.quote: In Japanese Buddhist myth, Varuna is known as Suiten ... and ranks among the Twelve Devas

claims.statement: A Hindu explanation connects his name with the root vr, meaning to encompass or bind.
claims.statement_id: Penjelasan Hindu mengaitkan namanya dengan akar vr yang berarti meliputi atau mengikat.
claims.quote: In Hindu tradition, the theonym Váruṇa (Devanagari: वरुण) is described as a derivation from the verbal root vṛ ("to surround, to cover" or "to restrain, bind") by means of a suffixal -uṇa-, for an interpretation of the name as  "he who covers or binds", in reference to the cosmological ocean or river encircling the world, but also in reference to the "binding" by universal law or Ṛta.

claims.statement: The Rigveda contains several Varuna hymns and depicts him as sky sovereign, guardian of rta, water deity, and wielder of maya.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda memuat sejumlah himne Varuna dan menggambarkannya sebagai raja langit, penjaga rta, penguasa air, serta pemilik maya.
claims.quote: Varuṇa is portrayed in four principal aspects: as a universal monarch and sovereign of the sky, the upholder of ṛta (cosmic order), a deity associated with water (āpah), and a wielder of māyā (cosmic illusion or creative power).

claims.statement: Rigveda 1.25 praises him for understanding the paths of birds, ships, and winds.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda 1.25 memujinya karena memahami lintasan burung, kapal, dan angin.
claims.quote: In Rigveda 1.25, Varuṇa is praised for his understanding of the paths of birds, the movement of ships and winds, and the secrets of time and space. Hymns characterize him as a sovereign deity, intimately acquainted with both the sacred and the profane.

claims.statement: Hymns depict him as punishing wrongdoing while showing mercy to the penitent.
claims.statement_id: Himne menggambarkannya menghukum pelanggaran tetapi mengasihi orang yang bertobat.
claims.quote: Varuṇa's foremost role is as the enforcer of ṛta, the cosmic and moral order that governs both the natural world and human conduct. Hymns such as Rigveda VII.11.1 and II.29.8 present him as a vigilant upholder of truth, who punishes transgressors while showing mercy to the penitent. Ethical instructions against killing, deceit, and gambling are linked with his domain.

claims.statement: The 1911 Britannica records the epithets Jalapati and Amburaja referring to lordship over water.
claims.statement_id: Britannica 1911 mencatat gelar Jalapati dan Amburaja yang merujuk penguasa air.
claims.quote:
Among Varuna's aliases are Jalapati, "Lord of Water," and 
Amburaja, " King of Water."

claims.statement: The NGV Varuna sculpture is a red sandstone figure in a columned arch, flanked by guardians and leogryphs.
claims.statement_id: Patung Varuna di NGV berupa sosok batu pasir merah dalam lengkung berpilar, diapit penjaga dan makhluk leogryph.
claims.quote:
Physical description
		Figure of Varuna, red sandstone. Standing in columned arch, flanked by guardians and leogryphs.

claims.statement: The 1911 Britannica calls Varuna, together with Indra, the greatest of the gods of the Rig Veda, and says he is invoked with Mitra in some dozen hymns.
claims.statement_id: Britannica 1911 menyebut Varuna, bersama Indra, sebagai dewa terbesar dalam Rigveda, dan ia dipanggil bersama Mitra dalam sekitar selusin himne.
claims.quote: VARUNA, in early Hindu mythology, the greatest, with Indra, of the gods of the Rig Veda. He is invoked with his double Mitra in some dozen hymns.

claims.statement: The 1911 Britannica says Varuna's power is limitless, his anger at wrongdoing unassuageable, and that he is omniscient; he makes the sunshine, the wind is his breath, and river valleys are hollowed out at his command.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Britannica 1911, kekuasaan Varuna tak terbatas, murkanya pada kejahatan tak dapat diredakan, dan ia mahatahu; ia membuat sinar matahari, angin adalah napasnya, dan lembah sungai digali atas perintahnya.
claims.quote: His power is limitless, his anger at wrong-doing unassuageable, and he is omniscient. He makes the sunshine; the wind is his breath; river valleys are hollowed out at his command.

claims.statement: The 1911 Britannica notes that, unlike Indra, no myths are related of Varuna; in the later Vedic period he is connected with the nocturnal heavens, and in post-Vedic mythology he becomes the Hindu Neptune.
claims.statement_id: Britannica 1911 mencatat bahwa, berbeda dari Indra, tidak ada mitos yang dikisahkan tentang Varuna; pada masa Weda akhir ia dikaitkan dengan langit malam, dan dalam mitologi pasca-Weda ia menjadi Neptunus Hindu.
claims.quote: Unlike Indra, Varuna has no myths related of him. In the later Vedic period he is specially connected with the nocturnal heavens. Ultimately in post-Vedic mythology he becomes the Hindu Neptune.

claims.statement: The 1911 Britannica refers the name to a root var, "to cover," so that Varuna means "the Encompasser."
claims.statement_id: Britannica 1911 mengaitkan nama Varuna dengan akar kata var yang berarti menutupi, sehingga Varuna berarti Sang Peliput (the Encompasser).
claims.quote: and ultimately referable to a root var, "to cover," Varuna thus meaning "the Encompasser."

claims.statement: In Griffith's translation of Rigveda 1.25, Varuna is said to know the path of birds that fly through heaven and, as sovereign of the sea, the ships that are on it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Griffith atas Rigveda 1.25, Varuna dikatakan mengetahui jalan burung yang terbang di langit dan, sebagai penguasa laut, mengetahui kapal-kapal di atasnya.
claims.quote: He knows the path of birds that fly through heaven, and, Sovran of the sea, He knows the ships that are thereon.

claims.statement: Rigveda 1.25 closes with a plea to release the upper bond, untie the bond between, and loose the bonds below, that the worshipper may live.
claims.statement_id: Himne Rigveda 1.25 menutup dengan permohonan agar ikatan atas dilepaskan, ikatan di tengah diurai, dan ikatan di bawah dibebaskan supaya pemuja dapat hidup.
claims.quote: Release us from the upper bond, untie the bond between, and loose The bonds below, that I may live.

claims.statement: Mackenzie calls Varuna Indra's great rival, who symbolized the investing sky and was "the all-enveloping one."
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menyebut Varuna sebagai saingan besar Indra, yang melambangkan langit yang meliputi segalanya ("the all-enveloping one").
claims.quote: Indra's great rival, however, was Varuna, who symbolized the investing sky: he was “the all-enveloping one”.

claims.statement: Mackenzie says the hymns give Varuna a character of Hebraic grandeur: he was the sustainer of the universe, the lawgiver, the god of moral rectitude, and the sublime sovereign of gods and men.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Mackenzie, himne-himne memberi Varuna keagungan Ibrani (Hebraic grandeur): ia penopang alam semesta, pemberi hukum, dewa kelurusan moral, dan penguasa agung para dewa dan manusia.
claims.quote: The hymns impart to him a character of Hebraic grandeur. He was the sustainer of the universe, the lawgiver, the god of moral rectitude, and the sublime sovereign of gods and men.

claims.statement: In the account Mackenzie quotes, the heaven of Varuna was built by Vishwakarman (Twashtri) within the sea; its walls are pure white and surrounded by celestial trees of sparkling jewels that always blossom and bear fruit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam uraian yang dikutip Mackenzie, surga Varuna dibangun oleh Vishwakarman (Twashtri) di dalam laut; dindingnya putih murni dan dikelilingi pohon-pohon langit dari permata yang selalu berbunga dan berbuah.
claims.quote: The heaven of Varuna was constructed by Vishwakarman (Twashtri) within the sea. Its walls and arches are of pure white, and they are surrounded by celestial trees, made of sparkling jewels, which always blossom and always bear fruit.

claims.statement: In the same account, Varuna is enthroned with his queen, richly decked with jewels, golden ornaments, and flowers.
claims.statement_id: Dalam uraian yang sama, Varuna bertakhta bersama ratunya, berhias permata, ornamen emas, dan bunga.
claims.quote: Varuna, richly decked with jewels and golden ornaments and flowers, is throned there with his queen.

claims.statement: Varuna is also mentioned as the king of the asuras who gained the status of a deva and served as chief of the Adityas, a group of celestial deities.
claims.statement_id: Varuna juga disebut sebagai raja para asura yang memperoleh kedudukan deva dan menjadi pemimpin para Aditya, kelompok dewa langit.
claims.quote: He is also mentioned as the king of asuras, who gained the status of a deva, serving as the chief of the Adityas, a group of celestial deities.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, in the Ramayana Varuna is depicted primarily as a dikpala and a water deity appointed by Brahma, weaker than in earlier portrayals, overpowered or sidelined by both Rama, an avatar of Vishnu, and Ravana, the demon king.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, dalam Ramayana Varuna digambarkan terutama sebagai dikpala dan dewa air yang ditunjuk Brahma, lebih lemah daripada penggambaran awalnya karena dikalahkan atau dikesampingkan oleh Rama, awatara Vishnu, maupun oleh Ravana, raja iblis.
claims.quote: As in the Mahabharata, in the other major epic, the Ramayana (300 BCE - 300 CE), Varuna is depicted primarily as a Dikpala and as a water deity appointed by chief-god Brahma. Varuna appears weaker than in his earlier portrayals, being overpowered or sidelined by both the protagonist Rama—an avatar of Vishnu—and the antagonist Ravana, the demon king.

claims.statement: In the Yuddha Kanda, as Rama prepares to invade the island Lanka to rescue his abducted wife Sita, he seeks passage across the ocean and performs a three-day penance to Varuna, lord of the oceans, but receives no reply.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Yuddha Kanda, ketika Rama bersiap menyerbu pulau Lanka untuk menyelamatkan istrinya Sita yang diculik, ia mencari jalan melintasi samudra dan bertapa tiga hari kepada Varuna, penguasa samudra, tetapi tidak dijawab.
claims.quote: One of the most well-known episodes involving Varuna occurs in the Yuddha Kanda when Rama, preparing to invade the island Lanka to rescue his abducted wife Sita, seeks passage across the ocean. Rama performs a three-day penance to Varuna, the lord of oceans, but receives no reply.

claims.statement: When Varuna initially stays silent, an enraged Rama threatens to evaporate the sea with his divine weapons, including the Brahmastra; Varuna then appears, recognizing Rama's authority and righteousness.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Varuna tetap diam, Rama yang murka mengancam menguapkan laut dengan senjata ilahi, termasuk Brahmastra; Varuna lalu muncul dan mengakui kewenangan serta kebenaran Rama.
claims.quote: When Varuna initially remains silent, Rama, enraged, threatens to unleash his divine weapons, including the Brahmastra, to evaporate the sea. Varuna then appears, recognizing Rama’s authority and righteousness.

claims.statement: Varuna explains that his role as guardian of natural order prevents him from parting the ocean, since that would disrupt natural balance; he suggests building a bridge and pledges to stabilize the waters.
claims.statement_id: Varuna menjelaskan bahwa perannya menjaga tatanan alam melarangnya membelah samudra karena akan mengganggu keseimbangan alam; ia menyarankan pembangunan jembatan dan berjanji menenangkan air.
claims.quote: He explains that his role as a guardian of natural order prevents him from parting the ocean, as it would disrupt natural balance. Instead, Varuna suggests constructing a bridge and pledges to stabilize the waters to aid the effort.

claims.statement: Wikipedia notes that many sources claim it was Samudra, the personification of the oceans, who met Rama and not the water god Varuna.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa banyak sumber menyatakan yang menemui Rama adalah Samudra, personifikasi samudra, dan bukan dewa air Varuna.
claims.quote: Many sources claim it was Samudra, the personification of the oceans, who met Rama not the water god Varuna.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, in the Mahabharata Varuna undergoes a notable transformation from his Vedic portrayal: he is no longer depicted as the supreme sky god or an omnipotent sovereign over cosmic and moral order, though his pairing with Mitra remains.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, dalam Mahabharata Varuna mengalami perubahan besar dari penggambaran Weda: ia tidak lagi digambarkan sebagai dewa langit tertinggi atau penguasa mahakuasa atas tatanan kosmis dan moral, meski pasangannya dengan Mitra tetap ada.
claims.quote: In the epic Mahabharata (c. 400 BCE - 400 CE), Varuna undergoes a notable transformation from his earlier Vedic portrayal. He is no longer depicted as the supreme sky god or an omnipotent sovereign administering cosmic order and morality, though his pairing with Mitra remains.

claims.statement: According to the Adi Parva, during the burning of the Khandava forest Varuna gave Arjuna the celestial bow Gandiva, an inexhaustible quiver, and a monkey-bannered chariot, and gave Krishna the mace Kaumodaki.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Adi Parva, saat hutan Khandava terbakar Varuna menghadiahkan busur langit Gandiva, tabung panah tak habis, dan kereta berpanji kera kepada Arjuna, serta gada Kaumodaki kepada Krishna.
claims.quote: The Adi Parva recounts that during the burning of the Khandava forest, Varuna gifted Arjuna the celestial bow Gandiva, an inexhaustible quiver, and a monkey-bannered chariot, as well as the mace Kaumodaki to Krishna.

claims.statement: Kartikeya is a Hindu war god generally described as the son of Shiva and Parvati.
claims.statement_id: Kartikeya adalah dewa perang Hindu yang umumnya disebut putra Shiva dan Parvati.
claims.quote: Kartikeya (IAST: Kārttikeya), also known as Skanda, Subrahmanya, Shanmukha or Muruga, is the Hindu god of war. He is generally described as the son of the deities Shiva and Parvati and the brother of Ganesha.

claims.statement: He is also known as Skanda, Subrahmanya, Shanmukha, and Muruga.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga dikenal sebagai Skanda, Subrahmanya, Shanmukha, dan Muruga.
claims.quote: Kartikeya (IAST: Kārttikeya), also known as Skanda, Subrahmanya, Shanmukha or Muruga, is the Hindu god of war. He is generally described as the son of the deities Shiva and Parvati and the brother of Ganesha.

claims.statement: Ganesha is described as his brother.
claims.statement_id: Ganesha disebut saudaranya.
claims.quote: Kartikeya (IAST: Kārttikeya), also known as Skanda, Subrahmanya, Shanmukha or Muruga, is the Hindu god of war. He is generally described as the son of the deities Shiva and Parvati and the brother of Ganesha.

claims.statement: Kaumaram is a Hindu denomination that primarily venerates Kartikeya.
claims.statement_id: Kaumaram adalah aliran Hindu yang terutama memuja Kartikeya.
claims.quote: Kaumaram is the Hindu denomination that primarily venerates Kartikeya.

claims.statement: The article connects Muruga in Tamil Sangam literature with the Kurinji region.
claims.statement_id: Artikel mengaitkan Muruga dalam sastra Sangam Tamil dengan wilayah Kurinji.
claims.quote: Muruga is a tutelary deity mentioned in Tamil Sangam literature, of the Kurinji region.

claims.statement: He is commonly depicted as a young man with a peacock named Paravani.
claims.statement_id: Ia lazim digambarkan sebagai pemuda dengan merak bernama Paravani.
claims.quote: He is typically represented as an ever-youthful man, riding or near an Peacock (named Paravani), and sometimes with an emblem of a rooster on his banner.

claims.statement: He carries the vel spear associated with Parvati's gift.
claims.statement_id: Ia membawa tombak vel yang dikaitkan dengan pemberian Parvati.
claims.quote: He wields a spear called the vel, supposedly given to him by his mother Parvati.

claims.statement: Some images show one head, while others show six.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian gambar menunjukkan satu kepala, sebagian lainnya enam.
claims.quote: While most icons represent him with only one head, some have six heads, a reflection of legends surrounding his birth wherein he was fused from six boys or borne of six conceptions.

claims.statement: He leads the devas' army against asuras including Tarakasura and Surapadma.
claims.statement_id: Ia memimpin pasukan deva melawan asura termasuk Tarakasura dan Surapadma.
claims.quote: He is described to have aged quickly from childhood, becoming a warrior, leading the army of the devas and credited with destroying asuras including Tarakasura and Surapadma.

claims.statement: Kartikeya means of the Krittikas, his nurses in the birth narrative.
claims.statement_id: Nama Kartikeya berarti milik para Krittika, pengasuhnya dalam cerita kelahiran.
claims.quote: Kartikeya means "of the Krittikas" in Sanskrit.

claims.statement: One account says Parvati merges six babies into six headed Kartikeya.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu cerita menyebut Parvati menyatukan enam bayi menjadi Kartikeya berkepala enam.
claims.quote: The epithet "Kartikeya" is linked to the circumstances surrounding the deity's birth. According to the Skanda Purana, six divine sparks emerged from Shiva, forming six separate baby boys. These boys were raised by handmaidens known as the Krittikas. Later, Parvati fused them into one, creating the six-headed Kartikeya. Kartikeya means "of the Krittikas" in Sanskrit.

claims.statement: The Vana Parva version of the Mahabharata describes him as the son of Agni and Svaha.
claims.statement_id: Versi Vana Parva Mahabharata menyebutnya putra Agni dan Svaha.
claims.quote: An alternate account of Kartikeya's parentage is narrated in the Vana Parva of the Mahabharata, where he is described as the son of Agni and Svaha.

claims.statement: Kartikeya worship also occurs in Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Singapore, and Indonesia.
claims.statement_id: Pemujaan Kartikeya juga terdapat di Sri Lanka, Malaysia, Singapura, dan Indonesia.
claims.quote: He is also worshipped in Sri Lanka, Southeast Asia (notably in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia), other countries with significant populations of Tamil origin (including Fiji, Mauritius, South Africa and Canada), Caribbean countries (including Trinidad and Tobago, Guyana and Suriname), and countries with significant Indian migrant populations (including the United States and A

claims.statement: The Bihar Museum discusses a red sandstone Kartikeya sculpture of the Later Gupta period with spear and peacock.
claims.statement_id: Museum Bihar membahas patung Kartikeya batu pasir merah dari masa Gupta akhir dengan tombak dan merak.
claims.quote: Kartikeya- This statue, from the Later Gupta period, is made of red sandstone. ... He is a red god seated on a blue peacock, and his weapon, a spear, is engraved on the left of the sculpture.

claims.statement: Mackenzie summarises a version connecting Kartikeya with Agni and the Ganges.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie merangkum versi yang menghubungkan Kartikeya dengan Agni dan Gangga.
claims.quote:
Another son of Shiva and Parvati is Kartikeya, the
Celestial general and slayer of demons. He is also
regarded as the son of Agni and the Ganges.

claims.statement: The 1911 Britannica calls Kartikeya the god of war in Hindu mythology and notes that there are various legends of his birth.
claims.statement_id: Britannica 1911 menyebut Kartikeya sebagai dewa perang dalam mitologi Hindu dan mencatat bahwa ada berbagai legenda tentang kelahirannya.
claims.quote: KARTIKEYA, in Hindu mythology, the god of war. Of his birth there are various legends.

claims.statement: One legend in the 1911 Britannica says he had no mother but was produced by Siva alone, was suckled by six nymphs of the Ganges, and was miraculously given six faces so he could take nourishment from each at once.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu legenda dalam Britannica 1911, Kartikeya tidak beribu dan dihasilkan oleh Siva sendiri, disusui enam bidadari Sungai Gangga, dan secara ajaib diberi enam wajah agar dapat menyusu dari masing-masing sekaligus.
claims.quote: One relates that he had no mother but was produced by Siva alone, and was suckled by six nymphs of the Ganges, being miraculously endowed with six faces that he might simultaneously obtain nourishment from each.

claims.statement: Another story in the 1911 Britannica says six miraculously conceived babes were born of the six nymphs and that Parvati, wife of Siva, embraced them so closely that they became one while keeping six faces, twelve arms, and feet and eyes to match.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita lain dalam Britannica 1911, enam bayi yang dikandung secara ajaib lahir dari keenam bidadari itu, dan Parvati, istri Siva, memeluk mereka begitu erat hingga menyatu, tetapi tetap berenam wajah, berdua belas lengan, serta berkaki dan bermata sebanyak itu.
claims.quote: Another story is that six babes, miraculously conceived, were born of the six nymphs, and that Parvati, the wife of Siva, in her great affection for them, embraced the infants so closely that they became one, but preserved six faces, twelve arms, feet, eyes, &c.

claims.statement: The 1911 Britannica records that Kartikeya became the victor of giants and leader of the armies of the gods, is represented riding a peacock, and is known in southern India as Subramanya.
claims.statement_id: Britannica 1911 mencatat bahwa Kartikeya menjadi penakluk para raksasa dan pemimpin pasukan para dewa, digambarkan menunggang merak, dan di India selatan dikenal sebagai Subramanya.
claims.quote: Kartikeya became the victor of giants and the leader of the armies of the gods. He is represented as riding a peacock. In southern India he is known as Subramanya.

claims.statement: The Bihar Museum text says that according to the Shiva Purana he is considered the eldest son of Shiva, and that he is also the god of war and commander of the gods.
claims.statement_id: Museum Bihar menulis bahwa menurut Shiva Purana ia dianggap putra sulung Shiva, dan ia juga dewa perang serta panglima para dewa.
claims.quote: According to Shiva-Purana, he is considered the eldest son of Shiva. He is also the god of war and the commander of the gods.

claims.statement: Wikipedia notes that Shavite puranas such as the Ganesha Purana, Shiva Purana, and Skanda Purana state that Ganesha is the elder of the two sons of Shiva and Parvati.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa Purana Saiwa seperti Ganesha Purana, Shiva Purana, dan Skanda Purana menyatakan bahwa Ganesha adalah yang lebih tua di antara kedua putra Shiva dan Parvati.
claims.quote: Indian religious literature describes Kartikeya and Ganesha as sons of Shiva and Parvati. Shavite puranas such as Ganesha Purana, Shiva Purana and Skanda Purana state that Ganesha is the elder of the two.

claims.statement: The Bihar Museum describes the sculpture as seated on the peacock and wearing a necklace with a tiger's nail and an amulet.
claims.statement_id: Museum Bihar menggambarkan arca itu duduk di atas merak dengan kalung berhias kuku harimau dan jimat.
claims.quote: Kartikey is seated on the peacock, wearing a necklace with a Tigher's nail and amulet.

claims.statement: In Valmiki's Ramayana (seventh to fourth century BCE), he is described as the child of Rudra and Parvati, with his birth aided by Agni and Ganga.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Ramayana Valmiki (abad ketujuh hingga keempat SM), ia digambarkan sebagai anak Rudra dan Parvati, dengan kelahiran yang dibantu Agni dan Ganga.
claims.quote: In Valmiki's Ramayana (seventh to fourth century BCE), he is described as the child of deities Rudra and Parvati, with his birth aided by Agni and Ganga.

claims.statement: According to the Shiva Purana, the asura Tarakasura performed tapas to Brahma and received two boons: none would be his equal in the three worlds, and only a son of Shiva could slay him.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Shiva Purana, asura Tarakasura bertapa kepada Brahma dan memperoleh dua anugerah: tak seorang pun setara dengannya di tiga dunia, dan hanya putra Shiva yang dapat membunuhnya.
claims.quote: According to Shiva Purana, asura Tarakasura performed tapas to propitiate the creator god Brahma. Brahma granted him two boons: one, that none shall be his equal in all of the three worlds, and two, that only a son of Shiva could slay him.

claims.statement: When Kartikeya threw his vel, Surapadma escaped to the sea as a large mango tree; Kartikeya split it with the vel and the halves became a peacock and a rooster. After Surapadma was killed, he took the peacock as his vahana and the rooster as his pennant.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Kartikeya melempar vel, Surapadma lari ke laut dan menjelma pohon mangga besar; Kartikeya membelahnya dengan vel, dan kedua belahannya menjadi merak dan ayam jantan. Setelah Surapadma tewas, ia menjadikan merak sebagai wahana dan ayam jantan sebagai panjinya.
claims.quote: When Kartikeya threw his vel, Surapadma escaped to the sea and took the form of a large mango tree, which spread across the three worlds. Kartikeya used his vel to split the tree in half, with each half transforming into a peacock and a rooster, respectively. After Surapadma was killed, Kartikeya took the peacock as his vahana and the rooster as his pennant.

claims.statement: In the story of the fruit of knowledge, Kartikeya sets off around the globe on his peacock, but Ganesha, reasoning that the world is no more than his parents Shiva and Shakti combined, circles them and wins the fruit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah buah pengetahuan, Kartikeya mengelilingi dunia dengan merak, tetapi Ganesha, yang menganggap dunia tidak lebih dari orang tuanya Shiva dan Shakti, mengelilingi mereka dan memenangkan buah itu.
claims.quote: Accepting the challenge, Kartikeya started his journey around the globe atop his peacock mount. However, Ganesha surmised that the world was no more than his parents Shiva and Shakti combined, circumambulated them, and won the fruit.

claims.statement: When Kartikeya returned he was furious that his efforts had been in vain and felt cheated; he discarded all his belongings, left Kailasha, and took up abode in the Palani Hills as a hermit.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Kartikeya kembali, ia murka karena jerih payahnya sia-sia dan merasa dicurangi; ia membuang semua harta bendanya, meninggalkan Kailasha, dan menetap di Bukit Palani sebagai pertapa.
claims.quote: When Kartikeya returned, he was furious to learn that his efforts had been in vain, and felt cheated. He discarded all his material belongings and left Kailasha to take up abode in the Palani Hills as a hermit.

claims.statement: The ancient Tamil text Tolkappiyam, from the second century BCE, mentions Ceyon ("the red one") and Murukan ("the youth"), identified with Murugan, as the god of the hilly regions.
claims.statement_id: Teks Tamil kuno Tolkappiyam dari abad kedua SM menyebut Ceyon ("si merah") dan Murukan ("si pemuda"), yang diidentifikasi dengan Murugan, sebagai dewa daerah perbukitan.
claims.quote: Ancient Tamil text Tolkappiyam from the second century BCE mentions Ceyon ("the red one"), and Murukan ("the youth"), identified with Murugan, as the god of the hilly regions.

claims.statement: Thaipusam is celebrated on the full moon day of the Tamil month of Thai to commemorate Murugan's victory over the asuras, and includes the ritual practice of Kavadi Aattam.
claims.statement_id: Thaipusam dirayakan pada hari bulan purnama di bulan Thai dalam penanggalan Tamil, untuk memperingati kemenangan Murugan atas para asura, dan mencakup praktik ritual Kavadi Aattam.
claims.quote: Thaipusam is celebrated on the full moon day in the Tamil month of Thai on the confluence of star Pusam. The festival is celebrated to commemorate the victory of Murugan over the asuras, and includes ritualistic practices of Kavadi Aattam.

claims.statement: Ravana is the rakshasa king of Lanka traditionally depicted with ten heads.
claims.statement_id: Ravana adalah raja rakshasa Lanka yang lazim digambarkan berkepala sepuluh.
claims.quote: He is traditionally depicted as a ten-headed rakshasa (demon) king of Lanka.

claims.statement: He is described as the son of Vishrava and Kaikasi.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut putra Vishrava dan Kaikasi.
claims.quote: In the Ramayana, Ravana is described as the eldest son of sage Vishrava and Kaikasi.

claims.statement: He abducts Sita and holds her in Ashoka Vatika.
claims.statement_id: Ia menculik Sita dan menahannya di Ashoka Vatika.
claims.quote: He abducted Rama's wife, Sita, and took her to his kingdom of Lanka, where he held her in the Ashoka Vatika.

claims.statement: Rama fights him with Sugriva and the vanara army's support and kills him.
claims.statement_id: Rama melawannya dengan dukungan Sugriva dan pasukan vanara lalu membunuhnya.
claims.quote: Rama, with the support of vanara King Sugriva and his army of vanaras, launched a rescue operation for Sita against Ravana in Lanka. Ravana was subsequently slain, and Rama rescued his beloved wife Sita.

claims.statement: His defeat is commemorated by burning Ravana effigies at Dussehra.
claims.statement_id: Kekalahannya diperingati dengan pembakaran patung Ravana pada Dussehra.
claims.quote: His epic defeat is celebrated yearly by burning a large effigy, depicting the ten-headed Ravana, during the Hindu festival of Dussehra.

claims.statement: Ravana is regarded as a devotee of Shiva.
claims.statement_id: Ravana dipandang sebagai pemuja Shiva.
claims.quote: Ravana is also considered to be an ardent devotee of Shiva.

claims.statement: He also appears in the Lankavatara Sutra, Buddhist Jatakas, and Jain Ramayanas.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga hadir dalam Lankavatara Sutra, Jataka Buddha, dan Ramayana Jain.
claims.quote: He also appears in the Buddhist Mahayana text Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra, in Buddhist Jatakas, as well as in Jain Ramayanas.

claims.statement: The name Ravana is explained as meaning roaring.
claims.statement_id: Nama Ravana diterangkan berarti mengaum.
claims.quote: The word Rāvaṇa (Sanskrit: रावण) means "Roaring" (active), the opposite of Vaiśravaṇa which means to "hear distinctly" (passive). Both Ravana and Vaiśravaṇa, who is commonly known as Kubera, are considered to be patronymics derived from "sons of Vishrava".

claims.statement: The epithet Dashanana means the one with ten heads.
claims.statement_id: Gelar Dashanana berarti yang berkepala sepuluh.
claims.quote: Dashānana was a title later taken on by Ravana, and it means "the one with ten (dasha) Heads (anana)". Further, roravana is Sanskrit for "loud roaring." In Abhinava Gupta's Krama Shaiva scripture, yāsām rāvanam is used as an expression to mean people who are truly aware of the materialism of their environment.

claims.statement: His other names include Lankapati and Lankeshwara.
claims.statement_id: Nama lainnya mencakup Lankapati dan Lankeshwara.
claims.quote: Ravana is also known by several other names including Dasis Ravana, Dasis Sakvithi Maha Ravana, Dashaanan, Ravula, Lankapati, Lankeshwara, Ravanasura and Ravanaeshwara.

claims.statement: Brahma grants him immunity against his creations except humans in the story.
claims.statement_id: Brahma memberinya anugerah kebal terhadap ciptaannya kecuali manusia dalam cerita.
claims.quote: Ravana and his two brothers, Kumbhakarna and Vibhishana, performed penance on Mount Gokarna for 10,000 years and won boons from Brahma. Ravana was blessed with a boon that would make him invincible to all the creations of Brahma, except for humans.

claims.statement: Brahma's gifts also include weapons, a chariot, and shapeshifting.
claims.statement_id: Anugerah Brahma juga mencakup senjata, kereta, dan kemampuan berganti wujud.
claims.quote: He also received weapons, a chariot, as well as the ability to shapeshift from Brahma.

claims.statement: Mandodari, Maya's daughter, is described as his chief queen.
claims.statement_id: Mandodari, putri Maya, disebut sebagai ratu utamanya.
claims.quote: According to Sundara Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, Ravana had over a thousand wives, with Mandodari, the daughter of the celestial architect Maya, being his chief queen. His sons were Meghanada, Atikaya, Akshayakumara, Narantaka, Devantaka and Trishira.

claims.statement: Mackenzie describes Rama as the slayer of Ravana who oppresses humans in the Ramayana.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menggambarkan Rama sebagai pembunuh Ravana yang menindas manusia dalam Ramayana.
claims.quote:
Rama Chandra is the hero of the Ramáyana epic,
which is summarized in our closing chapters; he is the
human ideal of devotion, righteousness, and manliness,
the slayer of the demon Ravana, who oppressed and
persecuted mankind.

claims.statement: The Carlos Museum collection scene depicts Ravana carrying Sita from her forest hermitage.
claims.statement_id: Adegan koleksi Museum Carlos menggambarkan Ravana membawa Sita dari pertapaannya di hutan.
claims.quote: Ravana carries Sita away from her opulent hermitage in the highly stylized forest

claims.statement: In Griffith's verse translation of the Ramayana, the assembled Immortals pray to Brahma: Ravan (Rávaṇ), who rules the giant race, torments them and the penance-loving saints in his senseless pride, and the boon given long ago, that neither god nor demon should kill his charmed life, makes him bold.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan syair Ramayana oleh Griffith, para dewa (the Immortals) berdoa kepada Brahma: Ravan (Rávaṇ), penguasa kaum raksasa, menyiksa mereka dan para resi pencinta tapa dalam kesombongannya, dan anugerah yang Brahma berikan pada masa lampau, bahwa dewa maupun iblis tidak akan membunuh nyawanya yang terlindung, membuatnya berani.
claims.quote: The Immortals all assembled prayed: “O Brahmá, mighty by thy grace, Rávaṇ, who rules the giant race, Torments us in his senseless pride, And penance-loving saints beside. For thou well pleased in days of old Gavest the boon that makes him bold, That God nor demon e'er should kill His charmed life, for so thy will.

claims.statement: In the reply to that prayer, the speaker says the giant once asked that his life be guarded from demon, god, heavenly bard, and spirits of earth and air, and that request was granted; but in his scorn he took no account of man born of woman, so only a man may slay the fiend.
claims.statement_id: Dalam jawaban atas doa itu, pembicara berkata bahwa si raksasa pernah meminta nyawanya dijaga dari iblis, dewa, penyanyi surgawi, serta roh bumi dan udara, dan permintaan itu dikabulkan; tetapi dalam kesombongannya ia tidak memedulikan manusia yang terlahir dari perempuan, sehingga hanya manusia yang dapat membunuhnya.
claims.quote: He prayed me once his life to guard From demon, God, and heavenly bard, And spirits of the earth and air, And I consenting heard his prayer. But the proud giant in his scorn Recked not of man of woman born. None else may take his life away, But only man the fiend may slay.

claims.statement: The Carlos Museum description says that after his sister is mutilated Ravana plots revenge in the form of an elaborate scheme to kidnap Sita.
claims.statement_id: Menurut keterangan Museum Carlos, setelah saudarinya dilukai Ravana merancang balas dendam berupa skema rumit untuk menculik Sita.
claims.quote: After his sister is mutilated, Ravana plots revenge in the form an elaborate scheme to kidnap Sita.

claims.statement: According to the Carlos Museum, Ravana's brother Maricha takes the form of a golden deer and bounds past Rama's hermitage; Sita asks Rama to kill the deer, so Rama tells Lakshmana to watch over Sita while he hunts.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Museum Carlos, Maricha, saudara Ravana, menjelma kijang emas dan melompat melewati pertapaan Rama; Sita meminta Rama membunuh kijang itu, sehingga Rama menyuruh Lakshmana menjaga Sita selagi ia berburu.
claims.quote: Ravana’s brother Maricha takes the form of a golden deer and bounds past Rama’s hermitage. Sita requests her prince to kill the deer, so Rama instructs Lakshmana to watch over Sita while he goes hunting.

claims.statement: According to the Carlos Museum, when Lakshmana hears the dying Maricha call for help in Rama's voice he is fooled into leaving his post, and Ravana seizes the opportunity to abduct Sita.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Museum Carlos, ketika Lakshmana mendengar Maricha yang sekarat meminta tolong dengan suara Rama, ia tertipu dan meninggalkan posnya; Ravana memanfaatkan kesempatan itu untuk menculik Sita.
claims.quote: When Rama is gone, Lakshmana hears Maricha, dying from Rama’s arrow, call for help in Rama’s voice, and is fooled into abandoning his post to search for Rama. Ravana seizes the opportunity to abduct Sita.

claims.statement: Ravana is depicted with ten heads, though sometimes with nine because he cut one off to convince Shiva; he is described as a devout follower of Shiva, a great scholar, a capable ruler, and a maestro of the veena.
claims.statement_id: Ravana digambarkan berkepala sepuluh, tetapi kadang hanya sembilan karena ia memotong satu kepala untuk meyakinkan Shiva; ia dilukiskan sebagai pengikut Shiva yang taat, sarjana besar, penguasa cakap, dan ahli veena.
claims.quote: Ravana is depicted and described as having ten heads, although he is sometimes shown with only nine heads since he cut one off to convince Shiva. He is described as a devout follower of Shiva, a great scholar, a capable ruler, and a maestro of the Veena.

claims.statement: A popular image of Shiva called Ravananugraha, popular in the Gupta era, depicts Ravana beneath Mount Kailash playing a veena made from his head and hands with strings of his tendons, while Shiva and Parvati sit on top of the mountain.
claims.statement_id: Citra Shiva bernama Ravananugraha, yang populer pada masa Gupta, menggambarkan Ravana di bawah Gunung Kailash memainkan veena dari kepala dan tangannya dengan dawai dari uratnya, sementara Shiva dan Parvati duduk di puncak gunung.
claims.quote: One of the most popular images of Shiva is called "Ravananugraha", which was popular in the Gupta era. It depicts Ravana beneath Mount Kailash playing a veena made out of his head and hands, and strings made out of his tendons, while Shiva and Parvati sit on top of the mountain.

claims.statement: According to scriptures, Ravana once tried to lift Mount Kailash but Shiva pushed it back and trapped him beneath it; for a thousand years he sang the Shiva Tandava Stotra until Shiva blessed him and gave him an invincible sword and a powerful linga to worship.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kitab-kitab, Ravana pernah mencoba mengangkat Gunung Kailash tetapi Shiva menekan gunung itu dan menjepit Ravana; selama seribu tahun ia menyanyikan Shiva Tandava Stotra hingga Shiva memberkatinya dengan pedang tak terkalahkan dan sebuah linga untuk dipuja.
claims.quote: According to scriptures, Ravana once tried to lift Mount Kailash, but Shiva pushed the mountain into place and trapped Ravana beneath it. For a thousand years, the imprisoned Ravana sang Shiva Tandava Stotra, a hymn in praise of Shiva, who finally blessed him and granted him an invincible sword and a powerful linga (Shiva's iconic symbol, Atmalinga) to worship.

claims.statement: Wikipedia notes that this incident has little to no evidence in the Valmiki Ramayana.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa kisah itu nyaris tidak punya bukti dalam Ramayana Valmiki.
claims.quote: But this incident has little to no evidence in Valmiki Ramayana.

claims.statement: In the Bhagavata Purana, Ravana and his brother Kumbhakarna are said to be reincarnations of Jaya and Vijaya, gatekeepers at Vaikuntha, the abode of Vishnu, cursed to be born on Earth for their insolence.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Bhagavata Purana, Ravana dan saudaranya Kumbhakarna dikatakan penjelmaan Jaya dan Vijaya, penjaga gerbang Vaikuntha kediaman Vishnu, yang dikutuk lahir di bumi karena kelancangan mereka.
claims.quote: In the Bhagavata Purana, Ravana and his brother Kumbhakarna are said to be reincarnations of Jaya and Vijaya, gatekeepers at Vaikuntha (the abode of Vishnu), and were cursed to be born on Earth for their insolence.

claims.statement: In Jainism, Rama and Ravana were both devout Jains; Ravana was a Vidyadhara king with magical powers, and it was Lakshmana, not Rama, who ultimately killed him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Jainisme, Rama dan Ravana sama-sama penganut Jain yang taat; Ravana adalah raja Vidyadhara yang bersaktikan sihir, dan yang akhirnya membunuhnya adalah Lakshmana, bukan Rama.
claims.quote: In Jainism, both Rama and Ravana were devout Jains. Ravana was a Vidyadhara king who had magical powers, and Lakshmana, not Rama, was the one who ultimately killed Ravana.

claims.statement: Ravana is worshipped as one of Shiva's most revered followers and is even worshipped in some Shiva temples.
claims.statement_id: Ravana dipuja sebagai salah satu pengikut Shiva yang paling dihormati, bahkan dipuja di beberapa kuil Shiva.
claims.quote: Ravana is worshipped as one of Shiva's most revered followers, and he is even worshipped in some Shiva temples.

claims.statement: The Gondi people of central India claim descent from Ravana and have temples for him, his wife Mandodari, and their son Meghnad.
claims.statement_id: Suku Gondi di India tengah mengaku keturunan Ravana dan memiliki kuil untuknya, istrinya Mandodari, dan putra mereka Meghnad.
claims.quote: The Gondi people of central India claim to be descendants of Ravana, and have temples for him, his wife Mandodari, and their son Meghnad.

claims.statement: Ravana wrestled his brother Kubera and vanquished him for the Pushpaka Vimana.
claims.statement_id: Ravana bergulat dengan saudaranya Kubera dan menaklukkannya demi Pushpaka Vimana.
claims.quote: Ravana had wrestled his brother Kubera and vanquished him for the Pushpaka Vimana.

claims.statement: Yama is the Hindu god of death and justice associated with punishment in Naraka.
claims.statement_id: Yama adalah dewa kematian dan keadilan Hindu yang dikaitkan dengan hukuman di Naraka.
claims.quote: Yama ... is the Hindu god of death and justice, responsible for the dispensation of law and punishment of sinners in his abode, Naraka.

claims.statement: Kala and Dharmaraja are other names of Yama.
claims.statement_id: Kala dan Dharmaraja merupakan nama lain Yama.
claims.quote: also known as Kāla and Dharmarāja

claims.statement: In Vedic tradition he is the first mortal to die and find the path to the abode of the dead.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Weda ia adalah manusia pertama yang meninggal dan menemukan jalan ke tempat orang mati.
claims.quote: In Vedic tradition, Yama was considered the first mortal who died and espied the way to the celestial abodes; as a result, he became the ruler of the departed. His role, characteristics, and abode have been expounded in texts such as the Upanishads, the Ramayana, the Mahabharata, and the Puranas.

claims.statement: He is described as Yami's twin and the son of Surya and Sanjna.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut saudara kembar Yami serta putra Surya dan Sanjna.
claims.quote: Yama is described as the twin of the goddess Yami, and the son of the god Surya (sun) (in earlier traditions Vivasvat) and Sanjna.

claims.statement: He judges souls and assigns them according to their deeds to the ancestors' realm, Naraka, or rebirth.
claims.statement_id: Ia menilai jiwa dan menempatkannya menurut perbuatan ke alam leluhur, Naraka, atau kelahiran kembali.
claims.quote: He judges the souls of the dead and, depending on their deeds, assigns them to the realm of the Pitris (forefathers), Naraka (hell), or to be reborn on the earth.

claims.statement: Yama guards the south as one of the Lokapalas.
claims.statement_id: Yama menjaga arah selatan sebagai salah satu Lokapala.
claims.quote: Yama is one of the Lokapalas (guardians of the realms), appointed as the protector of the south direction.

claims.statement: He is often depicted with dark skin and riding a buffalo.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering digambarkan berkulit gelap dan menunggang kerbau.
claims.quote: He is often depicted as a dark-complexioned man riding a buffalo

claims.statement: In his depictions he carries a noose or mace to capture souls.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penggambarannya ia membawa jerat atau gada untuk menangkap jiwa.
claims.quote: and carrying a noose or mace to capture souls.

claims.statement: Yama means twin in one explanation of his name.
claims.statement_id: Yama berarti kembar dalam salah satu penjelasan etimologinya.
claims.quote: The word "Yama" means 'twin' (Yama has a twin sister, Yami), and later came to mean 'binder' (derived from "yam"); the word also means 'moral rule or duty' (i.e. dharma), 'self-control', 'forbearance', and 'cessation'.

claims.statement: Pashi is an epithet meaning bearer of a noose.
claims.statement_id: Pashi adalah sebutan yang bermakna pembawa jerat.
claims.quote: Yama is also known by many other names, including Kala ('time'), Pashi (one who carries a noose') and Dharmaraja ('lord of Dharma').

claims.statement: Yama is often identified with Dharmadeva in tradition.
claims.statement_id: Yama kerap diidentifikasi dengan Dharmadeva dalam tradisi.
claims.quote: Yama and Dharmadeva, the god personifying the concept of Dharma, are generally considered to be one and the same person. Author Vettam Mani speculates a reason for this identification:

claims.statement: Vettam Mani distinguishes Yama and Dharmadeva as two deities with different origin stories.
claims.statement_id: Vettam Mani membedakan Yama dan Dharmadeva sebagai dua dewa dengan kisah asal berbeda.
claims.quote: Mani believes that Yama and Dharmadeva are two different deities, citing that the Puranic scriptures depict at least two different legends about the deities —

claims.statement: Yama's figure is adapted as king of hell in Buddhist mythology and several East Asian and Tibetan traditions.
claims.statement_id: Sosok Yama diadaptasi sebagai raja neraka dalam mitologi Buddha dan sejumlah tradisi Asia Timur serta Tibet.
claims.quote: Yama was subsequently adopted by Buddhist, Chinese, Tibetan, Korean, and Japanese mythology as the king of hell. In modern culture, Yama has been depicted in various safety campaigns in India.

claims.statement: In the Savitri story retold by Mackenzie, Yama releases Satyavan and promises the couple long life.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Savitri yang diceritakan Mackenzie, Yama melepaskan Satyavan dan menjanjikan hidup panjang bagi pasangan itu.
claims.quote:
Said Yama: “So be it. With cheerful heart I now
unbind thy husband. He is free.... Disease cannot
afflict him again and he will prosper. Together you will
both have long life; you will live four hundred years;
you will have a century of sons and they will be kings,
and their sons will be kings also.”

claims.statement: The 1911 Britannica says three Rigveda hymns are addressed to Yama.
claims.statement_id: Britannica 1911 menyebut tiga himne Rigveda ditujukan kepada Yama.
claims.quote: ​YAMA (Sanskrit "twin," in allusion to his being twin with his sister Yami, traditionally the first human pair), in Hindu mythology, judge of men and king of the unseen world. He was the first mortal to die, and having discovered the way to the other world is the guide of the dead. Three hymns in the Rig Veda are addressed to him.

claims.statement: In Griffith's translation of Rigveda 10.14, Yama is called the King, Vivasvan's son, who gathers men together, travelled to the lofty heights above, and searches out and shows the path to many.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Griffith atas Rigveda 10.14, Yama disebut Raja, putra Vivasvan, yang mengumpulkan manusia, menempuh ketinggian di atas kita, serta mencari dan menunjukkan jalan bagi banyak orang.
claims.quote: HONOUR the King with thine oblations, Yama, Vivasvan's Son, who gathers men together, Who travelled to the lofty heights above us, who searches out and shows the path to many.

claims.statement: Rigveda 10.14 speaks of Yama's two dogs as watchers, four-eyed, who look on men and guard the pathway.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda 10.14 menyebut dua anjing Yama sebagai penjaga berempat mata yang mengawasi manusia dan menjaga jalan.
claims.quote: And those two dogs of thine, Yama, the watchers, four-eyed, who look on men and guard the pathway

claims.statement: In the translation Mackenzie quotes, Yama was the first of men that died, the first to brave Death's rapid rushing stream, and the first to point the road to heaven and welcome others to that abode.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan yang dikutip Mackenzie, Yama adalah manusia pertama yang mati, yang pertama menerjang arus deras kematian, dan yang pertama menunjukkan jalan ke surga serta menyambut orang lain di sana.
claims.quote: To Yama, mighty king, be gifts and homage paid. He was the first of men that died, the first to brave Death's rapid rushing stream, the first to point the road To heaven, and welcome others to that bright abode.

claims.statement: According to Mackenzie, Yama judged men as Dharma-rajah, "King of righteousness," and was called Pitripati, "lord of the fathers," Samavurti, "the impartial judge," Kritana, "the finisher," Antaka, "he who ends life," and Samana, "the leveller."
claims.statement_id: Menurut Mackenzie, Yama menghakimi manusia sebagai Dharma-rajah ("Raja Kebenaran"), dan ia disebut Pitripati ("penguasa para leluhur"), Samavurti ("hakim yang adil"), Kritana ("sang penyelesai"), Antaka ("yang mengakhiri hidup"), dan Samana ("sang perata").
claims.quote: Yama judged men as Dharma-rajah, “King of righteousness”; he was Pitripati, “lord of the fathers”; Samavurti, “the impartial judge”; Kritana, “the finisher”; Antaka, “he who ends life”; Samana, “the leveller”, &c.

claims.statement: According to Mackenzie, in post-Vedic times Yama presided over a complicated system of Hells as Dandadhara, "the wielder of the rod or mace," had a noose to bind souls, and carried out the decrees of the gods by taking souls at their appointed time.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Mackenzie, pada masa pasca-Weda Yama memimpin sistem neraka yang rumit sebagai Dandadhara ("pemegang tongkat atau gada"), memiliki jerat untuk mengikat jiwa, dan melaksanakan keputusan para dewa dengan mengambil jiwa pada waktunya.
claims.quote: In post-Vedic times he presided over a complicated system of Hells; he was Dandadhara, “the wielder of the rod or mace”. He had a noose with which to bind souls; he carried out the decrees of the gods, taking possession of souls at their appointed time.

claims.statement: Mackenzie writes that Yama gathers his people to him as a shepherd gathers his flock, so that he is called the "Noble Shepherd."
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menulis bahwa Yama mengumpulkan umatnya seperti gembala mengumpulkan kawanan dombanya, sehingga ia disebut Gembala Mulia (Noble Shepherd).
claims.quote: He gathers his people to him as a shepherd gathers his flock: indeed he is called the “Noble Shepherd”.

claims.statement: According to Mackenzie, Yama might prolong the life of one whose days had run out if another gave up part of his own life, and might even restore a soul he had bound, at the appeal of a mortal of great piety.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Mackenzie, Yama dapat memperpanjang umur orang yang waktunya habis bila orang lain merelakan sebagian umurnya, bahkan mengembalikan jiwa yang telah ia ikat atas permohonan manusia yang sangat saleh.
claims.quote: Yama might consent to prolong the life of one whose days had run out, on condition that another individual gave up part of his own life in compensation; he might even agree to restore a soul which he had bound to carry away, in response to the appeal of a mortal who had attained to great piety.

claims.statement: In the Katha Upanishad, Yama is portrayed as a teacher to the Brahmin boy Nachiketa; after granting three boons, their conversation turns to the nature of being, knowledge, the Atman, and moksha.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Katha Upanishad, Yama digambarkan sebagai guru bagi Nachiketa, anak Brahmana; setelah mengabulkan tiga permintaan, percakapan mereka berkembang menjadi pembahasan hakikat keberadaan, pengetahuan, Atman, dan moksha.
claims.quote: In the Katha Upanishad, Yama is portrayed as a teacher to the Brahmin boy Nachiketa. Having granted three boons to Nachiketa, their conversation evolves to a discussion of the nature of being, knowledge, the Atman (i.e. the soul, self) and moksha (liberation).

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, in the Yaksha Prashna Dharmadeva (Yama) appears as a yaksha in the form of a crane to test Yudhishthira; impressed by his answers, Yama reveals himself as his father, blesses him, and revives his younger Pandava brothers.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, dalam Yaksha Prashna Dharmadeva (Yama) menjelma yaksha berupa bangau untuk menguji Yudhishthira; terkesan oleh jawabannya, Yama menyatakan diri sebagai ayahnya, memberkatinya, dan menghidupkan kembali saudara-saudara Pandawa.
claims.quote: In the Yaksha Prashna, Dharmadeva (Yama) appears as a yaksha (nature spirit) in the form of a crane to question Yudhishthira and test his righteousness. Impressed by Yudhishthira's strict adherence to dharma and his answers to the riddles posed, Yama reveals himself as his father, blesses him, and brings his younger Pandava brothers back to life.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, in the Vana Parva the story of Savitri and Satyavan is told: after Savitri's husband Satyavan died, Yama came to carry away his soul but was so impressed by Savitri's purity and dedication to dharma and her husband that he brought Satyavan back to life.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, dalam Vana Parva diceritakan kisah Savitri dan Satyavan: setelah Satyavan, suami Savitri, meninggal, Yama datang mengambil jiwanya tetapi terkesan oleh kesucian dan pengabdian Savitri pada dharma dan suaminya, sehingga menghidupkan Satyavan kembali.
claims.quote: In the Vana Parva, ... the sage replied by relating the story of Savitri and Satyavan. After Savitri's husband Satyavan died, Yama arrived to carry away his soul. However, Yama was so impressed with Savitri's purity and dedication to dharma and to her husband, he was convinced to instead bring Satyavan back to life.

claims.statement: In the Puranas, Yama is described with four arms, protruding fangs, the complexion of storm clouds, a wrathful expression, a garland of flames, red, yellow, or blue garments, a noose and a mace or sword, riding a water-buffalo.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Purana, Yama dilukiskan berlengan empat, bertaring mencuat, berkulit seperti awan badai, berwajah murka, dikelilingi karangan api, berpakaian merah, kuning, atau biru, memegang jerat serta gada atau pedang, dan menunggang kerbau air.
claims.quote: In Puranas, Yama is described as having four arms, protruding fangs, and complexion of storm clouds, with a wrathful expression; surrounded by a garland of flames; dressed in red, yellow, or blue garments; holding a noose and a mace or sword; and riding a water-buffalo.

claims.statement: Wikipedia notes that throughout Vedic literature Yama becomes more and more associated with the negative aspects of death and eventually becomes the god of death.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa sepanjang sastra Weda Yama makin lekat dengan sisi gelap kematian hingga akhirnya menjadi dewa kematian.
claims.quote: Throughout the course of Vedic literature, Yama becomes more and more associated with the negative aspects of death and eventually becomes the god of death.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, Yama has two four-eyed, broad-nosed, reddish-brown dogs, Sharvara and Shyama, sons of Sarama; in the Atharvaveda one is brindled and the other dark.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, Yama memiliki dua anjing berempat mata berhidung lebar berwarna cokelat kemerahan, Sharvara dan Shyama, putra Sarama; dalam Atharwaweda salah satunya belang dan yang lain gelap.
claims.quote: Yama has two four-eyed, broad nosed, brindled, reddish-brown dogs, Sharvara and Shyama, who are the sons of Saramā. However, in the Atharvaveda, one of dogs is brindled and the other is dark.

claims.statement: Wikipedia notes that Yama is revered in Tibet as the Lord of Death and as a guardian of spiritual practice.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa Yama dihormati di Tibet sebagai Penguasa Kematian dan pelindung latihan spiritual.
claims.quote: Yama is revered in Tibet as the Lord of Death and as a guardian of spiritual practice.

claims.statement: Radha is a Hindu goddess and Krishna's chief consort.
claims.statement_id: Radha adalah dewi Hindu dan pasangan utama Krishna.
claims.quote: Radha (Sanskrit: राधा, IAST: Rādhā), also called Radhika, is a Hindu goddess and the chief consort of the god Krishna. She is revered as goddess of love, tenderness, compassion and devotion. In scriptures, Radha is mentioned as the avatar of Lakshmi and also as the Mūlaprakriti, the Supreme goddess, who is the feminine counterpart and internal potency (hladini shakti) of Krishna.

claims.statement: Radhika is another name for Radha.
claims.statement_id: Radhika merupakan nama lain Radha.
claims.quote: Radha (Sanskrit: राधा, IAST: Rādhā), also called Radhika, is a Hindu goddess and the chief consort of the god Krishna. She is revered as goddess of love, tenderness, compassion and devotion. In scriptures, Radha is mentioned as the avatar of Lakshmi and also as the Mūlaprakriti, the Supreme goddess, who is the feminine counterpart and internal potency (hladini shakti) of Krishna.

claims.statement: She is revered as a goddess of love, tenderness, compassion, and devotion.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipuja sebagai dewi cinta, kelembutan, kasih sayang, dan bakti.
claims.quote: Radha (Sanskrit: राधा, IAST: Rādhā), also called Radhika, is a Hindu goddess and the chief consort of the god Krishna. She is revered as goddess of love, tenderness, compassion and devotion. In scriptures, Radha is mentioned as the avatar of Lakshmi and also as the Mūlaprakriti, the Supreme goddess, who is the feminine counterpart and internal potency (hladini shakti) of Krishna.

claims.statement: Some scriptures call her Lakshmi's incarnation and Krishna's internal potency called hladini shakti.
claims.statement_id: Sejumlah kitab menyebutnya penjelmaan Lakshmi dan daya batin Krishna yang disebut hladini shakti.
claims.quote: In scriptures, Radha is mentioned as the avatar of Lakshmi and also as the Mūlaprakriti, the Supreme goddess, who is the feminine counterpart and internal potency (hladini shakti) of Krishna.

claims.statement: Nimbarka and many Vaishnava traditions worship her as Krishna's eternal wife.
claims.statement_id: Nimbarka dan banyak tradisi Waisnawa memujanya sebagai istri abadi Krishna.
claims.quote: Radha accompanies Krishna in all his incarnations. The Nimbarka Sampradaya and many other Vaishnava traditions worship Radha as the eternal consort and wedded wife of Krishna. In contrast, traditions like Gaudiya Vaishnavism revere her as Krishna's lover and the divine consort.

claims.statement: Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition emphasises Radha as Krishna's beloved and divine consort.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi Gaudiya Waisnawa menekankan Radha sebagai kekasih serta pasangan ilahi Krishna.
claims.quote: Radha accompanies Krishna in all his incarnations. The Nimbarka Sampradaya and many other Vaishnava traditions worship Radha as the eternal consort and wedded wife of Krishna. In contrast, traditions like Gaudiya Vaishnavism revere her as Krishna's lover and the divine consort.

claims.statement: Radha Vallabha and Haridasi venerate her as the supreme being.
claims.statement_id: Radha Vallabha dan Haridasi memujanya sebagai sosok tertinggi.
claims.quote: In Radha Vallabha Sampradaya and Haridasi Sampradaya, only Radha is worshipped as the Supreme being. Radha is described as the chief of Braj Gopis (milkmaids of Braj) and queen of Goloka and Braj including Vrindavan and Barsana. She has inspired numerous literary works, and her Raslila dance with Krishna has inspired many types of performance arts.

claims.statement: She is called chief of the Braj gopis and queen of Goloka and Braj.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut pemimpin para gopi Braj dan ratu Goloka serta Braj.
claims.quote: In Radha Vallabha Sampradaya and Haridasi Sampradaya, only Radha is worshipped as the Supreme being. Radha is described as the chief of Braj Gopis (milkmaids of Braj) and queen of Goloka and Braj including Vrindavan and Barsana. She has inspired numerous literary works, and her Raslila dance with Krishna has inspired many types of performance arts.

claims.statement: Radha's name is explained as prosperity, success, perfection, and wealth.
claims.statement_id: Nama Radha dijelaskan bermakna kemakmuran, keberhasilan, kesempurnaan, dan kekayaan.
claims.quote: The Sanskrit term Rādhā (Sanskrit: राधा) means "prosperity, success, perfection and wealth". It is a common word and name found in various contexts in the ancient and medieval texts of India. The word appears in the Vedic literature as well as the Hindu epics, but is elusive. The name also appears for a figure in the epic Mahabharata. Rādhikā refers to an endearing form of Radha.

claims.statement: The Narada Pancharatra records 1008 of her names in the Shri Radha Saharsnama Strotam.
claims.statement_id: Narada Pancharatra mencatat 1008 namanya dalam Shri Radha Saharsnama Strotam.
claims.quote: The fifth chapter, Fifth night of Narada Pancharatra mentioned 1008 names of Radha under the title Shri Radha Saharsnama Strotam. The 68th chapter, Tritiya paad of Narada Purana also listed 500 names of Radha. Some of the common names and epithets are:

claims.statement: In the sixteenth century Bhakti movement, Radha's love for Krishna became more prominent.
claims.statement_id: Pada gerakan Bhakti abad keenam belas, cinta Radha kepada Krishna menjadi lebih menonjol.
claims.quote: During the Bhakti movement era in the sixteenth century, she became more well known as her extraordinary love for Krishna was highlighted.

claims.statement: Jayadeva's twelfth century Gita Govinda is one of her major literary appearances.
claims.statement_id: Gita Govinda karya Jayadeva pada abad kedua belas menjadi salah satu penampilan sastra utamanya.
claims.quote: Radha's first major appearance in the 12th-century Gita Govinda in Sanskrit by Jayadeva, as well as Nimbarkacharya's philosophical works. Thus in the Gita Govinda Krishna speaks to Radha:

claims.statement: Scholarship summarised by the article distinguishes Radha as a gopi and as a goddess.
claims.statement_id: Kajian yang diringkas artikel membedakan Radha sebagai gopi dan sebagai dewi.
claims.quote: According to Jaya Chemburkar, there are at least two significant and different aspects of Radha in the literature associated with her, such as Sri Radhika namasahasram. One aspect is she is a milkmaid (gopi), another as a female deity similar to those found in the Hindu goddess traditions.

claims.statement: Archer's study says the Gita Govinda recounts separation, longing, and reunion between Radha and Krishna.
claims.statement_id: Kajian Archer menyebut Gita Govinda menuturkan perpisahan, kerinduan, dan pertemuan kembali Radha dengan Krishna.
claims.quote:
Its subject
is the estrangement of Radha and Krishna caused by Krishna's love
for other cowgirls, Radha's anguish at Krishna's neglect and lastly
the rapture which attends their final reunion.

claims.statement: Arnold's translation depicts Radha awaiting Krishna by the wood in spring.
claims.statement_id: Terjemahan Arnold menggambarkan Radha menanti Krishna di tepi hutan pada musim semi.
claims.quote:
Beautiful Radha, Jasmine bosomed Radha,
All in the Spring-time waited by the wood
For Krishna fair, Krishna the all-forgetful,

claims.statement: Radha's birthday is celebrated every year at Radhashtami.
claims.statement_id: Hari lahir Radha dirayakan setiap tahun pada Radhashtami.
claims.quote: Radha's birthday is celebrated every year on the occasion of Radhashtami.

claims.statement: Among her epithets are Raseshvari and Rasa-priya (queen of the Raslila, fond of the rasa dance), Vrindavaneshvari (queen of Vrindavan) and Krishneshvari (feminine counterpart of Krishna).
claims.statement_id: Di antara julukannya: Raseshvari dan Rasa-priya (ratu Raslila dan yang gemar tarian rasa), Vrindavaneshvari (ratu Vrindavan), dan Krishneshvari (padanan perempuan Krishna).
claims.quote: Raseshvari and Rasa-priya: Queen of Raslila and she who is fond of rasa dance Vrindavaneshvari: Queen of Vrindavan Krishneshvari: Feminine counterpart of Krishna

claims.statement: Radha appears in several Puranas: the Padma Purana (as an avatar of Lakshmi), the Devi-Bhagavata (as a form of Mahadevi), the Brahma Vaivarta (Radha-Krishna as supreme deity), the Matsya, Linga, Varaha (as Krishna's consort), Narada (as goddess of love), Skanda and Shiva Puranas.
claims.statement_id: Radha muncul dalam berbagai Purana: Padma Purana (avatar Lakshmi), Devi-Bhagavata Purana (wujud Mahadevi), Brahma Vaivarta Purana (Radha-Krishna sebagai dewa tertinggi), Matsya, Linga, Varaha (pasangan Krishna), Narada (dewi cinta), Skanda, dan Shiva Purana.
claims.quote: Radha also appears in the Puranas namely the Padma Purana (as an avatar of Lakshmi), the Devi-Bhagavata Purana (as a form of Mahadevi), the Brahma Vaivarta Purana (as Radha-Krishna supreme deity), the Matsya Purana (as form of Devi), the Linga Purana (as form of Lakshmi), the Varaha Purana (as consort of Krishna), the Narada Purana (as goddess of love), the Skanda Purana and the Shiva Purana.

claims.statement: The Gatha Saptasati, written around the first or second century AD, mentions Radha explicitly in its verse.
claims.statement_id: Gatha Saptasati, yang ditulis sekitar abad pertama atau kedua Masehi, menyebut Radha secara eksplisit dalam baitnya.
claims.quote: The text was written around first or second century AD. Gatha Saptasati mentioned Radha explicitly in its verse:

claims.statement: In Arnold's translation, the opening of the Gita Govinda has Krishna's feet find the road aright led by Radha's spirit, and together they taste love's divine delight.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Arnold, pembukaan Gita Govinda menyebut kaki Krishna menemukan jalan yang benar karena dituntun roh Radha, dan bersama-sama mereka mengecap kenikmatan ilahi cinta.
claims.quote: So Nanda spoke -- and led by Radha’s spirit, The feet of Krishna found the road aright; Wherefore, in bliss which all high hearts inherit, Together taste they love's divine delight.

claims.statement: Nagas are a class of divine or semidivine human and serpent beings in Asian traditions.
claims.statement_id: Naga adalah kelompok makhluk ilahi atau setengah ilahi berbentuk manusia dan ular dalam tradisi Asia.
claims.quote: In various Asian religious traditions, the Nāgas ... are a divine, or semi-divine, race of half-human, half-serpent beings

claims.statement: Their dwelling is called Patala, the netherworld.
claims.statement_id: Tempat tinggalnya disebut Patala, alam bawah.
claims.quote: that reside in the netherworld (Patala), and can occasionally take human or part-human form, or are so depicted in art.

claims.statement: They can appear as humans, serpents, or mixed human and serpent beings.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dapat tampil sebagai manusia, ular, atau makhluk campuran manusia dan ular.
claims.quote: They are principally depicted in three forms: as entirely human with snakes on the heads and necks, as common serpents, or as half-human, half-snake beings in Hinduism and Buddhism.

claims.statement: A female naga is called Nagini.
claims.statement_id: Naga perempuan disebut Nagini.
