claims.quote: A female nāga is called a Nagini

claims.statement: Kashyapa and Kadru are called this class's parents in legend.
claims.statement_id: Kashyapa dan Kadru disebut sebagai orang tua kelompok ini dalam legenda.
claims.quote: According to legend, they are the children of the sage Kashyapa and Kadru.

claims.statement: Nagaraja is the title of the king of nagas.
claims.statement_id: Nagaraja adalah gelar raja para naga.
claims.quote: Nagaraja is the title given to the king of the nāgas.

claims.statement: Their narratives are important in Hindu and Buddhist traditions in South and Southeast Asia.
claims.statement_id: Kisah mereka penting dalam tradisi Hindu dan Buddha di Asia Selatan serta Tenggara.
claims.quote: Narratives of these beings hold cultural significance in the mythological traditions of many South Asian and Southeast Asian cultures, and within Hinduism and Buddhism.

claims.statement: Naga in Sanskrit primarily means snake, often the Indian cobra.
claims.statement_id: Naga dalam Sanskerta terutama berarti ular, sering kali kobra India.
claims.quote: In Sanskrit, a nāga ... primarily refers to a snake, most often specifically the Indian cobra (Naja naja).

claims.statement: Nagas are prominent in Hindu iconography and the first book of the Mahabharata.
claims.statement_id: Naga menonjol dalam ikonografi Hindu dan buku pertama Mahabharata.
claims.quote: Nāgas, as a serpent-shaped group of deities that often take form as cobras, are prominent in Hindu iconography, throughout Hindu texts (especially in the first book of the Mahābhārata) and in local folk traditions of worship.

claims.statement: Naga-loka is described as containing gems, gold, and earthly treasures.
claims.statement_id: Alam Naga-loka digambarkan berisi permata, emas, dan harta bumi.
claims.quote: Their domain is in the enchanted underworld, the underground realm filled with gems, gold and other earthly treasures called Naga-loka or Patala-loka.

claims.statement: Nagas are associated with rivers, lakes, seas, and wells and with guarding treasure.
claims.statement_id: Naga dikaitkan dengan sungai, danau, laut, dan sumur serta peran penjaga harta.
claims.quote: They are also often associated with bodies of waters—including rivers, lakes, seas, and wells—and are guardians of treasure.

claims.statement: Vishnu is depicted reclining on Shesha or sheltered by his hood.
claims.statement_id: Vishnu digambarkan berbaring pada Shesha atau dilindungi tudungnya.
claims.quote: Vishnu is originally portrayed in the form sheltered by Sheshanāga or reclining on Shesha, but the iconography has been extended to other deities as well.

claims.statement: In South India, termite hills are regarded as dwellings of female nagammas.
claims.statement_id: Di India Selatan, sarang rayap dianggap tempat tinggal nagamma perempuan.
claims.quote: In South India, termite hills are believed to be the dwelling place of female nagammas, whereas Himalayan Nags and Naginis, such as Naiṇī Devī of Pindar Valley, are worshipped as underworld beings protecting water resources and the wellbeing of village and valley.

claims.statement: Mackenzie discusses nagas as demigods who sometimes aid humans and give strength enhancing drinks in stories.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie membahas naga sebagai setengah dewa yang kadang membantu manusia dan memberi minuman penambah kekuatan dalam cerita.
claims.quote:
When serpent worship became prevalent among the
Aryans, the Nagas were regarded as demigods. They
were occasionally “the friends of man”, and to those
they favoured they gave draughts of their nectar, which
endowed them with great strength. Their city was the
Paradise of serpent worshippers. The female Nagas
were beautiful nymphs, who were sometimes wooed by
mortals.

claims.statement: The Cleveland Museum explains the importance of nagas to local worshippers as controllers of water supporting prosperity.
claims.statement_id: Museum Cleveland menjelaskan pentingnya naga bagi pemuja lokal sebagai pengendali air yang menunjang kemakmuran.
claims.quote: Nagas continue to be important divinities in local piety, for they control the forces of water, essential for prosperity.

claims.statement: Wikipedia adds that nāgas are also known as dragons and water spirits.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia menambahkan bahwa naga juga dikenal sebagai dragon dan roh air.
claims.quote: Furthermore, nāgas are also known as dragons and water spirits.

claims.statement: The Cleveland Museum of Art reads the coils of a serpent's body and the bottle of water in the figure's hand as confirming it as a water serpent divinity called a naga.
claims.statement_id: Museum Seni Cleveland membaca lilitan tubuh ular dan botol air di tangan arca itu sebagai tanda bahwa tokohnya adalah dewa ular air yang disebut naga.
claims.quote: The coils of a serpent's body and the bottle of water in his hand confirm the identity of this figure as a water serpent divinity called a naga.

claims.statement: Mackenzie describes the Nagas as demoniac cobras dwelling in the Underworld, human to the waist and serpent below; their king is Shesha, also named Vasuki and Karkotaka, sometimes shown with a thousand heads.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menyebut para Naga sebagai kobra setan yang menghuni dunia bawah, berwujud manusia hingga pinggang dan seperti ular di bawahnya; rajanya Shesha, yang juga disebut Vasuki dan Karkotaka, kadang digambarkan berkepala seribu.
claims.quote: In the Underworld dwell also the Nagas, the demoniac Cobras; they are of human form to the waist, the rest of their bodies being like those of serpents. Their king is Shesha, who is also named Vasuki and Karkotáka; he is sometimes represented with a thousand heads

claims.statement: In the account of the heaven of Varuna that Mackenzie quotes, hooded snakes (Nagas) with human heads and arms wait upon the lord of the waters, together with Daityas and Danavas.
claims.statement_id: Dalam uraian surga Varuna yang dikutip Mackenzie, ular berkerudung (Naga) berkepala dan berlengan manusia melayani penguasa perairan, bersama para Daitya dan Danava.
claims.quote: Varuna, richly decked with jewels and golden ornaments and flowers, is throned there with his queen. ... wait upon the lord of the waters, as also do hooded snakes (Nagas) with human heads and arms, and Daityas and Danavas (giants and demons) who have taken vows and have been rewarded with immortality.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, ancient Sanskrit texts such as the Mahabharata, Ramayana, and Puranas describe the nāgas as a powerful, splendid, and proud semi-divine species that can appear as human (often with a halo of cobra hoods), as a partially human serpent, or as a whole serpent.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, teks Sanskerta kuno seperti Mahabharata, Ramayana, dan Purana menggambarkan naga sebagai spesies semi-ilahi yang perkasa, megah, dan angkuh, yang dapat tampil sebagai manusia (sering dengan lingkaran tudung kobra di belakang kepala), ular setengah manusia, atau ular utuh.
claims.quote: Ancient Sanskrit texts such as the Mahabharata, the Ramayana, and the Puranas describe the nāgas as a powerful, splendid and proud semi-divine species that can assume their physical form either as human (often with a halo of cobra hoods behind their head), as a partially human serpent, or as a whole serpent.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, their power and venom make nāgas potentially dangerous to humans, but in Hindu mythology they often play benevolent roles; in the Samudra Manthana, Vasuki, a nagaraja who abides on Shiva's neck, becomes the churning rope for the Ocean of Milk.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, kekuatan dan bisa naga berpotensi membahayakan manusia, tetapi dalam mitologi Hindu mereka sering menjadi tokoh yang baik hati; dalam Samudra Manthana, Vasuki, nagaraja yang bersemayam di leher Shiva, menjadi tali untuk mengaduk Lautan Susu.
claims.quote: Their power and venom make them potentially dangerous to humans. However, in Hindu mythology, they often take the role of benevolent protagonists: in the Samudra Manthana, Vasuki, a nagaraja who abides on Shiva's neck, became the churning rope for churning of the Ocean of Milk.

claims.statement: Wikipedia notes that the eternal archrival of the nāgas is Garuda, the legendary semi-divine bird-like deity.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia mencatat bahwa musuh bebuyutan abadi para naga adalah Garuda, dewa mirip burung yang legendaris dan semi-ilahi.
claims.quote: Their eternal archrival is the Garuḍa, the legendary semi-divine bird-like deity.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, the Mahabharata is the first text to introduce nāgas; the cosmic snake Shesha, the nagarajas Vasuki, Takshaka, Airavata, and Karkotaka, and the princess Ulupi all appear in it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, Mahabharata adalah teks pertama yang memperkenalkan naga; di dalamnya tampil ular kosmik Shesha, para nagaraja Vasuki, Takshaka, Airavata, dan Karkotaka, serta putri Ulupi.
claims.quote: The Mahabharata epic is the first text that introduces nāgas; it describes them in detail and narrates their stories. The cosmic snake Shesha, the nagarajas (nāga kings) Vasuki, Takshaka, Airavata and Karkotaka, and the princess Ulupi, are all depicted in the Mahabharata.

claims.statement: In Buddhist tradition, Mucalinda, nagaraja and protector of the Buddha, shelters the meditating Buddha from a great storm by covering his head with his seven snake heads.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Buddha, Mucalinda, nagaraja pelindung Buddha, menaungi Buddha yang bermeditasi di hutan dari badai besar dengan menutupi kepala Buddha dengan tujuh kepala ularnya.
claims.quote: Among the notable nāgas of Buddhist tradition is Mucalinda, nagaraja and protector of the Buddha. In the Vinaya Sutra (I, 3), shortly after his enlightenment, the Buddha is meditating in a forest when a great storm arises, but graciously, King Mucalinda gives shelter to the Buddha from the storm by covering the Buddha's head with his seven snake heads.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, the Khmer people regard themselves as descendants of the nāgas, and many still believe the nāgas exist today and are destined to return and restore prosperity to their people.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, orang Khmer menganggap diri keturunan para naga dan banyak yang masih percaya bahwa naga ada hingga kini dan ditakdirkan kembali untuk memulihkan kemakmuran rakyat mereka.
claims.quote: The Khmer people regard themselves as descendants of the nāgas and many still believe the nāga exist today, destined to one day return and restore prosperity to their people.

claims.statement: According to a popular legend, the Mekong River in north-eastern Thailand and Laos was created by two Nāga kings slithering through the area, which also created the nearby Nan River.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda populer, Sungai Mekong di timur laut Thailand dan Laos tercipta oleh dua raja Naga yang menggeliat di kawasan itu, sehingga terbentuk pula Sungai Nan di dekatnya.
claims.quote: According to a popular legend, the Mekong River in north-eastern Thailand and Laos was said to be created by two Nāga kings slithering through the area, thus creating the Mekong and the nearby Nan River.

claims.statement: In Tibetan Buddhism, nāgas are known as klu or klu-mo and are associated with water and cleanliness; they live in oceans, rivers, lakes, and springs and do not want their environments disturbed or polluted.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Buddhisme Tibet, naga dikenal sebagai klu atau klu-mo dan dikaitkan dengan air serta kebersihan; mereka hidup di samudra, sungai, danau, dan mata air, dan tidak ingin lingkungannya diganggu atau dicemari.
claims.quote: In Tibetan Buddhism, nāgas are known as klu or klu-mo and they are associated with water and cleanliness, as they live in oceans, rivers, lakes, and springs, and do not want their environments to be disturbed or polluted.

claims.statement: In Javanese, Sundanese, and Balinese culture in Indonesia, a nāga is depicted as a crowned, giant, magical serpent, sometimes winged.
claims.statement_id: Dalam budaya Jawa, Sunda, dan Bali di Indonesia, naga digambarkan sebagai ular raksasa bermahkota yang berdaya sihir dan kadang bersayap.
claims.quote: In Javanese, Sundanese, and Balinese culture, Indonesia, a nāga is depicted as a crowned, giant, magical serpent, sometimes winged.

claims.statement: In Balinese tradition, nāgas are often depicted battling garuḍas.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Bali, naga sering digambarkan bertarung melawan garuda.
claims.quote: In Balinese tradition, nāgas are often depicted battling garuḍas.

claims.statement: Deva is a Sanskrit term for a god or divine being in Hinduism.
claims.statement_id: Deva adalah istilah Sanskerta untuk dewa atau makhluk ilahi dalam agama Hindu.
claims.quote: Deva ... and is also one of the Sanskrit terms used to indicate a deity in Hinduism.

claims.statement: Deva is masculine, with the feminine form Devi.
claims.statement_id: Deva bersifat maskulin, dengan bentuk feminin Devi.
claims.quote: Deva is a masculine term; the feminine equivalent is Devi.

claims.statement: Its meanings include shining, exalted, and heavenly being.
claims.statement_id: Maknanya mencakup bersinar, luhur, dan makhluk surgawi.
claims.quote: Deva ... means 'god', 'shiny', 'exalted', 'heavenly being', 'divine being', 'anything of excellence'

claims.statement: Early Vedic literature uses Deva and Asura for supernatural beings, with meanings that later change.
claims.statement_id: Literatur Weda awal menggunakan Deva dan Asura untuk makhluk gaib, dengan pemaknaan yang berubah kemudian.
claims.quote: In the earliest Vedic literature, all supernatural beings are called Devas and Asuras. The concepts and legends evolved in ancient Indian literature, and by the late Vedic period, benevolent supernatural beings are referred to as Deva-Asuras.

claims.statement: In post Vedic texts, devas represent good and asuras evil.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks pasca-Weda, deva mewakili kebaikan dan asura keburukan.
claims.quote: In post-Vedic Hindu texts, such as the Puranas and the Itihasas of Hinduism, the Devas represent the good, and the Asuras the bad.

claims.statement: Some medieval works also use Sura as a name for devas.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian karya abad pertengahan juga memakai nama Sura untuk deva.
claims.quote: In some medieval works of Indian literature, Devas are also referred to as Suras and contrasted with their equally powerful but malevolent half-brothers, referred to as the Asuras.

claims.statement: Devas occur in Hindu cosmological theories alongside other classes of beings.
claims.statement_id: Deva termasuk dalam teori kosmologi Hindu bersama kelompok makhluk lain.
claims.quote: Devas, along with Asuras, Yakshas (nature spirits), and Rakshasas (ghoulish ogres/demons), are part of Indian mythology, and Devas feature in many cosmological theories in Hinduism.

claims.statement: The Samhitas describe 33 devas divided into eleven in each of three worlds.
claims.statement_id: Samhita menyebut 33 deva dengan pembagian sebelas pada masing-masing dari tiga dunia.
claims.quote: The Samhitas, which are the oldest layer of text in Vedas, enumerate 33 devas, either 11 each for the three worlds

claims.statement: The Brahmana layer uses a division of 12 Adityas, 11 Rudras, 8 Vasus, and 2 Asvins.
claims.statement_id: Lapisan Brahmana memakai pembagian 12 Aditya, 11 Rudra, 8 Vasu, dan 2 Aswin.
claims.quote: or as 12 Adityas, 11 Rudras, 8 Vasus and 2 Asvins in the Brahmanas layer of Vedic texts.

claims.statement: Some devas represent natural forces and others moral values, such as Varuna and Mitra.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian deva mewakili kekuatan alam, sebagian nilai moral seperti Varuna dan Mitra.
claims.quote: Some devas represent the forces of nature and some represent moral values (such as the Adityas, Varuna, and Mitra), each symbolizing the epitome of a specialized knowledge, creative energy, exalted and magical powers (Siddhis).

claims.statement: Indra, Agni, and Soma are among the devas frequently mentioned in the Rigveda.
claims.statement_id: Indra, Agni, dan Soma termasuk deva yang sering disebut Rigveda.
claims.quote: The most referred to Devas in the Rig Veda are Indra, Agni (fire) and Soma,

claims.statement: Max Muller interprets Vedic worship of devas as henotheism.
claims.statement_id: Max Muller menginterpretasikan pemujaan deva Weda sebagai henoteisme.
claims.quote: Muller concluded that the Vedic ideas about devas are best understood neither as polytheism nor as monotheism, but as henotheism

claims.statement: Max Muller interprets hymns exalting each deva in turn as henotheism.
claims.statement_id: Max Muller menafsirkan himne yang meninggikan masing-masing deva sebagai henoteisme.
claims.quote: Max Muller states that the Vedic hymns are remarkable in calling every one of the different devas as "the only one, the supreme, the greatest".

claims.statement: Mackenzie quotes an account distinguishing devas choosing truth from asuras choosing falsehood.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie mengutip kisah yang membedakan deva memilih kebenaran dan asura memilih kebohongan.
claims.quote:
This explanation is but an echo of the Indra-Vritra
combat. Another statement is to the effect that “the
Devas gave up falsehood and adopted truth, while the
Asuras gave up truth and adopted falsehood”. Further,
we learn that when a sacrifice was performed the Asuras
put the offerings into their own mouths, while the Suras
(gods) gave the offerings they received to one another.

claims.statement: Rigveda 1.139.11 invites eleven gods in heaven, eleven on earth, and eleven in the waters to accept sacrifice.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda 1.139.11 mengundang sebelas dewa di langit, sebelas di bumi, dan sebelas di air menerima pengorbanan.
claims.quote:
O ye Eleven Gods whose home is heaven, O ye Eleven who make earth your dwelling,
     Ye who with might, Eleven, live in waters, accept this sacrifice, O Gods, with pleasure.

claims.statement: Mackenzie writes that the gods are the Suras and the demons the Asuras or "non-gods," but that this distinction did not hold in the early Vedic period.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menulis bahwa para dewa adalah Sura dan para iblis adalah Asura atau "bukan-dewa", tetapi pembedaan ini belum berlaku pada masa Weda awal.
claims.quote: The gods are the Suras and the demons the Asuras or “non-gods”. This distinction, however, did not obtain in the early Vedic period.

claims.statement: According to Mackenzie, the deities, especially Varuna and Mitra, were originally called Asuras, but in the later part of the Rigveda the term is applied chiefly to the enemies of the gods.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Mackenzie, pada mulanya para dewa, terutama Varuna dan Mitra, disebut Asura, tetapi pada bagian akhir Rigveda istilah itu dipakai terutama untuk musuh para dewa.
claims.quote: Originally the deities, and especially Varuna and Mitra, were called Asuras, but in the later part of the Rigveda the term is applied chiefly to the enemies of the gods.

claims.statement: Mackenzie notes that "daeva" in the Iranian dialect, cognate with Sanskrit "deva" ("god"), came to mean "demon."
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie mencatat bahwa "daeva" dalam dialek Iran, yang sekerabat dengan "deva" Sanskerta ("dewa"), akhirnya berarti "iblis".
claims.quote: On the other hand “daeva” in the Iranian dialect, which is cognate with Sanskrit “deva”, “god”, came to mean “demon”.

claims.statement: According to Mackenzie, "asura" derives from the root "asu," which signifies "the air of life," and "deva" from "div," "to shine," or "deiwo," "heavenly."
claims.statement_id: Menurut Mackenzie, "asura" berasal dari akar "asu" yang berarti "napas kehidupan", sedangkan "deva" berasal dari "div" ("bersinar") atau "deiwo" ("surgawi").
claims.quote: “Asura” is derived from the root “asu”, which signifies “the air of life”, and “deva” from “div”, “to shine”, or “deiwo”, “heavenly”.

claims.statement: Wikipedia states that deva is a Sanskrit word found in Vedic literature of the 2nd millennium BCE.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia menyatakan bahwa deva adalah kata Sanskerta yang dijumpai dalam sastra Weda milenium ke-2 SM.
claims.quote: Deva is a Sanskrit word found in Vedic literature of the 2nd millennium BCE.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, in Vedic literature Deva is not a monotheistic God but a "supernatural, divine" concept that combines excellence in some aspects with weakness and questions in others, heroic in outlook and action, yet tied to emotions and desires.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, dalam sastra Weda Deva bukanlah Tuhan monoteistik, melainkan konsep "adikodrati dan ilahi" yang memadukan keunggulan di satu sisi dengan kelemahan dan pertanyaan di sisi lain, heroik dalam sikap dan tindakan, tetapi terikat pada emosi dan keinginan.
claims.quote: In Vedic literature, Deva is not a monotheistic God; rather a "supernatural, divine" concept manifesting in various ideas and knowledge, in a form that combines excellence in some aspects, wrestling with weakness and questions in other aspects, heroic in their outlook and actions, yet tied up with emotions and desires.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, in the oldest layer of Vedic texts all-powerful beings, good or evil, are called Devas and Asuras; they are born from the same father, Prajapati, the primordial progenitor, and his sons are envisioned as the Asuras and Devas.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, pada lapisan tertua teks Weda makhluk perkasa, baik atau jahat, disebut Deva dan Asura; mereka lahir dari ayah yang sama, Prajapati, sang pencipta awal, dan putra-putranya dibayangkan sebagai para Asura dan Deva.
claims.quote: All-powerful beings, good or evil, are called Devas and Asuras in the oldest layer of Vedic texts. ... They are born from the same father, Prajapati, the primordial progenitor; his sons are envisioned as the Asuras and Devas.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, Mantra 5.2.1 of the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad describes Devas, men, and Asuras as sons of Prajapati; Prajapati tells the Devas to observe temperance (Dama), men charity (Dana), and Asuras compassion (Daya).
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, Mantra 5.2.1 Brihadaranyaka Upanishad menyebut Deva, manusia, dan Asura sebagai putra Prajapati; Prajapati menasihati Deva untuk menjaga pengendalian diri (Dama), manusia untuk bersedekah (Dana), dan Asura untuk berwelas asih (Daya).
claims.quote: Mantra 5.2.1 of the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad describes Devas, Men, and Asuras as sons of Prajapati, the primordial father. Each asks for a lesson on ethics. Prajapati tells the Devas to observe the virtue of temperance (self-restraint, Dama), the Men to observe the virtue of charity (Dana), and Asuras to observe the virtue of compassion (Daya).

claims.statement: According to the Bhagavad Gita (16.6-16.7), as Wikipedia records, all beings in the universe have both divine qualities (daivi sampad) and demonic qualities (asuri sampad) within each.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Bhagavad Gita (16.6-16.7), sebagaimana dicatat Wikipedia, semua makhluk di alam semesta memiliki sifat ilahi (daivi sampad) sekaligus sifat iblis (asuri sampad) dalam dirinya.
claims.quote: According to the Bhagavad Gita (16.6-16.7), all beings in the universe have both the divine qualities (daivi sampad) and the demonic qualities (asuri sampad) within each.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, Ananda Coomaraswamy states that Devas and Asuras in Vedic lore are similar to the Olympian gods and Titans of Greek mythology.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, Ananda Coomaraswamy menyatakan bahwa Deva dan Asura dalam tradisi Weda mirip dengan para dewa Olympus (Olympian) dan para Titan dalam mitologi Yunani.
claims.quote: Ananda Coomaraswamy states that Devas and Asuras in the Vedic lore are similar to the Olympian gods and Titans of Greek mythology.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, Edelmann suggests that the Deva-Asura dichotomies in Hindu mythology may be seen as "narrative depictions of tendencies within our selves."
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, Edelmann menyarankan bahwa pertentangan Deva dan Asura dalam mitologi Hindu dapat dilihat sebagai "gambaran naratif kecenderungan dalam diri kita".
claims.quote: Edelmann suggests that the Deva-Asura dichotomies in Hindu mythology may be seen as "narrative depictions of tendencies within our selves".

claims.statement: Apsaras are a class of celestial female beings in Hindu and Buddhist traditions.
claims.statement_id: Apsara adalah kelompok makhluk perempuan surgawi dalam tradisi Hindu dan Buddha.
claims.quote: Apsaras (Sanskrit: अप्सरस्, IAST: Apsaras, Khmer: អប្សរា, Pali: अच्छरा, romanized: Accharā, Thai: อัปสร) are a class of celestial beings in Hindu and Buddhist culture. They were originally a type of female spirit associated with clouds and water, but, later came to play the role of a "nymph" or "fairy".

claims.statement: They are known as dancers at Indra's court.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dikenal sebagai penari istana Indra.
claims.quote: Later Hindu scriptures allow for the existence of numerous apsaras, who act as the handmaidens of Indra or as dancers at his celestial court serving as musicians alongside the gandharvas

claims.statement: Gandharvas are associated with them as musicians and partners.
claims.statement_id: Gandharva berhubungan dengan mereka sebagai musisi dan pasangan.
claims.quote: They are said to excel at dancing, and are often considered the wives of the gandharvas, the court musicians of Indra.

claims.statement: Apsaras are described as able to change their shape at will.
claims.statement_id: Apsara digambarkan dapat mengubah wujud sesuka hati.
claims.quote: The apsaras are described as being beautiful, youthful and elegant, and are said to be able to change their shape at will; making anyone fall for their beauty.

claims.statement: Apsaras are well known for a special task: being sent to earth by Indra to seduce ascetics whose severe practices may make them more powerful than the gods.
claims.statement_id: Apsara dikenal dengan tugas khusus: dikirim Indra ke bumi untuk menggoda para pertapa yang karena tapa kerasnya bisa menjadi lebih kuat daripada para dewa.
claims.quote: They are well known for their special task: being sent to earth by Indra to seduce ascetics who by their severe practices may become more powerful than the gods.

claims.statement: Urvashi, Menaka, Rambha, Tilottama, and Ghritachi are among the known apsaras.
claims.statement_id: Urvashi, Menaka, Rambha, Tilottama, dan Ghritachi termasuk apsara yang dikenal.
claims.quote: Famous apsaras include Urvashi, Menaka, Rambha, Tilottama and Ghritachi.

claims.statement: In Japan, the names Tennin and Tennyo are used for figures associated with apsaras.
claims.statement_id: Di Jepang, nama Tennin dan Tennyo digunakan untuk sosok terkait apsara.
claims.quote: In Japan, Apsara are known as "Tennin" (天人); "Tennyo" (天女) for "female Tennin" and "Tennan" (天男) for "male Tennin".

claims.statement: Monier Williams's etymology connects the name with moving in water or among cloud waters.
claims.statement_id: Etimologi Monier-Williams menghubungkan namanya dengan bergerak di air atau di antara air awan.
claims.quote: The Monier-Williams et al. (1899) gives the etymology as अप् + √सृ, "going in the waters or between the waters of the clouds".

claims.statement: Early descriptions compare apsaras to water nymphs.
claims.statement_id: Uraian awal membandingkan apsara dengan nimfa air.
claims.quote: The most ancient descriptions of apsara portray them as "water nymph"-like beings.

claims.statement: The Rigveda contains Urvashi's dialogue with her mortal lover Pururavas.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda memuat dialog Urvashi dengan kekasih manusia Pururavas.
claims.quote:
The Rigveda tells of an apsara who is the wife of Gandharva; however, the Rigveda also seems to allow for the existence of more than one apsara.
The only apsara specifically named is Urvashi.  An entire hymn deals with the colloquy between Urvashi and her mortal lover Pururavas.

claims.statement: The Kaushitaki Upanishad associates apsaras with ointments, garlands, clothes, and powdered aromatics.
claims.statement_id: Kaushitaki Upanishad mengaitkan apsara dengan minyak wangi, rangkaian bunga, pakaian, dan wewangian bubuk.
claims.quote: The Kaushitaki Upanishad mentions apsaras as a class of divinities associated with ointments, garlands, vestments, and powdered aromatics.

claims.statement: The Ramayana and Puranas connect the origin of apsaras with the churning of the ocean.
claims.statement_id: Ramayana dan Purana menghubungkan asal apsara dengan pengadukan lautan.
claims.quote: The origin of the apsaras is described in the Ramayana and Puranas. Apsaras are further associated with water by relating them to the churning of the ocean, water sports, and groups such as nāgas.

claims.statement: The Mahabharata recounts Tilottama saving the world from Sunda and Upasunda.
claims.statement_id: Mahabharata menuturkan Tilottama menyelamatkan dunia dari Sunda dan Upasunda.
claims.quote: The Mahabharata documents the exploits of individual apsaras, such as Tilottama, who rescued the world from the rampaging asura brothers Sunda and Upasunda; and Urvashi, who attempted to seduce the hero Arjuna.

claims.statement: Mackenzie recounts apsaras dancing when Gandharvas play divine instruments.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menuturkan apsara menari ketika Gandharva memainkan alat musik ilahi.
claims.quote:
When they play on their divine instruments the fairy-like
Apsaras, who are all females, dance merrily.

claims.statement: The Cleveland collection includes an Apsaras sculpture around 1920 following the style of Angkor Thom celestial maiden reliefs.
claims.statement_id: Koleksi Cleveland mencakup patung Apsaras sekitar 1920 yang mengikuti gaya relief bidadari surgawi Angkor Thom.
claims.quote: Apsaras c. 1920 France or Cambodia ... This sculpture has been carved in the style of the reliefs depicting celestial maidens at the "Terrace of the Leper King" in Angkor Thom.

claims.statement: Two types of apsaras are distinguished: laukika (worldly) and daivika (divine).
claims.statement_id: Dibedakan dua jenis apsara: laukika (duniawi) dan daivika (ilahi).
claims.quote: There are two types of apsaras—laukika (worldly) and daivika (divine).

claims.statement: Of the 26 apsaras at Indra's court, each is said to stand for a separate aspect of the performing arts, and the group is compared to the Muses of Ancient Greece.
claims.statement_id: Dari 26 apsara di istana Indra, masing-masing dikatakan melambangkan satu segi seni pertunjukan, sehingga dibandingkan dengan Muse Yunani Kuno.
claims.quote: The 26 apsaras of Indra's court are each said to symbolise a different facet of the performing arts, drawing comparisons to the Muses of Ancient Greece.

claims.statement: A recurring theme in the Mahabharata is an apsara sent to distract a sage from his ascetic practices.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Mahabharata, tema yang berulang adalah apsara yang diutus untuk mengalihkan seorang resi dari tapanya.
claims.quote: A recurring theme in the Mahabharata is that of an apsara sent to distract a sage from his ascetic practices.

claims.statement: Mackenzie states that in the Rigveda there is a water-nymph named Apsaras, the "spouse" of Gandharva, an atmospheric deity.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menyebut bahwa dalam Rigveda ada seorang nimfa air bernama Apsaras, yang menjadi "pasangan" Gandharva, dewa atmosfer.
claims.quote: In the Rigveda there is a water-nymph, named Apsaras; she is the “spouse” of Gandharva, an atmospheric deity who prepares Soma for the gods and reveals divine truths to mortals.

claims.statement: Mackenzie describes the Apsara dancing girls as "voluptuous and beautiful", inspiring love in Paradise and on earth; their lovers include gods, Gandharvas, and mortals.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menggambarkan para penari Apsara sebagai "menggairahkan dan cantik", yang membangkitkan cinta di surga maupun di bumi; kekasih mereka meliputi dewa, Gandharva, dan manusia.
claims.quote: The Apsara dancing girls are “voluptuous and beautiful”, and inspire love in Paradise as well as upon earth. Their lovers include gods, Gandharvas, and mortals.

claims.statement: In Mackenzie's retelling, the Apsaras arose from the ocean after the moon and became nymphs in Indra's heaven.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penuturan Mackenzie, apsara muncul dari lautan setelah bulan muncul dan menjadi nimfa di surga Indra.
claims.quote: At length the moon emerged from the ocean; then arose the Apsaras, who became nymphs in Indra's heaven

claims.statement: Devi is the Sanskrit word for 'goddess'; the masculine form is Deva.
claims.statement_id: Devi adalah kata Sanskerta untuk 'dewi'; bentuk maskulinnya adalah Deva.
claims.quote: Devī (/ˈdeɪvi/; Sanskrit: देवी) is the Sanskrit word for 'goddess'; the masculine form is Deva.

claims.statement: Devi and Deva mean 'heavenly, divine, anything of excellence' and are gender-specific terms for deity in Indian religions.
claims.statement_id: Devi dan Deva berarti 'surgawi, ilahi, segala yang unggul' dan merupakan istilah khusus gender untuk dewa dalam agama-agama India.
claims.quote: Devi and Deva mean 'heavenly, divine, anything of excellence', and are gender-specific terms for deity in Indian religions.

claims.statement: Shaktism centres on Devi.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi Shaktisme berpusat pada Devi.
claims.quote: The goddess centric tradition within Hinduism, namely Shaktism, is centred around Devi.

claims.statement: Medieval Puranic literature expands Devi narratives, including the Devi Mahatmya.
claims.statement_id: Literatur Purana abad pertengahan memperluas kisah Devi, termasuk Devi Mahatmya.
claims.quote: The medieval era Puranas witnessed a major expansion in mythology and literature associated with Devi, with texts such as the Devi Mahatmya, wherein the goddess is revered as the ultimate truth and supreme power.

claims.statement: The Devi Mahatmya reveres her as ultimate truth and supreme power.
claims.statement_id: Devi Mahatmya memujanya sebagai kebenaran tertinggi dan daya utama.
claims.quote: The medieval era Puranas witnessed a major expansion in mythology and literature associated with Devi, with texts such as the Devi Mahatmya, wherein the goddess is revered as the ultimate truth and supreme power.

claims.statement: Devi and Deva are explained as referring to the divine, exalted, and shining.
claims.statement_id: Devi dan Deva dijelaskan mengacu pada yang ilahi, luhur, dan bersinar.
claims.quote:
Devi and deva are Sanskrit terms found in Vedic literature around the 3rd millennium BCE. Deva is masculine, and the related feminine equivalent is devi. Monier-Williams translates it as 'heavenly, divine, terrestrial things of high excellence, exalted, shining ones'.
Etymologically, a cognate of devi is Latin dea. When capitalised, Devi maata refers to the mother goddess in Hinduism.

claims.statement: Bhagavati is an honorific for goddesses such as Lakshmi and Durga.
claims.statement_id: Bhagavati menjadi sebutan kehormatan dewi seperti Lakshmi dan Durga.
claims.quote: A synonym for the word Devi in the Vedas is Bhagavati. Bhagavatī (Devanagari: भगवती, IAST: Bhagavatī), is an Indian epithet of Sanskrit origin, used as an honorific title for goddesses in Hinduism and Buddhism. In Hinduism, it is primarily used to address the goddesses Lakshmi and Durga. In Buddhism, it is used to refer to several Mahayana Buddhist female deities, like Cundā.

claims.statement: The article connects the Devisukta with Rigveda 10.125.
claims.statement_id: Artikel menghubungkan Devisukta dengan Rigveda 10.125.
claims.quote: The Devīsūkta of the Rigveda (10.125.1 to 10.125.8) is among the most studied hymns declaring that the ultimate reality is a goddess:

claims.statement: The Vedas name Prithvi, Aditi, Vac, Ratri, and Aranyani among cosmic goddesses.
claims.statement_id: Weda menyebut Prithvi, Aditi, Vac, Ratri, dan Aranyani sebagai sejumlah dewi kosmis.
claims.quote: The Vedas name numerous cosmic goddesses such as Prithvi (earth), Aditi (cosmic moral order), Vāc (sound), Nirṛti (destruction), Ratri (night) and Aranyani (forest); bounty goddesses such as Dinsana, Raka, Puramdhi, Parendi, Bharati and Mahi are among others are mentioned in the Rigveda. However, the goddesses are not discussed as frequently as gods (devas).

claims.statement: In Shakta tradition Devi is supreme; Smarta tradition includes her among five primary forms of Brahman.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Shakta Devi adalah sosok tertinggi; tradisi Smarta memasukkannya dalam lima bentuk utama Brahman.
claims.quote: Devi is the supreme being in the Shakta tradition of Hinduism; in the Smarta tradition, she is one of the five primary forms of Brahman that is revered.

claims.statement: Other traditions emphasise the goddess's active power complementing her divine partner.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi lain menekankan daya aktif dewi yang melengkapi dewa pasangan.
claims.quote: In other Hindu traditions, Devi embodies the active energy and power of Deva, and they always appear together complementing each other.

claims.statement: The Devi Upanishad teaches Shakti as Brahman and the origin of matter and consciousness.
claims.statement_id: Devi Upanishad mengajarkan Shakti sebagai Brahman serta asal materi dan kesadaran.
claims.quote: Devi-inspired philosophy is propounded in many Hindu texts such as the Devi Upanishad, which teaches that Shakti is essentially Brahman (ultimate metaphysical Reality) and that from her arises prakṛti (matter) and purusha (consciousness) and that she is bliss and non-bliss, the Vedas and what is different from it, the born and the unborn and all of the universe.

claims.statement: In the Devi Upanishad, Devi declares herself creator of earth and heaven and infinite consciousness.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Devi Upanishad, Devi menyatakan dirinya pencipta bumi dan langit serta kesadaran tak terbatas.
claims.quote: Devi asserts that she is the creator of earth and heaven and resides there. ... She is, states Devi, the eternal and infinite consciousness engulfing earth and heaven, and 'all forms of bliss and non-bliss, knowledge and ignorance, Brahman and Non-Brahman'.

claims.statement: WHE explains benevolent Uma and fearsome Durga as different depictions of Devi.
claims.statement_id: WHE menjelaskan sisi Uma yang ramah dan sisi Durga yang menakutkan sebagai penggambaran Devi berbeda.
claims.quote: Devi's character has two opposing sides represented by various separate female deities: as Uma, the benevolent, and as Durga, the terrible.

claims.statement: The female speaker in Rigveda 10.125 calls herself Queen and gatherer of treasures worthy of worship.
claims.statement_id: Pembicara perempuan dalam Rigveda 10.125 menyebut dirinya Ratu dan penghimpun harta yang layak dipuja.
claims.quote: I am the Queen, the gatherer-up of treasures, most thoughtful, first of those who merit worship.

claims.statement: According to World History Encyclopedia, Devi, also known as Mahadevi or 'Great Goddess', is an all-embracing Mother Goddess first worshipped in India in Prehistoric times.
claims.statement_id: Menurut World History Encyclopedia, Devi, yang juga dikenal sebagai Mahadevi atau 'Dewi Agung', adalah Dewi Ibu yang merangkul segalanya dan pertama kali dipuja di India pada zaman prasejarah.
claims.quote: Devi, also known as Mahadevi or 'Great Goddess', is an all-embracing Mother Goddess first worshipped in India in Prehistoric times.

claims.statement: In the Vedic period she was assimilated into the Hindu pantheon and came to represent the female energy or Sakti (Power) of her husband Shiva.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa Weda ia diserap ke dalam jajaran dewa Hindu dan mewakili energi perempuan atau Sakti (Daya) suaminya, Shiva.
claims.quote: In the Vedic period, she was assimilated into the Hindu pantheon and so came to represent the female energy or Sakti (Power) of her husband Shiva.

claims.statement: Devi is most often manifested as the fearsome female warriors Durga and Kali, both of whom killed a number of terrible demons in Hindu mythology.
claims.statement_id: Devi paling sering mewujud sebagai pejuang perempuan yang menakutkan, Durga dan Kali, yang keduanya dikenal membunuh sejumlah iblis dalam mitologi Hindu.
claims.quote: Devi is most often manifested as the fearsome female warriors Durga and Kali, both of whom famously killed a number of terrible demons in Hindu mythology.

claims.statement: One of Devi's most famous mythological episodes is her slaying of Mahisa, the demon with a man's body and a buffalo's head, as told in the epic poem the Candipat (or Candi-mahatmya), part of the Skanda Purana.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu kisah mitologis Devi yang paling terkenal adalah pembunuhannya atas Mahisa, iblis bertubuh manusia dan berkepala kerbau, sebagaimana dituturkan dalam puisi epik Candipat (atau Candi-mahatmya), bagian dari Skanda Purana.
claims.quote: One of Devi's most famous mythological escapades is her slaying of Mahisa, the demon who had the body of a man and the head of a buffalo, as told in the epic poem the Candipat (or Candi-mahatmya), which is part of the Skanda Purana.

claims.statement: Devi's more benevolent side is worshipped as Uma, and this facet of her character is represented as both beauty and light.
claims.statement_id: Sisi Devi yang lebih ramah dipuja sebagai Uma, dan segi wataknya ini digambarkan sebagai keindahan sekaligus cahaya.
claims.quote: Devi's more benevolent side is worshipped as Uma, and this facet of her character is represented as both beauty and light.

claims.statement: In Rigveda 10.125 the speaker says she travels with the Rudras and the Vasus and wanders with the Adityas and All-Gods.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Rigveda 10.125, si pembicara berkata bahwa ia bepergian bersama para Rudra dan Vasu serta mengembara bersama para Aditya dan Semua-Dewa.
claims.quote: I TRAVEL with the Rudras and the Vasus, with the Adityas and All-Gods I wander.

claims.statement: In Rigveda 10.125 the speaker says she makes the man she loves exceedingly mighty, a sage, a Rsi, and a Brahman.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Rigveda 10.125, si pembicara berkata bahwa ia membuat orang yang dicintainya sangat perkasa, seorang bijak, seorang Rsi, dan seorang Brahmana.
claims.quote: I make the man I love exceeding mighty, make him a sage, a Rsi, and a Brahman.

claims.statement: In Vedic times gods and goddesses are distinguished, but in post-Vedic texts, particularly early medieval literature, they are ultimately seen as aspects or manifestations of one Devi, the Supreme Power.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa Weda dewa dan dewi dibedakan, tetapi dalam teks pasca-Weda, terutama sastra awal abad pertengahan, semuanya akhirnya dipandang sebagai aspek atau perwujudan satu Devi, Daya Tertinggi.
claims.quote: All gods and goddesses are distinguished in Vedic times, but in post-Vedic texts, particularly in the early medieval era literature, they are ultimately seen as aspects or manifestations of one Devi, the Supreme Power.

claims.statement: Aditi is an important Vedic goddess in Hinduism, with a name meaning boundless or unbound.
claims.statement_id: Aditi adalah dewi Weda penting dalam Hindu, dengan nama yang berarti tak terbatas atau tak terikat.
claims.quote: Aditi  (Sanskrit: अदिति, lit. 'boundless' or 'limitless' or 'innocence')  is an important Vedic goddess in Hinduism.

claims.statement: She personifies the vastness of the cosmos.
claims.statement_id: Ia mempersonifikasikan keluasan kosmos.
claims.quote: She is the personification of the sprawling infinite and vast cosmos.

claims.statement: She is associated with motherhood and fertility.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikaitkan dengan keibuan dan kesuburan.
claims.quote: She is the goddess of motherhood, consciousness, unconsciousness, the past, the future, and fertility.

claims.statement: Aditi is called the mother of the Aditya gods.
claims.statement_id: Aditi disebut ibu kelompok dewa Aditya.
claims.quote: She is the mother of the celestial deities known as the Adityas, and is referred to as the mother of many deities.

claims.statement: The article records her name appearing more than 250 times in the Rigveda.
claims.statement_id: Artikel mencatat namanya disebut lebih dari 250 kali dalam Rigveda.
claims.quote: She is mentioned more than 250 times in the Rigveda, the verses replete with her praise.

claims.statement: A Puranic version describes Aditi as Daksha and Asikni's daughter and Kashyapa's consort.
claims.statement_id: Versi Purana menyebut Aditi putri Daksha dan Asikni serta pasangan Kashyapa.
claims.quote: Aditi is the daughter of Daksha and Asikni (Panchajani). The Puranas, such as the Shiva Purana and the Bhagavata Purana, suggest that Daksha married all of his daughters off to different people, including Aditi and 12 others to sage Kashyapa. When Kashyapa was living with Aditi and Diti in his ashrama, he was really pleased with Aditi's services, and told her to ask for a boon.

claims.statement: In that account Indra is born after Aditi asks for an ideal son.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu Indra lahir setelah Aditi meminta seorang putra ideal.
claims.quote: Aditi prayed for one ideal son. Accordingly, Indra was born.

claims.statement: That Puranic version subsequently gives twelve Adityas as her sons.
claims.statement_id: Versi Purana tersebut kemudian memberi dua belas Aditya sebagai putranya.
claims.quote: Later, Aditi gave birth to the twelve adityas, namely Varuna, Parjanya, Mitra, Amsha, Pushan, Dhatri, Aryaman, Surya, Bhaga, Savitr, Vamana, and Viṣṇu.

claims.statement: The Shatapatha Brahmana also invokes Aditi as earth in sacrifice.
claims.statement_id: Shatapatha Brahmana juga memanggil Aditi sebagai bumi dalam pengorbanan.
claims.quote: According to the Shatapatha Brahmana (a commentary on the Shukla Yajurveda), Aditi is also invoked during ritual sacrificial offerings as being synonymous with the Earth:

claims.statement: She is called Vamana's mother, an incarnation of Vishnu.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut ibu Vamana, penjelmaan Vishnu.
claims.quote: She is also the mother of the Vamana, avatar of Vishnu. Accordingly, the Vamana avatar, as the son of Aditi was born in the month of Shravana (fourth month of the Hindu Calendar, also called Avani) under the star Shravana. Many auspicious signs appeared in the heavens, foretelling the good fortune of this child.

claims.statement: Petitioners invoke Aditi for protection, safety, and abundance.
claims.statement_id: Pemohon memanggil Aditi untuk perlindungan, keselamatan, dan kelimpahan.
claims.quote: In the Rigveda, Aditi is one of the most important figures of all. As a mothering presence, Aditi is often asked to guard the one who petitions her (Mandala 1.106.7; Mandala 8.18.6) or to provide him or her with wealth, safety, and abundance (Mandala 10.100; 1.94.15).

claims.statement: Rigveda 1.89.10 calls Aditi all Gods.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda 1.89.10 menyebut Aditi sebagai semua dewa.
claims.quote: Aditi is all Gods, Aditi five-classed men, Aditi all that hath been born and shall be born.

claims.statement: The hymn also identifies Aditi with all that has been born and shall be born.
claims.statement_id: Himne itu juga menyamakan Aditi dengan segala yang telah lahir dan yang akan lahir.
claims.quote: Aditi is all Gods, Aditi five-classed men, Aditi all that hath been born and shall be born.

claims.statement: The version discussed by Mackenzie gives Aditi eight sons and describes the discarded eighth son later fashioned into Vivasvat.
claims.statement_id: Versi yang dibahas Mackenzie memberi Aditi delapan putra dan menyebut putra kedelapan yang dibuang lalu dibentuk menjadi Vivasvat.
claims.quote:
Aditi, the mother of the Adityas, who is
believed to be of later origin than her children, had eight
sons. She cherished seven of them; the eighth, which
was a shapeless lump, was thrown away, but was afterwards
moulded into Vivasvat, the sun;

claims.statement: Rigveda 1.89.10 identifies Aditi with heaven, mid air, mother, father, and son.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda 1.89.10 mengidentifikasi Aditi dengan langit, ruang antara, ibu, ayah, dan putra.
claims.quote: Aditi is the heaven, Aditi is mid-air, Aditi is the Mother and the Sire and Son.

claims.statement: As celestial mother of numerous beings, the synthesis of all things, she is associated with space (akasha) and with mystic speech (Vac).
claims.statement_id: Sebagai ibu surgawi bagi banyak makhluk, sintesis segala sesuatu, ia dikaitkan dengan ruang (akasha) dan ucapan mistis (Vac).
claims.quote: As celestial mother of numerous beings, the synthesis of all things, she is associated with space (akasha) and with mystic speech (Vāc).

claims.statement: She is portrayed as the mother of the Adityas, a group of societal Rigvedic deities, including Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman, Daksha, Bhaga, Amsha, and sometimes Surya and Savitar.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai ibu para Aditya, kelompok dewa Rigveda yang bersifat kemasyarakatan, termasuk Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman, Daksha, Bhaga, Amsha, dan kadang-kadang Surya dan Savitar.
claims.quote: She is portrayed as the mother of the Adityas, a group of societal Rigvedic deities, including Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman, Daksha, Bhaga, Amsha, and sometimes Surya and Savitar.

claims.statement: Aditi is said to be the mother of the great god Indra, the mother of kings (Mandala 2.27) and the mother of gods (Mandala 1.113.19).
claims.statement_id: Aditi dikatakan sebagai ibu dewa agung Indra, ibu para raja (Mandala 2.27), dan ibu para dewa (Mandala 1.113.19).
claims.quote: Aditi is said to be the mother of the great god Indra, the mother of kings (Mandala 2.27) and the mother of gods (Mandala 1.113.19).

claims.statement: Aditi is usually mentioned in the Rigveda along with other gods and goddesses; no single hymn is addressed exclusively to her, unlike other Vedic gods.
claims.statement_id: Aditi biasanya disebut dalam Rigveda bersama dewa dan dewi lain; tidak ada satu himne pun yang ditujukan khusus kepadanya, tidak seperti dewa Weda lainnya.
claims.quote: Aditi is usually mentioned in the Rigveda along with other gods and goddesses. There is no one hymn addressed exclusively to her, unlike other Vedic gods.

claims.statement: In Rigveda 1.89.3, Aditi is named among the gods called hither with a hymn of olden time: Bhaga, the friendly Daksa, Mitra, Aditi, Aryaman, Varuna, Soma, and the Asvins.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Rigveda 1.89.3, Aditi disebut di antara dewa-dewa yang diundang dengan himne kuno: Bhaga, Daksa yang bersahabat, Mitra, Aditi, Aryaman, Varuna, Soma, dan Asvins.
claims.quote: We call them hither with a hymn of olden time, Bhaga, the friendly Daksa, Mitra, Aditi, Aryaman, Varuna, Soma, the Asvins.

claims.statement: Mackenzie writes that Aditi, mother of the Adityas, is believed to be of more recent origin than her sons.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menulis bahwa Aditi, ibu para Aditya, diyakini berasal dari masa yang lebih baru daripada putra-putranya.
claims.quote: Aditi, mother of the Adityas, is believed to be of more recent origin than her sons.

claims.statement: Aditi and the sage Kashyapa are said to have had 33 sons, twelve of whom are called Adityas including Surya, eleven Rudras, and eight Vasus.
claims.statement_id: Aditi dan resi Kashyapa disebut memiliki 33 putra; dua belas di antaranya disebut Aditya termasuk Surya, sebelas disebut Rudra, dan delapan disebut Vasu.
claims.quote: Aditi and the sage Kashyapa had 33 sons, out of whom twelve are called Ādityas including Surya, eleven are called Rudras, and eight are called Vasus.

claims.statement: Vayu is the Hindu wind god and divine messenger of the gods.
claims.statement_id: Vayu adalah dewa angin Hindu dan utusan ilahi para dewa.
claims.quote: is the Hindu god of the winds as well as the divine messenger of the gods.

claims.statement: His other names include Vata and Pavana.
claims.statement_id: Nama lainnya termasuk Vata dan Pavana.
claims.quote: also known as Vata (Sanskrit: वात, romanised: Vāta, lit. 'Wind/Air') and Pavana (Sanskrit: पवन, romanised: Pávana, lit. 'Purifier')

claims.statement: He is closely associated with Indra in Vedic scriptures.
claims.statement_id: Ia berhubungan erat dengan Indra dalam kitab Weda.
claims.quote: In the Vedic scriptures, Vayu is an important deity and is closely associated with Indra, the king of gods.

claims.statement: He is described as born from Vishvapurusha's breath.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut lahir dari napas Vishvapurusha.
claims.quote: He is mentioned to be born from the breath of Supreme Being Vishvapurusha

claims.statement: Vayu is the first god to receive soma in the ritual; he and Indra then share their first drink.
claims.statement_id: Vayu adalah dewa pertama yang menerima soma dalam ritual, lalu ia dan Indra berbagi tegukan pertama mereka.
claims.quote: Vayu is also the first god to receive soma in the ritual, and then he and Indra share their first drink.

claims.statement: The Upanishads praise him as Prana, the world's life breath.
claims.statement_id: Upanishad memujinya sebagai Prana, napas hidup dunia.
claims.quote: The Upanishads praise him as Prana or 'life breath of the world'.

claims.statement: Later scriptures describe him as guardian of the northwest.
claims.statement_id: Kitab kemudian menyebutnya penjaga arah barat laut.
claims.quote: In the later Hindu scriptures, he is described as a dikpala (one of the guardians of the direction), who looks over the north-west direction.

claims.statement: The epics describe him as Hanuman and Bhima's father.
claims.statement_id: Wiracarita menyebutnya ayah Hanuman dan Bhima.
claims.quote: The Hindu epics describe him as the father of the god Hanuman and Bhima.

claims.statement: Vayu is explained as blower and Prana as the breath of life.
claims.statement_id: Vayu dijelaskan sebagai peniup dan Prana sebagai napas kehidupan.
claims.quote: The word for air (vāyu) or wind (pavana) is one of the classical elements in Hinduism. The Sanskrit word Vāta literally means 'blown'; Vāyu, 'blower' and Prāna, 'breathing' (viz. the breath of life, cf. the *an- in animate).

claims.statement: The Rigveda connects him with a shining chariot drawn by horses.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda menghubungkannya dengan kereta bercahaya yang ditarik kuda.
claims.quote: In the hymns, Vayu is 'described as having "exceptional beauty" and moving noisily in his shining coach, driven by two or forty-nine or one-thousand white and purple horses.

claims.statement: As a member of the eight Vasus he is also called Anila.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai anggota delapan Vasu ia juga disebut Anila.
claims.quote: Vayu is also one of the Vasus, a group of eight deities mentioned in Ramayana, Mahabharata and Vedas. Within this categorisation, Vayu is also known as Anila.

claims.statement: In Japanese Buddhism he belongs to the Twelve Devas guarding directions.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Buddhisme Jepang ia termasuk Dua Belas Dewa penjaga arah.
claims.quote: In Japanese Buddhism, especially Mikkyō traditions such as Shingon, he is usually classified as one of the Twelve Devas (Japanese: 十二天, romanised: Jūniten) grouped together as directional guardians. He presides over the northwest direction.

claims.statement: His Japanese name is Futen.
claims.statement_id: Nama Jepangnya adalah Futen.
claims.quote: In Japan, he is called Fūten (風天). He is included with the other eleven devas, which include Taishakuten (Śakra/Indra), Katen (Agni), Enmaten (Yama), Rasetsuten (Nirṛti/Rākṣasa), Ishanaten (Īśāna), Bishamonten (Vaiśravaṇa/Kubera), Suiten (Varuṇa), Bonten (Brahmā), Jiten (Pṛthivī), Nitten (Sūrya/Āditya) and Gatten (Candra).

claims.statement: Mackenzie quotes a hymn connecting Vayu with two red horses on a chariot and a team of deer.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie mengutip himne yang menghubungkan Vayu dengan dua kuda merah pada kereta serta kawanan rusa.
claims.quote:
The Indian Vata is invoked, as Vayu, in a beautiful
passage in one of the hymns which refers to his “two
red horses yoked to the chariot”: he had also, like the
Maruts, a team of deer. The poet calls to the wind:

claims.statement: Rigveda 1.2 calls Vayu to drink the prepared Soma and hear the prayer.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda 1.2 memanggil Vayu untuk minum Soma yang dipersiapkan dan mendengar doa.
claims.quote:
BEAUTIFUL Vayu, come, for thee these Soma drops have been prepared:
     Drink of them, hearken to our call.

claims.statement: In the Rigveda, Vayu is associated with the winds, and the Maruts are described as born from Vayu's belly.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Rigveda, Vayu dikaitkan dengan angin, dan para Marut digambarkan lahir dari perut Vayu.
claims.quote: In the Rigveda, Vayu is associated with the winds, with the Maruts being described as being born from Vayu's belly.

claims.statement: In the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad the gods who control bodily functions once contest which of them is greatest, and the other deities come to realise that they can function only when empowered by Vayu and can easily be overpowered by him.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Brihadaranyaka Upanishad, para dewa yang mengatur fungsi tubuh pernah berlomba untuk menentukan siapa yang terbesar; hasilnya para dewa menyadari bahwa mereka hanya dapat berfungsi bila diberdayakan oleh Vayu dan dapat dengan mudah ditaklukkan olehnya.
claims.quote: The Brihadaranyaka Upanishad says that the gods who control bodily functions once engaged in a contest to determine who among them is the greatest. ... This caused the other deities to realise that they can function only when empowered by Vayu, and can be overpowered by him easily.

claims.statement: The Chandogya Upanishad says that one cannot know Brahman except by knowing Vayu as the udgitha (the mantric syllable om).
claims.statement_id: Chandogya Upanishad menyatakan bahwa orang tidak dapat mengenal Brahman kecuali dengan mengenal Vayu sebagai udgitha (suku kata mantra om).
claims.quote: The Chandogya Upanishad says that one cannot know Brahman except by knowing Vayu as the udgitha (the mantric syllable om).

claims.statement: In the Mahabharata, Bhima was the spiritual son of Vayu and played a major role in the Kurukshetra War.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Mahabharata, Bhima adalah putra spiritual Vayu dan berperan besar dalam Perang Kurukshetra.
claims.quote: In the Mahabharata, Bhima was the spiritual son of Vayu and played a major role in the Kurukshetra War.

claims.statement: Mackenzie writes that Indra absorbed, and was absorbed by, the wind god Vayu or Vata, who is also called the father of the Maruts and the son-in-law of the artisan god Twashtri.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menulis bahwa Indra menyerap dan diserap oleh dewa angin Vayu atau Vata, yang juga disebut ayah para Marut dan menantu dewa pengrajin Twashtri.
claims.quote: Indra similarly absorbed, and was absorbed by, the wind god Vayu or Vata, who is also referred to as the father of the Maruts and the son-in-law of the artisan god Twashtri.

claims.statement: In Mackenzie's retelling about Purusha, Indra and Agni came from his mouth and Vayu from his breath.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penuturan Mackenzie tentang Purusha, Indra dan Agni muncul dari mulutnya, sedangkan Vayu dari napasnya.
claims.quote: The Brahman rose from Purusha's mouth, the Rajanya (Kshatriya) from his arms, the Vaisya from his thighs, and the Sudra sprang from his feet. Indra and Agni came from his mouth, and Vayu from his breath.

claims.statement: In Mackenzie's retelling, a serpent noose binds two brothers so that they cannot move; Vayu, god of wind, sends the Celestial bird Garuda, the serpent killer, to their aid and the snakes forming the noose flee.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penuturan Mackenzie, jerat ular mengikat dua bersaudara sehingga tak dapat bergerak; Vayu, dewa angin, mengirim burung surgawi Garuda, pembunuh ular, untuk menolong mereka, dan ular-ular pembentuk jerat itu lari.
claims.quote: Then he threw a serpent noose, which bound the two brothers so that they were unable to move. Great was their peril, but Vayu, god of wind, sent to their aid the great Celestial bird Garuda, the serpent killer, and the snakes which formed the noose fled from before it

claims.statement: Rigveda 1.2.3 says that Vayu's penetrating stream goes forth to the worshipper, spreading far for the Soma draught.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda 1.2.3 berkata bahwa aliran Vayu yang menembus mengalir menuju pemuja, menyebar jauh untuk minuman Soma.
claims.quote: Vayu, thy penetrating stream goes forth unto the worshipper, Far-spreading for the Soma draught.

claims.statement: Rigveda 1.2.4 addresses Indra and Vayu together and invites both to come for the offerings.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda 1.2.4 menyapa Indra dan Vayu bersama dan mengundang keduanya datang demi persembahan.
claims.quote: These, Indra-Vayu, have been shed; come for our offered dainties' sake: The drops are yearning for you both.

claims.statement: Sati is the Hindu goddess of marital felicity and longevity and an aspect of Shakti.
claims.statement_id: Sati adalah dewi Hindu kebahagiaan perkawinan dan umur panjang, serta aspek Shakti.
claims.quote: is the Hindu goddess of marital felicity and longevity, and is worshipped as an aspect of the mother goddess Shakti.

claims.statement: She is Shiva's first wife; Parvati is regarded as her reincarnation.
claims.statement_id: Ia merupakan istri pertama Shiva; Parvati dipandang sebagai kelahirannya kembali.
claims.quote: Sati was the first wife of Shiva, the other being Parvati, who was Sati's reincarnation after her death.

claims.statement: In legend she marries Shiva against her father Daksha's wishes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda, ia menikahi Shiva bertentangan dengan keinginan ayahnya, Daksha.
claims.quote: Legends describe Sati as the favourite child of Daksha, who marries Shiva against her father's wishes.

claims.statement: Sati's body parts falling to earth are associated with sacred Shakti pithas.
claims.statement_id: Bagian tubuh Sati yang jatuh ke bumi dikaitkan dengan tempat suci Shakti pitha.
claims.quote: his Sudarshana Chakra which divided Sati's body parts falling on the ground at 51 different places. These places are now known as Shakti pithas, and they are sacred to Hindus.

claims.statement: The name Sati is explained as truthful, virtuous, or noble in Sanskrit.
claims.statement_id: Nama Sati dijelaskan berarti benar, berbudi, atau mulia dalam bahasa Sanskerta.
claims.quote: The name "Satī" means "truthful", "virtuous" or "noble" in Sanskrit. The word is derived from the "sat" which means "truth".

claims.statement: Mackenzie recounts Sati entering the sacrificial fire after her father slighted her husband.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menuturkan Sati terjun ke api pengorbanan setelah ayahnya menghina suaminya.
claims.quote:
As Sati, Shiva's wife is the ideal of a true and virtuous
Hindu woman. When Sati's husband was slighted by
her father, the Deva-rishi, Daksha, she cast herself on
the sacrificial fire. Widows who died on the funeral
pyres of their husbands were called Sati[184], because in performing
this rite they imitated the faithful goddess.

claims.statement: Yakshas are a class of nature spirits in Hindu mythology associated with water, trees, forests, treasure, and fertility.
claims.statement_id: Yaksha merupakan kelompok roh alam dalam mitologi Hindu yang berkaitan dengan air, pepohonan, hutan, harta, dan kesuburan.
claims.quote: are a broad class of nature spirits in Hindu mythology which are associated with water, trees, forests, wilderness, treasure, and fertility.

claims.statement: The female form is called yakshi or yakshini.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk perempuan disebut yakshi atau yakshini.
claims.quote: The feminine form of the word is IAST: Yakṣī or Yakshini

claims.statement: A yaksha may be a harmless nature spirit or a ghost that waylays and devours travellers.
claims.statement_id: Versi yaksha dapat berupa roh alam yang tidak berbahaya atau hantu yang menghadang dan memangsa pelancong.
claims.quote: In Hindu, Jain and Buddhist texts, the yakṣas have a dual personality. A yakṣa may be an inoffensive nature spirit associated with woods and mountains, or a darker version of the yakṣa which is a kind of Bhoota (ghost) that haunts the wilderness and waylays and devours travellers, similar to the rakṣasas.

claims.statement: Kubera is regarded as king of yakshas in Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism.
claims.statement_id: Kubera dipandang sebagai raja para yaksha dalam Hindu, Buddha, dan Jain.
claims.quote: In Hindu, Buddhist and Jain Religion, Kubera, the god of wealth and prosperity, is considered the king of the yakshas and protector of the world (Lokapāla). In Buddhism, he is equated with Vaiśravaṇa.

claims.statement: In Buddhist literature yakshas attend Vaisravana, guardian of the northern quarter.
claims.statement_id: Dalam literatur Buddhis, yaksha menjadi pengiring Vaisravana, penjaga arah utara.
claims.quote: In Buddhist literature, the yakṣa are the attendants of Vaiśravaṇa, the guardian of the northern quarter, a beneficent god who protects the righteous. The term also refers to the Twelve Heavenly Generals who guard Bhaiṣajyaguru, the Medicine Buddha. The yakshas of many Buddhist stories are ugly ogres, reborn in that form because of sins committed during their past lives as humans.

claims.statement: Mackenzie calls yakshas guardians of hidden treasure associated with Kuvera.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menyebut yaksha sebagai penjaga harta tersembunyi yang berkaitan dengan Kuvera.
claims.quote:
They are guardians of hidden
treasure, like the dwarfs and giants of Teutonic legend,
being associated with Kuvera, god of wealth, whose abode
is situated among the Himalayan mountains.

claims.statement: Kamadeva is the Hindu god of love, attraction, pleasure, and beauty.
claims.statement_id: Kamadeva adalah dewa Hindu cinta, ketertarikan, kesenangan, dan keindahan.
claims.quote: is the Hindu god of love, attraction, pleasure and beauty, as well as the personification of the concept of kāma.

claims.statement: He is depicted as a young man with a sugarcane bow and flower arrows.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai pemuda dengan busur tebu dan panah bunga.
claims.quote: He is depicted as a handsome young man decked with ornaments and flowers, armed with a bow of sugarcane and shooting arrows of flowers.

claims.statement: His consort is Rati.
claims.statement_id: Pasangannya adalah Rati.
claims.quote: He is often portrayed alongside his consort and female counterpart, Rati.

claims.statement: Puranic accounts generally call him Brahma's mind born son.
claims.statement_id: Versi Purana umumnya menyebutnya putra Brahma yang lahir dari pikiran.
claims.quote: In the Puranas, Kamadeva is generally mentioned as a manasaputra (mind-born son) of the creator god Brahma.

claims.statement: His story includes incineration by Shiva's third eye and rebirth as Pradyumna.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya mencakup pembakaran oleh mata ketiga Shiva dan kelahiran kembali sebagai Pradyumna.
claims.quote: His most popular myth is his incineration by the god Shiva's third eye and rebirth on earth as Pradyumna, the eldest son of Krishna and his chief consort Rukmini.

claims.statement: Mackenzie's version calls Kamadeva the son of Vishnu and Lakshmi.
claims.statement_id: Versi Mackenzie menyebut Kamadeva sebagai putra Vishnu dan Lakshmi.
claims.quote: This god is the son of Vishnu and Lakshmi.

claims.statement: Kamadeva is also known as Kama, Manmatha, and Madana.
claims.statement_id: Kamadeva juga dikenal sebagai Kama, Manmatha, dan Madana.
claims.quote: also known as Kama, Manmatha, and Madana

claims.statement: Kamadeva's origins are traced to the verses of the Rig Veda and Atharva Veda, although he is better known from the stories of the Puranas.
claims.statement_id: Asal-usul Kamadeva ditelusuri hingga ayat-ayat Rig Veda dan Atharva Veda, meskipun ia lebih dikenal dari kisah-kisah Purana.
claims.quote: Kamadeva's origins are traced to the verses of the Rig Veda and Atharva Veda, although he is better known from the stories of the Puranas.

claims.statement: The Shiva Purana describes Kamadeva being resurrected by Shiva on the occasion of his marriage to Parvati.
claims.statement_id: Shiva Purana menggambarkan Kamadeva dihidupkan kembali oleh Shiva pada peristiwa pernikahannya dengan Parvati.
claims.quote: Shiva Purana describes Kamadeva being resurrected by Shiva on the event of his marriage to Parvati.

claims.statement: Mackenzie writes that after Sati burned herself, the sorrowing Shiva was wounded by Kamadeva, the love god, whom he slew by sending a flame of fire from his third eye.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menulis bahwa setelah Sati membakar dirinya, Shiva yang berduka dilukai oleh Kamadeva, dewa cinta, yang kemudian dibunuhnya dengan memancarkan nyala api dari mata ketiganya.
claims.quote: It was after Sati burned herself that the sorrowing Shiva was wounded by Kamadeva, the love god, whom he slew by causing a flame of fire to dart from his third eye.

claims.statement: Mackenzie lists several epithets and glosses them: Manmatha, the "mind-disturber"; Mara, "the wounder"; Madan, "he who makes one love-drunk"; and Pradyumna, the "all-conqueror".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Mackenzie, sebagai Manmatha ia adalah "pengganggu pikiran", sebagai Mara "sang pelukai", sebagai Madan "yang membuat orang mabuk cinta", dan sebagai Pradyumna "sang penakluk segalanya".
claims.quote: As Manmatha he is the “mind-disturber”; as Mara, “the wounder”; as Madan, “he who makes one love-drunk”; and as Pradyumna he is the “all-conqueror”.

claims.statement: Kubera is the Hindu god of wealth and king of yakshas.
claims.statement_id: Kubera adalah dewa kekayaan dan raja yaksha dalam Hindu.
claims.quote: is the god of wealth, and the god-king of the semi-divine yakshas in Hinduism.

claims.statement: He is regent of the north and protector of the world.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi penjaga arah utara dan pelindung dunia.
claims.quote: He is regarded as the regent of the north (Dikpala), and a protector of the world (Lokapala).

claims.statement: Common depictions show a plump body, jewels, money pot, and club.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran umum memperlihatkan tubuh gemuk, perhiasan, wadah uang, dan gada.
claims.quote: Kubera is often depicted with a plump body, adorned with jewels, and carrying a money-pot and a club.

claims.statement: In scriptural narratives Ravana overthrows him from Lanka before he settles in Alaka in the Himalayas.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah kitab, Ravana menggulingkannya dari Lanka sebelum ia menetap di Alaka di Himalaya.
claims.quote: Originally described as the chief of evil spirits in Vedic-era texts, Kubera acquired the status of a deva (god) only in the Puranas and the Hindu epics. The scriptures describe that Kubera once ruled Lanka, but was overthrown by his half-brother Ravana, later settling in the city of Alaka in the Himalayas.

claims.statement: His Buddhist name is Vaisravana; in Indonesia he is also known as Daneswara.
claims.statement_id: Nama Buddhisnya Vaisravana; di Indonesia ia juga dikenal sebagai Daneswara.
claims.quote: In Buddhism, he is known as Vaisravana, the patronymic used of the Hindu Kubera and is also equated with Pañcika, while in Jainism, he is known as Sarvanubhuti. In Indonesia, Kubera is also known as Daneswara.

claims.statement: Mackenzie places Kuvera's dwelling in the Himalayas and associates him with treasure guarding yakshas.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menempatkan kediaman Kuvera di Himalaya dan mengaitkannya dengan yaksha penjaga harta.
claims.quote:
They are guardians of hidden
treasure, like the dwarfs and giants of Teutonic legend,
being associated with Kuvera, god of wealth, whose abode
is situated among the Himalayan mountains.
