claims.statement: Chandra is the Hindu Moon god associated with night and plants.
claims.statement_id: Chandra adalah dewa Bulan dalam Hindu yang terkait malam dan tumbuhan.
claims.quote: Chandra (Sanskrit: चन्द्र, romanized: Chandra, lit. 'shining' or 'moon'), also known as Soma (Sanskrit: सोम), is the Hindu god of the Moon, and is associated with the night, plants and vegetation. He is one of the Navagraha (nine planets of Hinduism).

claims.statement: He belongs to the Navagraha, nine planets in Hindu tradition.
claims.statement_id: Ia termasuk Navagraha, sembilan planet dalam tradisi Hindu.
claims.quote: Chandra (Sanskrit: चन्द्र, romanized: Chandra, lit. 'shining' or 'moon'), also known as Soma (Sanskrit: सोम), is the Hindu god of the Moon, and is associated with the night, plants and vegetation. He is one of the Navagraha (nine planets of Hinduism).

claims.statement: Chandra means bright or shining in Sanskrit.
claims.statement_id: Chandra berarti terang atau berkilau dalam bahasa Sanskerta.
claims.quote: The word "Chandra" literally means "bright, shining or glittering" and is used for the "Moon" in Sanskrit and other Indo-Aryan languages. It is also the name of various other figures in Hindu mythology, including an asura and a Suryavamsha king. It is also a common Indian name and surname.

claims.statement: His epithets include Shashank, meaning hare marked.
claims.statement_id: Epitetnya mencakup Shashank, yang berarti bertanda kelinci.
claims.quote: Some of the epithets of Chandra include Soma (distill), Indu (bright drop), Shashank (hare-marked), Atrisuta (son of Atri), Shashin or Shachin (the essence), Taradhipa (lord of stars), Nishakara (the night maker), Nakshatrapati (lord of the Nakshatra), Oshadhipati (lord of herbs), Uduraj or Udupati (water lord), Kumudanatha (lord of lotuses), and Udupa (boat).

claims.statement: The time when Soma became a name of the Moon is debated by scholars.
claims.statement_id: Waktu pemakaian Soma sebagai nama Bulan diperdebatkan oleh para sarjana.
claims.quote: Soma is one of the most common other names used for the deity; but the earliest use of the word to refer to the Moon is a subject of scholarly debate. Some scholars state that the word Soma is occasionally used for the Moon in the Vedas, while other scholars suggest that such usage emerged only in the post-Vedic literature.

claims.statement: Mackenzie identifies the Moon god Chandra with Soma.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie mengidentifikasi dewa Bulan Chandra dengan Soma.
claims.quote:
The moon is the god Chandra, who became identified
with Soma.

claims.statement: Chandra is traditionally married to the 27 daughters of the sage Daksha, who personify the 27 Nakshatras.
claims.statement_id: Chandra secara tradisional menikahi 27 putri resi Daksha, yang mempersonifikasikan 27 Nakshatra (rumah bulan).
claims.quote: Chandra is traditionally married to the 27 daughters of the sage Daksha, who personify the 27 Nakshatras (lunar mansions).

claims.statement: In anger Daksha cursed Chandra to suffer from Kshayaroga (consumption); the affliction struck not only Chandra but also the medicinal plants and other living beings dependent on lunar influence.
claims.statement_id: Karena murka, Daksha mengutuk Chandra menderita Kshayaroga (penyakit susut); penderitaan itu tidak hanya menimpa Chandra tetapi juga tanaman obat dan makhluk hidup lain yang bergantung pada pengaruh bulan.
claims.quote: Despite being married to all 27, Chandra showed special affection for Rohini, causing jealousy among his other wives. ... In anger, Daksha cursed Chandra to suffer from Kshayaroga (consumption or tuberculosis). This affliction impacted not just Chandra but also affected the medicinal plants and other living beings dependent on lunar influence.

claims.statement: His most common iconography is a white deity holding a mace, riding a three-wheeled chariot drawn by three or more white horses (up to ten).
claims.statement_id: Ikonografinya yang paling umum: dewa berwarna putih yang memegang gada dan mengendarai kereta beroda tiga yang ditarik tiga atau lebih kuda putih (sampai sepuluh).
claims.quote: The most common is one where he is a white-coloured deity, holding a mace in his hand, riding a chariot with three wheels and three or more white horses (up to ten).

claims.statement: Ganga personifies the Ganges and is worshipped as goddess of purification and forgiveness.
claims.statement_id: Ganga adalah personifikasi Sungai Gangga yang dipuja sebagai dewi pemurnian dan pengampunan.
claims.quote: Ganga (Sanskrit: गङ्गा, IAST: Gaṅgā) is the personification of the river Ganges, who is worshipped by Hindus as the goddess of purification and forgiveness.

claims.statement: She is commonly depicted riding a makara, a divine crocodile like creature.
claims.statement_id: Ia lazim digambarkan mengendarai makara, makhluk ilahi yang menyerupai buaya.
claims.quote: She is often depicted as a fair, beautiful ornate woman, riding a divine crocodile-like creature called the makara.

claims.statement: Some scriptures call her Himavat's daughter and Parvati's elder sister, while other versions connect her origin to Vishnu's feet.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian kitab menyebutnya putri Himavat dan kakak Parvati, sedangkan versi lain mengaitkan asalnya dengan kaki Vishnu.
claims.quote: In Hindu mythology, Ganga is generally described as originating from the feet of the preserver deity Vishnu. However, according to some scriptures, including the Ramayana, she is the firstborn daughter of Himavat (the personification of the Himalayas) and the elder sister of the goddess Parvati.

claims.statement: Her descent narrative recounts Shiva breaking her fall with his hair.
claims.statement_id: Kisah turunnya ke bumi menuturkan Shiva menahan jatuhnya dengan rambutnya.
claims.quote: This descent was facilitated by the god Shiva, who caught Ganga in his matted hair to break her fall and later released her gently onto the earth.

claims.statement: Hindu pilgrims immerse relatives' ashes in the Ganges in the belief in purification toward moksha.
claims.statement_id: Peziarah Hindu menenggelamkan abu keluarga di Gangga dalam keyakinan pemurnian menuju moksha.
claims.quote: Pilgrims immerse the ashes of their kin in the river Ganga, which is considered by them to bring the souls (purified spirits) closer to moksha, the liberation from the cycle of life and death.

claims.statement: In Mackenzie's retelling, Ganga becomes Shantanu's wife and promises human birth for eight cursed Vasus.
claims.statement_id: Dalam retelling Mackenzie, Ganga menjadi istri Shantanu dan menjanjikan kelahiran manusia bagi delapan Vasu yang terkena kutukan.
claims.quote:
His first wife was the goddess
Ganga of the Ganges river, and she was divinely
beautiful like to her kind. ... So they hastened to Ganga, and
she consented to become their human mother, promising
that she would cast them one by one into the Ganges
soon after birth, so that they might return speedily to
their celestial state.

claims.statement: Her most famous story is her descent to Earth, granted as a boon to the royal sage Bhagiratha so that she could purify the souls of his ancestors.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya yang paling terkenal adalah turunnya ke bumi, yang dianugerahkan sebagai anugerah kepada resi kerajaan Bhagiratha agar ia dapat menyucikan roh leluhurnya.
claims.quote: Her most famous story is her descent to Earth, which was granted as a boon to the royal sage Bhagiratha so that she could purify the souls of his ancestors.

claims.statement: In the Mahabharata, Ganga is also portrayed as the mother of the warrior Bhishma through her union with the Kuru king Shantanu.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Mahabharata, Ganga juga digambarkan sebagai ibu prajurit Bhishma melalui persatuannya dengan raja Kuru, Shantanu.
claims.quote: In the Mahabharata, Ganga is also portrayed as the mother of the warrior Bhishma through her union with the Kuru king Shantanu.

claims.statement: Ganga is represented as a fair-complexioned woman wearing a white crown and sitting on a crocodile, holding a water lily in her right hand and a flute in her left.
claims.statement_id: Ganga digambarkan sebagai perempuan berkulit cerah yang bermahkota putih dan duduk di atas buaya; tangan kanannya memegang teratai air dan tangan kirinya seruling.
claims.quote: Ganga is represented as a fair-complexioned woman, wearing a white crown and sitting on a crocodile. She holds a water lily in her right hand and a flute in her left.

claims.statement: Because of Bhagiratha's efforts the river is also known as Bhagirathi, and she is also known as Tripathaga because she flows in the three worlds: heaven, earth, and the netherworld.
claims.statement_id: Karena upaya Bhagiratha, sungai itu juga dikenal sebagai Bhagirathi; ia juga dikenal sebagai Tripathaga karena mengalir di tiga dunia: surga, bumi, dan dunia bawah.
claims.quote: Because of Bhagiratha's efforts, the river is also known as Bhagirathi. She is also known as Tripathaga because she flows in the three worlds, heaven, earth, and the netherworld.

claims.statement: In Mackenzie's retelling, as King Shantanu walks beside the Ganges, Ganga appears before him in human form as a maiden of surpassing beauty, her celestial garments splendid as lotus blooms, adorned with rare ornaments, her teeth radiant as pearls.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penuturan Mackenzie, ketika Raja Shantanu berjalan di tepi sungai Gangga, Ganga muncul di hadapannya dalam rupa manusia sebagai gadis berkecantikan luar biasa, berpakaian surgawi yang bersinar seperti bunga teratai, berhias perhiasan langka, dengan gigi secemerlang mutiara.
claims.quote: A day came thereafter when King Shantanu walked beside the Ganges. Suddenly there appeared before him a maiden of surpassing beauty. She was Ganga in human form. Her celestial garments had the splendour of lotus blooms; she was adorned with rare ornaments, and her teeth were radiant as pearls.

claims.statement: Balarama is a Hindu deity and Krishna's elder brother.
claims.statement_id: Balarama adalah dewa Hindu dan kakak Krishna.
claims.quote: Balarama (Sanskrit: बलराम, IAST: Balarāma) is a Hindu god, and the elder brother of Krishna. He is particularly significant in the Jagannath tradition, as one of the triad deities. He is also known as Haladhara, Halayudha, Baladeva, Balabhadra, and Sankarshana.

claims.statement: He is important as one of the three deities in the Jagannath tradition.
claims.statement_id: Ia penting sebagai salah satu tiga dewa dalam tradisi Jagannath.
claims.quote: Balarama (Sanskrit: बलराम, IAST: Balarāma) is a Hindu god, and the elder brother of Krishna. He is particularly significant in the Jagannath tradition, as one of the triad deities. He is also known as Haladhara, Halayudha, Baladeva, Balabhadra, and Sankarshana.

claims.statement: His other names include Baladeva, Balabhadra, and Sankarshana.
claims.statement_id: Nama lainnya mencakup Baladeva, Balabhadra, dan Sankarshana.
claims.quote: Balarama (Sanskrit: बलराम, IAST: Balarāma) is a Hindu god, and the elder brother of Krishna. He is particularly significant in the Jagannath tradition, as one of the triad deities. He is also known as Haladhara, Halayudha, Baladeva, Balabhadra, and Sankarshana.

claims.statement: The epithets Haladhara and Halayudha connect him with the plough and farming.
claims.statement_id: Epitet Haladhara dan Halayudha berhubungan dengan bajak dan pertanian.
claims.quote: The first two epithets associate him with hala (langala, "plough") from his strong associations with farming and farmers, as the deity who used farm equipment as weapons when needed, and the next two refer to his strength.

claims.statement: He is usually regarded as an incarnation of Shesha, but some traditions count him as an avatar of Vishnu.
claims.statement_id: Ia biasanya dipandang sebagai inkarnasi Shesha, tetapi sebagian tradisi menempatkannya sebagai avatar Vishnu.
claims.quote: Originally an agricultural deity, Balarama is mostly described as an incarnation of Shesha, the serpent associated with the deity Vishnu while some Vaishnava traditions regard him as the eighth avatar of Vishnu, with Jayadeva’s Gita Govinda (c.1200) "incorporat[ing] Balarama into the pantheon" as the ninth of the 10 principal avatars of Vishnu.

claims.statement: Mackenzie describes Balarama as an incarnation of the world serpent Shesha.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menjelaskan Balarama sebagai inkarnasi ular dunia Shesha.
claims.quote:
Balarama is an incarnation of the world serpent
Shesha.

claims.statement: Balarama killed Dhenuka, an asura sent by Kamsa, and the wrestlers Pralamba and Mushtika sent by the king; while Krishna killed Kamsa, Balarama slew his mighty commander Kalavakra.
claims.statement_id: Balarama membunuh Dhenuka, asura kiriman Kamsa, serta pegulat Pralamba dan Mushtika yang dikirim raja itu; ketika Krishna membunuh Kamsa, Balarama menewaskan panglima perkasanya, Kalavakra.
claims.quote: He killed Dhenuka, an asura sent by Kamsa, as well as Pralamba and Mushtika wrestlers sent by the king. When Krishna was killing Kamsa, Balarama slew his mighty commander, Kalavakra.

claims.statement: The plough is Balarama's weapon; in the Bhagavata Purana he uses it to fight asuras, to dig a channel bringing the Yamuna closer to Vrindavan, and to drag the whole capital of Hastinapura into the Ganga.
claims.statement_id: Bajak adalah senjata Balarama; dalam Bhagavata Purana ia memakainya untuk melawan asura, menggali jalan bagi Sungai Yamuna agar lebih dekat ke Vrindavan, dan menyeret seluruh ibu kota Hastinapura ke Sungai Gangga.
claims.quote: The plough is Balarama's weapon. In the Bhagavata Purana, he uses it to fight asuras, dig a way for Yamuna river to bring it closer to Vrindavan, and he also availed it to drag the entire capital of Hastinapura into the Ganga river.

claims.statement: Balarama taught both Duryodhana of the Kauravas and Bhima of the Pandavas the art of mace warfare; when war broke out he had obligations to both sides and stayed neutral.
claims.statement_id: Balarama mengajari Duryodhana dari pihak Kaurava dan Bhima dari pihak Pandawa seni perang dengan gada; ketika perang pecah ia terikat pada kedua pihak dan tetap netral.
claims.quote: Balarama taught both Duryodhana of the Kauravas and Bhima of the Pandavas the art of war with a mace. When war broke between the Kauravas and the Pandavas, Balarama carried obligations for both sides and so remained neutral.

claims.statement: Rudra is a Rigvedic deity associated with Shiva, wind or storms, medicine, and wildlife.
claims.statement_id: Rudra adalah dewa Rigveda yang dikaitkan dengan Shiva, angin atau badai, pengobatan, dan satwa liar.
claims.quote: is a Rigvedic deity associated with Shiva, the wind or storms, Vayu, medicine, and wildlife.

claims.statement: The Shri Rudram hymn in the Yajurveda is dedicated to him.
claims.statement_id: Himne Shri Rudram dalam Yajurveda dipersembahkan kepadanya.
claims.quote: The "Shri Rudram" hymn from the Yajurveda is dedicated to Rudra and is important in the Shaivite sect.

claims.statement: Rudra's etymology is uncertain; explanations include the roarer and the red or shining one.
claims.statement_id: Etimologi Rudra tidak pasti; penjelasan mencakup sang pengaum dan yang merah atau bersinar.
claims.quote: The etymology of the theonym Rudra is uncertain. It is usually derived from the Proto-Indo-European (PIE) root rud- (related to English rude), which means 'to cry, howl'. The name Rudra may thus be translated as 'the roarer'.

claims.statement: The word shiva meaning kind or propitious is applied to Rudra in Rigveda 10.92.9.
claims.statement_id: Kata shiva yang bermakna baik atau menguntungkan digunakan untuk Rudra dalam Rigveda 10.92.9.
claims.quote: The adjective śiva (shiva) in the sense of 'propitious' or 'kind' is first applied to the Rudra in RV 10.92.9.

claims.statement: The name Sharva and the arrow attribute connect with his depiction as archer.
claims.statement_id: Nama Sharva dan atribut panah berkaitan dengan penggambarannya sebagai pemanah.
claims.quote: Rudra is called 'the archer' (Sanskrit: Śarva) and the arrow is an essential attribute of Rudra.

claims.statement: Mackenzie describes Rudra as a wind or storm god and father of the Maruts.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menjelaskan Rudra sebagai dewa angin atau badai dan ayah para Marut.
claims.quote:
Another wind or storm god is Rudra, also the father
of the Maruts, who are called “Rudras”.

claims.statement: Karna is a major character in the Hindu epic Mahabharata and son of Surya and Kunti.
claims.statement_id: Karna adalah tokoh utama wiracarita Hindu Mahabharata dan putra Surya serta Kunti.
claims.quote: is one of the major characters in the Hindu epic Mahābhārata. He is the son of Surya (the solar deity) and princess Kunti (later the Pandava mother).

claims.statement: Radha and Adhiratha find and foster him after he is abandoned in a basket on the Ganges.
claims.statement_id: Radha dan Adhiratha menemukan dan membesarkannya setelah ia ditinggalkan dalam keranjang di Gangga.
claims.quote: she is forced to abandon the infant in a basket on the Ganges. He is discovered and fostered by Radha and Adhiratha Nandana, the sūta (charioteer) of King Dhritarashtra.

claims.statement: He becomes Duryodhana's friend and is appointed king of Anga.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi sahabat Duryodhana dan diangkat sebagai raja Anga.
claims.quote: He becomes a loyal friend of Duryodhana, and is appointed the king of Anga (Bihar-Bengal) by the prince.

claims.statement: He fights on the Kaurava side and is ultimately killed by Arjuna.
claims.statement_id: Ia berperang di pihak Kaurava dan akhirnya dibunuh Arjuna.
claims.quote: Karna joins the Kaurava side of the Kurukshetra War, and is ultimately slain by Arjuna.

claims.statement: According to David Slavitt's explanation, his childhood name is Vasusena and the name Karna is linked to Surya's golden earrings.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penjelasan David Slavitt, nama masa kecilnya Vasusena dan nama Karna dikaitkan dengan anting emas Surya.
claims.quote: In the Mahabharata and the Puranas, it is the name of a warrior character. Called Vasusena as a child by his foster parents, he became known by the name Karna because of the golden earrings of Surya he used to wear, according to the Sanskrit epics scholar David Slavitt.

claims.statement: Mackenzie recounts Pritha and the sun god's son being concealed in a basket floated on a river.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menceritakan putra Pritha dan dewa matahari disembunyikan dalam keranjang yang dihanyutkan di sungai.
claims.quote:
In Mahabharata there is a fragment of an old legend
which relates the origin of Karna, the son of Queen
Pritha and the sun god: the birth of the child is concealed,
and he is placed in a basket which is set afloat on
the river and is carried to a distant country.[72]

claims.statement: Mara in Siddhartha's awakening story appears as a powerful deity trying to obstruct his awakening.
claims.statement_id: Mara dalam kisah pencerahan Siddhartha tampil sebagai dewa kuat yang berupaya menggagalkan pencerahannya.
claims.quote: In the story of the Awakening of Prince Siddhartha Māra appears as a powerful deva, trying to seduce him with his celestial army and a vision of beautiful maidens (accharā) who, in various legends, are often said to be Mara's daughters. In other iterations, Māra is inspired by Hindu myths about asuras, a class of titans or lesser deities.

claims.statement: He uses a celestial army and a vision of beautiful women; some legends call them his daughters.
claims.statement_id: Ia menggunakan pasukan surgawi dan penampakan perempuan cantik; beberapa legenda menyebut mereka putrinya.
claims.quote: In the story of the Awakening of Prince Siddhartha Māra appears as a powerful deva, trying to seduce him with his celestial army and a vision of beautiful maidens (accharā) who, in various legends, are often said to be Mara's daughters. In other iterations, Māra is inspired by Hindu myths about asuras, a class of titans or lesser deities.

claims.statement: In Buddhist cosmology Mara is associated with death, rebirth, and desire.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kosmologi Buddhis, Mara dikaitkan dengan kematian, kelahiran kembali, dan hasrat.
claims.quote: In Buddhist cosmology, Mara is associated with death, rebirth and desire. Nyanaponika Thera has described Mara as "the personification of the forces antagonistic to enlightenment."

claims.statement: The epithet Papiyan describes a being associated with evil, sorrow, and misfortune.
claims.statement_id: Epitet Papiyan menggambarkan sosok yang berkaitan dengan kejahatan, kesedihan, dan kemalangan.
claims.quote: His name is first mentioned in the Atharva Veda (1200 BCE–1000 BCE) as  Mrtyu and Agha Mara, the evil slayer. He is called the "evil one who kills" and "Papiyan", denoting a being which is not only morally bad but intertwined with sorrow, pain and misfortune.

claims.statement: Mara's name derives from a Sanskrit root associated with causing death or killing.
claims.statement_id: Nama Mara berasal dari akar Sanskerta yang berkaitan dengan menyebabkan kematian atau membunuh.
claims.quote: The word Māra comes from the Sanskrit form of the verbal root mṛ. It takes a present indicative form mṛyate and a causative form mārayati (with strengthening of the root vowel from ṛ to ār). Māra is a verbal noun from the causative root and means 'causing death' or 'killing'. It is related to other words for death from the same root, such as: maraṇa and mṛtyu.

claims.statement: Guruge's study quotes a definition of Mara as personification of Death, the Evil One, and the Tempter.
claims.statement_id: Kajian Guruge mengutip definisi Mara sebagai personifikasi kematian, kejahatan, dan godaan.
claims.quote: Maara as "the personification of Death, the Evil One, the Tempter

claims.statement: In Buddhism, Mara refers to any form of malicious force hindering enlightenment.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Buddhisme, Mara merujuk pada segala bentuk kekuatan jahat yang menghalangi pencerahan.
claims.quote: Mara, in Buddhism, refers to any form of malicious force hindering enlightenment.

claims.statement: In traditional Buddhism, Devaputra-mara is the deva of the sensuous realm who tried to prevent Gautama Buddha from attaining liberation from the cycle of rebirth on the night of his enlightenment.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Buddhisme tradisional, Devaputra-mara adalah dewa alam indriawi yang berusaha mencegah Gautama Buddha mencapai pembebasan dari lingkaran kelahiran kembali pada malam pencerahannya.
claims.quote: Devaputra-māra – the deva of the sensuous realm, who tried to prevent Gautama Buddha from attaining liberation from the cycle of rebirth on the night of the Buddha's enlightenment.

claims.statement: Mara's three daughters are identified as Taṇhā (Thirst), Arati (Aversion, Discontentment), and Rāga (Attachment, Desire, Greed, Passion).
claims.statement_id: Tiga putri Mara disebut Taṇhā (Dahaga), Arati (Keengganan, Ketidakpuasan), dan Rāga (Kemelekatan, Hasrat, Keserakahan, Nafsu).
claims.quote: Mara's three daughters are identified as Taṇhā (Thirst), Arati (Aversion, Discontentment), and Rāga (Attachment, Desire, Greed, Passion).

claims.statement: Guruge writes that this Maara, or Maaradevaputta, is not only a very powerful deity but is also bent on making life difficult for holy persons.
claims.statement_id: Guruge menulis bahwa Maara, atau Maaradevaputta, bukan hanya dewa yang sangat kuat tetapi juga bertekad mempersulit hidup orang-orang suci.
claims.quote: This Maara, or Maaradevaputta, is not only a very powerful deity but is also bent on making life difficult for holy persons.

claims.statement: According to Guruge, a personification of Death is also called the lord of death (Maccuraaja), the exterminator (Antaka), the great king (mahaaraaja), and the inescapable (Namuci).
claims.statement_id: Menurut Guruge, personifikasi Kematian juga disebut penguasa kematian (Maccuraaja), pembinasa (Antaka), raja agung (mahaaraaja), dan yang tak terelakkan (Namuci).
claims.quote: A personification of Death is called also the lord of death (Maccuraaja), the exterminator (Antaka), the great king (mahaaraaja), and the inescapable (Namuci).

claims.statement: According to Guruge, the Buddha recognizes the speaker of the "kind" words, is aware of Maara's hidden agenda, and rebukes him as Pamattabandhu (the Friend of Heedlessness), Paapimaa (the Evil One), and Ka.nha (the Black One).
claims.statement_id: Menurut Guruge, sang Buddha mengenali pembicara kata-kata "ramah" itu, menyadari maksud tersembunyi Maara, lalu menegurnya sebagai Pamattabandhu (Sahabat Kelalaian), Paapimaa (Sang Jahat), dan Ka.nha (Sang Hitam).
claims.quote: The Buddha recognizes the speaker of these "kind" words and is conscious of Maara's hidden agenda. So he rebukes him as Pamattabandhu (the Friend of Heedlessness), Paapimaa (the Evil One), and Ka.nha (the Black One).

claims.statement: Guruge quotes a verse naming the hosts of Maara; the first four squadrons are Sense-Desires, Boredom, Hunger and Thirst, and Craving.
claims.statement_id: Guruge mengutip sebuah bait yang menyebut pasukan Maara; empat pasukan pertama adalah Nafsu Indriawi, Kebosanan, Rasa Lapar dan Haus, serta Keinginan.
claims.quote: The hosts of Maara are also identified: ... Your first squadron is Sense-Desires, Your second is called Boredom, then Hunger and Thirst compose the third, And Craving is the fourth in rank,

claims.statement: Guruge quotes a verse in which Maara says that for seven years he pursued the Buddha at every step but got no chance against the wakeful Buddha.
claims.statement_id: Guruge mengutip bait tempat Maara berkata bahwa selama tujuh tahun ia mengikuti sang Buddha di setiap langkah, tetapi tidak mendapat kesempatan terhadap sang Buddha yang waspada.
claims.quote: Here, Maara says: ... For seven years I pursued the Buddha at every step Yet with the wakeful Buddha I got no chance.

claims.statement: Nandi is Shiva's bull mount and the guardian deity of Kailash.
claims.statement_id: Nandi adalah banteng tunggangan Shiva sekaligus dewa penjaga Kailash.
claims.quote: is the bull vahana (mount) of the Hindu god Shiva. He is also the guardian deity of Kailash, the abode of Shiva.

claims.statement: His other names are Nandikeshvara and Nandideva.
claims.statement_id: Nama lainnya Nandikeshvara dan Nandideva.
claims.quote: Nandi (Sanskrit: नन्दि), also known as Nandikeshvara or Nandideva, is the bull vahana (mount) of the Hindu god Shiva.

claims.statement: Almost all Shiva temples display a seated Nandi image facing the main shrine.
claims.statement_id: Hampir semua kuil Shiva menampilkan patung Nandi duduk menghadap tempat suci utama.
claims.quote: Almost all Shiva temples display stone images of a seated Nandi, generally facing the main shrine.

claims.statement: Nandi in Sanskrit means happy, joy, or satisfaction.
claims.statement_id: Nandi dalam bahasa Sanskerta berarti bahagia, sukacita, atau kepuasan.
claims.quote: The Sanskrit word nandi (Sanskrit: नन्दि) means happy, joy, and satisfaction, which are the properties of Nandi, the divine guardian of Shiva.

claims.statement: The narrative calls him the son of sage Shilada who practised penance to obtain a child.
claims.statement_id: Kisah menyebutnya putra resi Shilada yang menjalankan tapa untuk memperoleh anak.
claims.quote: Nandi is described as the son of the sage Shilada. Shilada underwent severe penance to have a boon– a child with immortality and blessings of Shiva, and received Nandi as his son.

claims.statement: Mackenzie calls Nandi Shiva's bull symbol.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menyebut Nandi sebagai simbol banteng Shiva.
claims.quote:
The bull symbol, Nandi, the moon crescent on his
forehead, and the serpent girdle, indicate that Shiva is a
god of fertility.

claims.statement: In Jainism a tirthankara is a saviour and preacher of dharma guiding beings across samsara.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Jainisme, tirthankara adalah penyelamat dan pengkhotbah dharma yang membimbing makhluk melewati samsara.
claims.quote: is a saviour and supreme preacher of the dharma (righteous path). The term refers to one who establishes a tirtha, a fordable passage across saṃsāra, the sea of interminable birth and death.

claims.statement: In Jain belief he attains kevala jnana, omniscience.
claims.statement_id: Menurut keyakinan Jain, ia mencapai kevala jnana, pengetahuan sempurna.
claims.quote: After understanding the true nature of the self or soul, the Tīrthaṅkara attains kevala jnana (omniscience).

claims.statement: Jain cosmology says 24 tirthankaras appear in each half cycle of time.
claims.statement_id: Kosmologi Jain menyebut 24 tirthankara muncul dalam setiap setengah siklus waktu.
claims.quote: In each half of the cycle, exactly 24 tirthaṅkaras are said to appear in this part of the universe.

claims.statement: Rishabhanatha is the first and Mahavira the last in the current cycle.
claims.statement_id: Rishabhanatha adalah yang pertama dan Mahavira yang terakhir dalam siklus yang sekarang.
claims.quote: The first tirthaṅkara in the present cycle (Hunda Avsarpinī) was Rishabhanatha, who is credited with formulating and organising humans to live in a society harmoniously. The 24th and last tirthaṅkara of the present half-cycle is traditionally identified as Mahavira (599 BCE–527 BCE).

claims.statement: A tirthankara organizes a fourfold sangha of male and female monastics and lay followers.
claims.statement_id: Tirthankara mengorganisasi sangha yang terdiri dari empat kelompok pengikut laki-laki dan perempuan, monastik dan awam.
claims.quote: A tirthaṅkara organises the sangha, a fourfold order of male and female monastics, śrāvakas (male followers) and śrāvikās (female followers).

claims.statement: In Jain belief their grace is available to all living beings regardless of religion.
claims.statement_id: Dalam keyakinan Jain, rahmat mereka tersedia bagi seluruh makhluk tanpa memandang agamanya.
claims.quote: While Jains document and revere tirthaṅkaras, their grace is said to be available to all living beings regardless of religion.

claims.statement: Vairocana is a major Buddha in Mahayana and Vajrayana traditions.
claims.statement_id: Vairocana adalah Buddha penting dalam tradisi Mahayana dan Vajrayana.
claims.quote: is a major Buddha from Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhism.

claims.statement: He is also called Mahavairocana, meaning Great Sun.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga disebut Mahavairocana, yang berarti Matahari Agung.
claims.quote: also known as Mahāvairocana (Great Sun),

claims.statement: This teaching identifies the Buddhas' true body, the Dharmakaya, with Ultimate Reality.
claims.statement_id: Dharmakaya dipahami sebagai tubuh sejati para Buddha dan sebagai realitas tertinggi dalam ajaran ini.
claims.quote: of all Buddhas (the Dharma-body is the "true body" of all Buddhas, equivalent to the Ultimate Reality)

claims.statement: In Vajrayana the cosmic Buddha Mahavairocana's body is understood as the entire universe.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Vajrayana, tubuh Buddha kosmis Mahavairocana dipahami sebagai keseluruhan alam semesta.
claims.quote: Mahāvairocana is considered to be a Cosmic Buddha whose body is the entire universe.

claims.statement: He is the central figure among the Five Buddhas of the Five Directions.
claims.statement_id: Ia merupakan tokoh pusat di antara Lima Buddha dari Lima Arah.
claims.quote: Among the Five Buddhas of the Five Directions, Vairocana is the central figure, symbolizing both the source and destination of all the other four.

claims.statement: HAR explains that Vairocana's Abhisambodhi Tantra does not present the Five Buddha system of Yoga and Anuttarayoga mandala classifications.
claims.statement_id: HAR menjelaskan bahwa Tantra Abhisambodhi Vairocana tidak memakai sistem Lima Buddha seperti klasifikasi mandala Yoga dan Anuttarayoga.
claims.quote: The Vairochana Abhisambodhi Tantra does not present a Five Buddha system as found in the Yoga and Anuttarayoga classifications of complex mandalas.

claims.statement: Ardhanarishvara is a form of Shiva united with Parvati.
claims.statement_id: Ardhanarisvara adalah bentuk Shiva yang menyatu dengan Parvati.
claims.quote: Ardhanarishvara (Sanskrit: अर्धनारीश्वर, romanized: Ardhanārīśvara, lit. 'the half-female Lord') is a form of the Hindu deity Shiva combined with his consort Parvati. Ardhanarishvara is depicted as half-male and half-female, equally split down the middle.

claims.statement: The form is divided equally into half male and half female.
claims.statement_id: Wujudnya dibagi sama rata menjadi setengah laki-laki dan setengah perempuan.
claims.quote: Ardhanarishvara (Sanskrit: अर्धनारीश्वर, romanized: Ardhanārīśvara, lit. 'the half-female Lord') is a form of the Hindu deity Shiva combined with his consort Parvati. Ardhanarishvara is depicted as half-male and half-female, equally split down the middle.

claims.statement: It symbolizes the union of masculine and feminine energies or Purusha and Prakriti.
claims.statement_id: Ia melambangkan penyatuan energi maskulin dan feminin atau Purusha dan Prakriti.
claims.quote: Ardhanarishvara represents the synthesis of masculine and feminine energies of the universe (Purusha and Prakriti) and illustrates how Shakti, the female principle of God, is inseparable from (or the same as, according to some interpretations) Shiva, the male principle of God, and vice versa. The union of these principles is exalted as the root and womb of all creation.

claims.statement: The right half is usually male Shiva.
claims.statement_id: Bagian kanan biasanya Shiva laki-laki.
claims.quote: The right half is usually the male Shiva, illustrating his traditional attributes.

claims.statement: Early depictions date to the Kushan period and develop in the Gupta era.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran awal berasal dari periode Kushan dan berkembang pada era Gupta.
claims.quote: The earliest Ardhanarishvara images are dated to the Kushan period, starting from the first century CE. Its iconography evolved and was perfected in the Gupta era. The Puranas and various iconographic treatises write about the mythology and iconography of Ardhanarishvara.

claims.statement: The name Ardhanarishvara means the Lord who is half woman.
claims.statement_id: Nama Ardhanarisvara berarti Tuhan yang setengah perempuan.
claims.quote: The name Ardhanarishvara means "the Lord Who is half woman".

claims.statement: Cleveland's description of Ardhanarishvara shows the left side female and the right side male.
claims.statement_id: Deskripsi Cleveland tentang Ardhanarisvara memperlihatkan sisi kiri perempuan dan sisi kanan laki-laki.
claims.quote: his form in which the left side is female and the right side is male.

claims.statement: Daksha is a Hindu deity who in the Rigveda is an Aditya associated with priestly skills.
claims.statement_id: Daksha adalah dewa Hindu yang dalam Rigveda merupakan Aditya terkait keterampilan kependetaan.
claims.quote: is a Hindu god whose role underwent a significant transformation from Vedic to Itihasa-Puranic mythology. In the Rigveda, Daksha is an aditya and is associated with priestly skills.

claims.statement: In epics and Puranas he is Brahma's son and one of the Prajapatis, agents of creation.
claims.statement_id: Dalam wiracarita dan Purana ia adalah putra Brahma dan salah satu Prajapati, agen penciptaan.
claims.quote: In the epics and Puranic scriptures, he is a son of the creator-god Brahma and one of the Prajapati, the agents of creation, as well as a divine king-rishi.

claims.statement: His narrative describes a sacrifice deliberately excluding Sati and Shiva.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya menyebut pengorbanan yang sengaja tidak mengundang Sati dan Shiva.
claims.quote: a resentful Daksha conducted a yajna (fire-sacrifice), and deliberately did not invite his youngest daughter Sati and her husband Shiva.

claims.statement: In the Linga Purana version Virabhadra beheads him and he later revives with a goat's head.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Linga Purana, Virabhadra memenggalnya dan ia kemudian hidup kembali berkepala kambing.

claims.statement: His iconography is a stocky man with a human face or goat's head.

claims.statement: In Mackenzie's retelling Shiva himself beheads Daksha and replaces his head with a goat's head.

Daksha is the father of Sati, the peerless wife of
Shiva. It was on account of this rishi's quarrel with

claims.statement: Tara is a female Buddha revered in Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhism.
claims.statement_id: Tara adalah Buddha perempuan yang dipuja dalam Buddhisme Mahayana dan Vajrayana.
claims.quote: is an important female Buddha in Buddhism, especially revered in Vajrayana Buddhism and Mahayana Buddhism.

claims.statement: She is known as a saviouress hearing beings' cries and saving them from worldly and spiritual danger.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikenal sebagai penyelamat yang mendengar jeritan makhluk dan menyelamatkan dari bahaya duniawi dan rohani.
claims.quote: Tārā is also known as a saviouress who hears the cries of beings in saṃsāra and saves them from worldly and spiritual danger.

claims.statement: Green and White Tara are popular meditation deities or yidams in Tibetan Buddhism.
claims.statement_id: Tara Hijau dan Tara Putih merupakan dewa meditasi atau yidam yang populer dalam Buddhisme Tibet.
claims.quote: Both Green and White Tārā remain popular meditation deities or yidams in Tibetan Buddhism, and Tara is also revered in Newar Buddhism.

claims.statement: Green Tara emanates twenty one Taras with different attributes and activities.
claims.statement_id: Tara Hijau memancarkan 21 Tara dengan atribut dan kegiatan berbeda.
claims.quote: Green Tara emanates twenty-one Tārās, each with different attributes—colors, implements, and activities such as pacifying (śānti), increasing (pauṣṭika), enthralling (vaśīkaraṇa), and wrathful (abhicāra).

claims.statement: Tara's name is linked to a Sanskrit root for crossing, in the sense of causing to cross or rescuing.
claims.statement_id: Nama Tara dihubungkan dengan akar Sanskerta untuk menyeberang, dalam makna menyebabkan menyeberang atau menyelamatkan.
claims.quote: Tārā (Devanagari: तारा) is a feminine noun derived from the root √tṝ, "to cross". It is causative, and as such means "to cause to cross", i.e., "to rescue".

claims.statement: HAR states that Tara is practised in all schools of Tibetan Buddhism.
claims.statement_id: HAR menyatakan Tara dipraktikkan dalam semua aliran Buddhisme Tibet.
claims.quote: Practiced in all Schools of Tibetan Buddhism Tara is second in popularity only to Avalokiteshvara.

claims.statement: Bhairava is a deity worshipped in Shaiva and Vajrayana traditions.
claims.statement_id: Bhairava merupakan dewa yang dipuja dalam tradisi Shaiva dan Vajrayana.
claims.quote: is a Shaivite and Vajrayāna deity worshipped by Hindus and Buddhists.

claims.statement: In Shaivism he is a powerful manifestation or avatar of Shiva.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Shaivisme ia merupakan manifestasi atau avatar Shiva yang kuat.
claims.quote: In Shaivism, he is a powerful manifestation, or avatar, of Shiva.

claims.statement: He is called Dandapani for carrying a rod to punish sinners.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut Dandapani karena membawa tongkat untuk menghukum pelaku dosa.
claims.quote: Bhairava is also called Daṇḍapāni ("he who holds the daṇḍa in his hand"), as he holds a rod or danda to punish sinners,

claims.statement: The epithet Shvashva means his vehicle is a dog.
claims.statement_id: Epitet Shvashva berarti ia memiliki kendaraan anjing.
claims.quote: Śvāśva, meaning, "he whose vehicle is a dog". In Vajrayana Buddhism, he is considered a fierce emanation

claims.statement: The Shiva Purana narrative recounts Bhairava beheading Brahma's fifth head to punish his lie.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Shiva Purana menuturkan Bhairava memenggal kepala kelima Brahma untuk menghukum kebohongannya.
claims.quote: Bhairava decapitated the fifth head of Brahma for uttering the falsehood.

claims.statement: In the continuation Brahma's skull leaves his hand when he arrives at Kashi.
claims.statement_id: Dalam lanjutan kisah, tengkorak Brahma terlepas dari tangannya setelah ia tiba di Kashi.
claims.quote: When Bhairava visited Kashi, the city of the liberated, Brahmahatya left him, and the skull of Brahma was released from his hand.

claims.statement: The Guimet Museum explains Bhairava as one of Shiva's fierce manifestations.
claims.statement_id: Museum Guimet menjelaskan Bhairava sebagai salah satu manifestasi ganas Shiva.
claims.quote: Bhairava, "le Terrible", l’une des manifestations farouches du dieu hindou Shiva.

claims.statement: Jagannath is a Hindu deity worshipped with his siblings Balabhadra and Subhadra.
claims.statement_id: Jagannath adalah dewa Hindu yang dipuja bersama saudaranya Balabhadra dan Subhadra.
claims.quote: Jagannath (Sanskrit: जगन्नाथ, Odia: ଜଗନ୍ନାଥ, romanized: Jagannātha, lit. 'Lord of the Universe', Odia pronunciation: [dʒɔɡɔnːat̪ʰɔ]; formerly English: Juggernaut) is a Hindu deity worshipped as part of a triad along with his brother, Balabhadra, and his sister, Subhadra.

claims.statement: Most Vaishnavas regard him as a regional form of Krishna or Vishnu.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian besar Waisnawa memandangnya sebagai bentuk regional Krishna atau Vishnu.
claims.quote: Jagannath, within Odia Hinduism, is the supreme god, Purushottama, and the Para Brahman. To most Vaishnava Hindus, Jagannath is a regional form of Krishna, sometimes as a form of Vishnu. To some Shaiva and Shakta Hindus, he is a symmetry-filled tantric form of Bhairava, a fierce manifestation of Shiva associated with annihilation.

claims.statement: His icon is decorated wood with large round eyes and no conspicuous hands or legs.
claims.statement_id: Ikonnya berupa kayu berhias dengan mata bulat besar dan tanpa tangan atau kaki yang menonjol.
claims.quote: The idol of Jagannath is a carved and decorated wooden stump with large round eyes and a symmetric face, and the idol has a conspicuous absence of hands or legs.

claims.statement: His wooden icon is replaced at regular intervals.
claims.statement_id: Ikon kayunya diganti secara berkala.
claims.quote: Unusually, the icon is made of wood and replaced with a new one at regular intervals.

claims.statement: The name Jagannath combines jagat and natha meaning Lord of the Universe.
claims.statement_id: Nama Jagannath menggabungkan jagat dan natha dalam arti penguasa alam semesta.
claims.quote: Jagannath is a Sanskrit word, compounded of jagat meaning "universe" and nātha meaning "Master" or "Lord". Thus, Jagannath means "lord of the universe".

claims.statement: Mackenzie recounts Jagannath's icon being carried in a great car drawn by worshippers once a year.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menuturkan ikon Jagannath dibawa dalam kereta besar yang ditarik pemuja sekali setahun.
claims.quote:
Once a
year the idol is bathed and afterwards taken forth in a
great car, which is dragged by pious worshippers.

claims.statement: Prithvi is the goddess personifying earth in Hinduism and a mother goddess in Vedic religion.
claims.statement_id: Prithvi adalah dewi personifikasi bumi dalam Hindu dan merupakan dewi ibu dalam agama Weda.
claims.quote: is the Sanskrit name for the Earth, as well as the name of the goddess-personification of it in Hinduism. The goddess Prithvi is an archetypal Mother Goddess, and one of the most important goddesses in the historical Vedic religion.

claims.statement: In the Vedas she is described as fertile, generous, and sustaining all beings.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Weda ia digambarkan subur, murah hati, dan memberi makan semua makhluk.
claims.quote: She is depicted as a stable, fertile, and benevolent presence in the Vedas. She is frequently addressed as a mother, and a nurturing, generous goddess who provides sustenance to all beings living on her vast, firm expanse. While the Rigveda predominantly associates her with Dyaus ('Father Sky'), the Atharvaveda and later texts portray her as an independent deity.

claims.statement: The Rigveda associates her with Dyaus, Father Sky; the Atharvaveda presents her as an independent goddess.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda mengaitkannya dengan Dyaus, Bapa Langit; Atharvaveda menampilkannya sebagai dewi mandiri.
claims.quote: She is depicted as a stable, fertile, and benevolent presence in the Vedas. She is frequently addressed as a mother, and a nurturing, generous goddess who provides sustenance to all beings living on her vast, firm expanse. While the Rigveda predominantly associates her with Dyaus ('Father Sky'), the Atharvaveda and later texts portray her as an independent deity.

claims.statement: In classical Hinduism her figure is supplanted by Bhumi, with Prithvi becoming an epithet of Bhumi.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Hindu klasik sosoknya digantikan Bhumi, dengan Prithvi menjadi salah satu epitet Bhumi.
claims.quote: In classical Hinduism, the figure of Prithvi is supplanted by the goddess Bhumi, while the term Prithvi serves as one of her epithets. She becomes significantly associated with Vishnu, one of the most important gods in later Hinduism, and two of his dashavatars—Varaha and Prithu.

claims.statement: The Prithu narrative recounts the earth goddess changing into a cow.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Prithu menuturkan dewi bumi berubah menjadi sapi.
claims.quote: Another connection is found between Prithvi and the mythological figure Prithu (Sanskrit: पृथु, Pṛthu), who chases the goddess Prthvi, shapeshifted as a cow. His name means 'far, wide, broad' and in later texts, the term Prithvi is treated as patronym for Earth derived from his name.

claims.statement: Rigveda 5.84 invokes Prithvi bearing the tool that rends hills and quickening earth.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda 5.84 menyeru Prithvi yang membawa alat pembelah bukit dan menghidupkan bumi.
claims.quote: THOU, of a truth, O Prthivi, bearest the tool that rends the hills: ... Thou rich in torrents, who with might quickenest earth, O Mighty One.

claims.statement: As in the Rig Veda, Prithvi is associated with the cow called Gauri, revered for giving milk; the cow is a symbol of nourishment and motherhood.
claims.statement_id: Seperti dalam Rig Veda, Prithvi dikaitkan dengan sapi yang disebut Gauri, dihormati karena memberi susu; sapi menjadi lambang pengasuhan dan keibuan.
claims.quote: Like in the Rig Veda, Prithvi is associated with the cow, called Gauri, which is revered for its milk-giving qualities. The cow is seen as a symbol of nourishment and motherhood, making this connection with Prithvi natural.

claims.statement: Rigveda 5.84 praises Prithvi who with her might grasps even the strong sovereigns of the wood when the rain-floods of heaven descend from the lightning of her cloud.
claims.statement_id: Rigveda 5.84 memuji Prithvi yang dengan kuasanya mencengkeram bahkan para penguasa hutan yang kuat ketika banjir hujan langit turun dari kilat awannya.
claims.quote: Who graspest with thy might on earth. e'en the strong sovrans of the wood, When from the lightning of thy cloud the rain-floods of the heaven descend.

claims.statement: Shani is the divine personification of Saturn and a member of the Navagraha in Hinduism.
claims.statement_id: Sani adalah personifikasi ilahi planet Saturnus dan anggota Navagraha dalam Hindu.
claims.quote: is the divine personification of the planet Saturn in Hinduism, and is one of the nine heavenly objects (Navagraha) in Hindu astrology.

claims.statement: Depictions include a dark figure with sword or sceptre and buffalo or crow mount.
claims.statement_id: Penggambarannya mencakup tubuh gelap dengan pedang atau tongkat serta tunggangan kerbau atau gagak.
claims.quote: whose iconography consists of a figure with a dark complexion carrying a sword or danda (sceptre) and sitting on a buffalo or some times on a crow.

claims.statement: He is god of karma, time, and retribution for thoughts, speech, and deeds.
claims.statement_id: Ia merupakan dewa karma, waktu, dan balasan atas pikiran, ucapan, serta tindakan.
claims.quote: He is the god of karma, time and retribution, and delivers results depending upon one's thoughts, speech, and deeds.

claims.statement: In the narrative Shani's wife curses his gaze to cause destruction or hardship.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah, istri Sani mengutuk tatapannya agar menyebabkan kehancuran atau kesulitan.
claims.quote: Shani is married to the daughter of gandharva Chitraratha, who cursed him that anyone he gazed upon would face destruction or hardship.

claims.statement: Different texts depict his mount as crow, vulture, chariot, or other animals.
claims.statement_id: Berbagai teks berbeda menggambarkan tunggangannya sebagai gagak, burung nasar, kereta, atau hewan lain.
claims.quote: Shani is depicted wearing blue or black robes, having a dark complexion and riding a vulture or on an iron chariot drawn by eight horses. He holds in his hands a bow, an arrow, an axe and a trident. He is canonically represented riding on a large crow or vulture which follows him wherever he goes.

claims.statement: Mackenzie recounts a myth in which cursed Saturn decapitates Ganesha through his gaze.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menuturkan versi mitos bahwa Saturnus yang terkutuk memenggal Ganesha dengan tatapannya.
claims.quote:
A myth in one of the
Puranas relates that the planet Saturn, being under a
curse, decapitated Ganesa simply by looking at him.

claims.statement: Airavata is a white divine elephant, king of elephants, and Indra's mount.
claims.statement_id: Airavata adalah gajah ilahi putih yang menjadi raja gajah dan tunggangan Indra.
claims.quote: He is pristine white. ... He is the "king of elephants" and serves as the main vehicle for the deity Indra.

claims.statement: The epithet Abhra matanga means elephant of the clouds.
claims.statement_id: Epitet Abhra-matanga berarti gajah awan.
claims.quote: He is also called 'Abhra-matanga', meaning "elephant of the clouds"

claims.statement: Abhramu is called Airavata's elephant consort.
claims.statement_id: Abhramu disebut sebagai pasangan gajah Airavata.
claims.quote: 'Abhramu' is the elephant wife of Airavata.

claims.statement: The Ramayana gives his birth from Iravati, while the Vishnu Purana gives birth from churning the milk ocean.
claims.statement_id: Ramayana menyebutnya lahir dari Iravati, sementara Vishnu Purana menyebut kelahiran dari pengadukan samudra susu.
claims.quote: The appearance or birth of Airavata varies according to different Hindu texts. In the Ramayana, Airavata was born to Iravati (descendant of the sage, Kashyapa), whereas the Vishnu Purana notes that Airavata was born from the churning of the ocean of milk.

claims.statement: Legend connects Airavata and elephants with water and rain.
claims.statement_id: Legenda menghubungkan Airavata dan gajah dengan air serta hujan.
claims.quote: Prithu made Airavata king of all elephants. The name of his consort, Abhramu, means "the one who knits or binds the clouds," reflecting the idea that elephants can produce rain clouds. The connection of elephants with water and rain is emphasized in the mythology of Indra, who rides the elephant Airavata when he defeats Vritra.

claims.statement: Mackenzie's version calls Airavata Indra's white elephant with four tusks.
claims.statement_id: Versi Mackenzie menyebut Airavata sebagai gajah putih Indra bertaring empat.
claims.quote:
seated
himself upon a great white elephant, “the handsome and
ever victorious”, named Airavata; it “was furnished with
four tusks”

claims.statement: A dakini is a type of goddess in Hinduism and Buddhism.
claims.statement_id: Dakini adalah jenis dewi dalam Hindu dan Buddha.
claims.quote: A dakini is a type of goddess in Hinduism and Buddhism.

claims.statement: Early Hindu texts and East Asian esoteric Buddhism describe dakinis as a race of demonesses eating human flesh.
claims.statement_id: Teks Hindu awal dan Buddhisme esoterik Asia Timur menggambarkan dakini sebagai kelompok perempuan demonis pemakan daging manusia.
claims.quote: in earlier Hindu texts and East Asian esoteric Buddhism, the term denotes a race of demonesses who ate the flesh and vital essence of humans.

claims.statement: In Hindu Tantric literature Dakini names a goddess associated with chakras or bodily elements.
claims.statement_id: Dalam literatur Tantra Hindu, Dakini adalah nama dewi yang terkait cakra atau unsur tubuh.
claims.quote: In Hindu Tantric literature, Ḍākinī is the name of a goddess often associated with one of the six chakras or the seven fundamental elements (dhātu) of the human body.

claims.statement: In Nepalese and Tibetan Buddhism wisdom dakinis are regarded as female embodiments of enlightened energy.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Buddha Nepal dan Tibet, dakini kebijaksanaan dipandang sebagai perwujudan perempuan dari energi tercerahkan.
claims.quote: Meanwhile, in Nepalese and Tibetan Buddhism, dakini (or wisdom dakini) can refer to both what can be best described as fierce-looking female embodiments of enlightened energy,

claims.quote: In Japan, the ḍākinīs – held in the East Asian Buddhist tradition to have been subjugated and converted to Buddhism by the buddha Vairocana under the guise of the god Mahākāla (Daikokuten in Japanese) – were eventually coalesced into a single deity called Dakiniten, who, after becoming syncretized with the native agricultural deity Inari, became linked to the fox (kitsune) iconography as

claims.statement: HAR explains dakini in Nyingma as a female deity or enlightened being.
claims.statement_id: HAR menjelaskan dakini dalam Nyingma sebagai dewi perempuan atau makhluk tercerahkan.
claims.quote: In the Nyingma Tradition of Tibetan Buddhism, a Dakini is a term generally used to describe a female deity or enlightened being.

claims.statement: Rahu is one of the Navagraha and personifies the north lunar node in Hindu tradition.
claims.statement_id: Rahu adalah salah satu Navagraha dan personifikasi titik simpul Bulan utara dalam tradisi Hindu.
claims.quote: is one of the nine major celestial bodies (navagraha) in Hindu texts ... also referred to as the north lunar node,

claims.statement: He is paired with Ketu, the south lunar node.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipasangkan dengan Ketu, titik simpul Bulan selatan.
claims.quote: Rahu is usually paired with Ketu, the south lunar node. The time of day considered to be under the influence of Rahu is called Rāhu kāla and is considered inauspicious.

claims.statement: Rahu kala is a time considered inauspicious in the astrological tradition.
claims.statement_id: Rahu kala merupakan waktu yang dianggap tidak menguntungkan dalam tradisi astrologi.
claims.quote: Rahu is usually paired with Ketu, the south lunar node. The time of day considered to be under the influence of Rahu is called Rāhu kāla and is considered inauspicious.

claims.statement: The Puranic narrative recounts Svarbhanu disguising himself to drink amrita.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Purana menuturkan Svarbhanu menyamar untuk meminum amrita.
claims.quote: one of the asuras, Svarbhanu, sat in the row of devas and drank the amrita.

claims.statement: The head severed by Vishnu is called Rahu, while the body is called Ketu.
claims.statement_id: Kepala yang dipotong Vishnu disebut Rahu, sedangkan tubuhnya disebut Ketu.
claims.quote: Vishnu, as Mohini, cut off Svarbhanu's head with his discus, the Sudarshana Chakra. ... his head came to be known as Rahu, while his body came to be known as Ketu.

claims.statement: Mackenzie depicts Rahu as a demon causing eclipses by swallowing the sun and moon.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menggambarkan Rahu sebagai demon yang menyebabkan gerhana dengan menelan Matahari dan Bulan.
claims.quote:
One of the terrible Asuras is the demon Rahu, who
causes eclipses by swallowing the sun and the moon, like
the Chinese dragon, the wolf Managarm of Teutonic
mythology, and the Grecian demons who devour Helena,
the sun maiden, sister of the twin Dioscuri. In the
Vedic period Rahu was represented by the demon Svarbhanu.

claims.statement: Surya and Chandra noticed him and told Mohini, but by then Svarbhanu had already become immortal.
claims.statement_id: Surya dan Chandra memergokinya dan memberi tahu Mohini, tetapi saat itu Svarbhanu sudah telanjur abadi.
claims.quote: Surya and Chandra noticed him and they informed Mohini; however, by that time, Svarbhanu had already become immortal.

claims.statement: Eclipses occur when the Sun and the Moon stand at one of these nodes, which gave rise to the understanding that the snake swallows the Sun and the Moon.
claims.statement_id: Gerhana terjadi ketika Matahari dan Bulan berada di salah satu simpul itu, sehingga muncul pemahaman bahwa sang ular menelan Matahari dan Bulan.
claims.quote: Eclipses occur when the Sun and the Moon are at one of these points, giving rise to the understanding of swallowing of the Sun and the Moon by the snake.

claims.statement: Vishvakarma is a craftsman deity and divine architect of the devas in Hinduism.
claims.statement_id: Vishvakarma adalah dewa perajin dan arsitek ilahi para deva dalam Hindu.
claims.quote: is a craftsman deity and the divine architect of the devas in contemporary Hinduism.

claims.statement: The name was originally an epithet for powerful deities and later became the craftsman god's name.
claims.statement_id: Nama itu semula merupakan epitet dewa kuat, kemudian menjadi nama dewa perajin.
claims.quote: Vishvakarma or Vishvakarman (Sanskrit: विश्वकर्मा, lit. 'all maker', IAST: Viśvakarmā) is a craftsman deity and the divine architect of the devas in contemporary Hinduism. In the early texts, the craftsman deity was known as Tvastar and the word "Vishvakarma" was originally used as an epithet for any powerful deity.

claims.statement: He makes the devas' chariots and weapons including Indra's vajra.
claims.statement_id: Ia membuat kereta para deva dan senjata, termasuk vajra Indra.
claims.quote: Vishvakarma crafted all of the chariots of the devas and weapons including the Vajra of the god Indra. Vishvakarma was related to the sun god Surya through his daughter Sanjna. According to the legend, when Sanjna left her house due to Surya's energy, Vishvakarma reduced the energy and created various other weapons using it.

claims.statement: His daughter Sanjna is married to Surya.
claims.statement_id: Putrinya Sanjna menikah dengan Surya.
claims.quote: Vishvakarma was related to the sun god Surya through his daughter Sanjna.

claims.statement: In the Ramayana Nala is Vishvakarma's son who helps Rama.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Ramayana, Nala adalah putra Vishvakarma yang membantu Rama.
claims.quote: According to the epic Ramayana, the vanara (forest-man or monkey) Nala was the son of Vishvakarma, created to aid the avatar Rama.

claims.statement: Mackenzie recounts Vishwakarman building Varuna's dwelling within the sea.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menuturkan Vishwakarman membangun kediaman Varuna di dalam laut.
claims.quote:
The heaven of Varuna was constructed by Vishwakarman
(Twashtri) within the sea.

claims.statement: Dyaus Pita is the Rigvedic sky deity and consort of Prithvi, the earth goddess.
claims.statement_id: Dyaus Pita adalah dewa langit Rigveda dan pasangan Prithvi, dewi bumi.
claims.quote: Dyaus (Vedic Sanskrit: द्यौस्, IAST: Dyáus) or Dyauspitr (Vedic Sanskrit: द्यौष्पितृ, IAST: Dyáuṣpitṛ́) is the Rigvedic sky deity. His consort is Prithvi, the earth goddess, and together they are the archetypal parents in the Rigveda.

claims.statement: Together they are archetypal parents in the Rigveda.
claims.statement_id: Keduanya merupakan orang tua arketipal dalam Rigveda.
claims.quote: Dyaus (Vedic Sanskrit: द्यौस्, IAST: Dyáus) or Dyauspitr (Vedic Sanskrit: द्यौष्पितृ, IAST: Dyáuṣpitṛ́) is the Rigvedic sky deity. His consort is Prithvi, the earth goddess, and together they are the archetypal parents in the Rigveda.

claims.statement: The word dyaus without the word father refers to the daylight sky.
claims.statement_id: Kata dyaus tanpa kata ayah menunjuk langit siang.
claims.quote: The noun dyaús (when used without the pitṛ́ 'father') refers to the daylight sky, and occurs frequently in the Rigveda, as an entity. The sky in Vedic writing was described as rising in three tiers: avamá, madhyamá, and uttamá or tṛtī́ya.

claims.statement: Vedic scriptures mention Dyaus Pita with Prithvi Mata, Mother Earth.
claims.statement_id: Kitab Weda menyebut Dyaus Pita bersama Prithvi Mata, Ibu Bumi.
claims.quote: Dyáuṣ Pitṛ́ appears in hymns with Prithvi Mata, 'Mother Earth' in the ancient Vedic scriptures of Hinduism.

claims.statement: He is likened to a black stallion studded with pearls representing the night sky.
claims.statement_id: Ia diumpamakan sebagai kuda hitam bertabur mutiara yang menggambarkan langit malam.
claims.quote: Dyauṣ is also stated to be like a black stallion studded with pearls in a simile with the night sky.

claims.statement: Mackenzie connects Dyaus with the image of a ruddy bull whose bellowing is thunder.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menghubungkan Dyaus dengan gambaran banteng merah yang gemuruhnya adalah guntur.

claims.statement: Dyaus's other sons include Agni, Parjanya, the Adityas, the Maruts and the Angirases; the Ashvins are called his offspring. Dyaus is often visualized as a roaring animal, often a bull, who fertilizes the earth.
claims.statement_id: Putra-putra Dyaus yang lain termasuk Agni, Parjanya, para Aditya, para Marut, dan para Angiras; para Ashvin disebut keturunannya. Dyaus sering digambarkan sebagai hewan yang mengaum, biasanya banteng, yang menyuburkan bumi.
claims.quote: Dyauṣ's other sons include Agni, Parjanya, the Ādityas, the Maruts, and the Angirases. The Ashvins are called "divó nápāt", meaning offspring/progeny/grandsons of Dyauṣ. Dyauṣ is often visualized as a roaring animal, often a bull, who fertilizes the earth.

claims.statement: Indra's separation of Dyaus and Prithvi is celebrated in the Rigveda as an important creation myth; in the Mahabharata Bhishma is the human incarnation of Dyaus after the Vasus were cursed to live as humans for stealing from Vasishtha.
claims.statement_id: Pemisahan Dyaus dan Prithvi oleh Indra dirayakan dalam Rigveda sebagai mitos penciptaan penting; dalam Mahabharata, Bhishma adalah penjelmaan manusia Dyaus setelah para Vasu dikutuk hidup sebagai manusia karena mencuri dari Vasishtha.
claims.quote: Indra's separation of Dyauṣ and Prithvi is celebrated in the Rigveda as an important creation myth. In the Mahabharata, Bhishma is the human incarnation of Dyaus after the Vasus got cursed to live a human life on earth for stealing from Vasishtha out of pride.

claims.statement: Gandharvas are a class of celestial beings in Indian religions associated with music and dance.
claims.statement_id: Gandharva adalah golongan makhluk surgawi dalam agama India yang berhubungan dengan musik dan tari.
claims.quote: A gandharva (Sanskrit: गन्धर्व) is a member of a class of celestial beings in Indian religions, such as Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism, whose males are divine performers such as musicians and singers, and the females are divine dancers. In Hinduism, they are regarded to be the celestial demigods who serve as the musicians of the devas.

claims.statement: In Hinduism they are minor deities serving as divine musicians.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Hindu mereka merupakan dewa kecil yang menjadi musisi ilahi.
claims.quote: In Hinduism, the gandharvas (Sanskrit: गन्धर्व, romanized: gandharva) are a class of minor deities who serve as divine musicians in Hindu mythology.

claims.statement: In Vedic sources gandharva can also designate a single celestial being guarding Soma.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sumber Weda, gandharva juga dapat menunjuk satu makhluk surgawi yang menjaga Soma.
claims.quote: gandharva is presented as a celestial being (dwelling near the Sun / in the heavenly waters) which watches over the Soma

claims.statement: Gandharvas are generally called the husbands of apsaras.
claims.statement_id: Gandharva umumnya disebut sebagai suami para apsara.
claims.quote: They are generally the husbands of apsaras. They are described as handsome beings who wear fragrant attire and are passionate about women.

claims.statement: They usually live in Svarga and serve Indra's court.
claims.statement_id: Mereka biasanya hidup di Svarga dan melayani istana Indra.
claims.quote: Gandharvas usually live in Svarga and serve at Indra's court, though they also have their own realm, called the Gandharvaloka.

claims.statement: Mackenzie describes Gandharva music accompanying apsara dances.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie menggambarkan musik Gandharva mengiringi tarian apsara.
claims.quote:
When they play on their divine instruments the fairy-like
Apsaras, who are all females, dance merrily.
